Every ind-object is such a filtered presentation; applying truncation to it proves agreement. Since the entire ordinary module category is left-complete, taking the limit of these identical bounded-below categories gives \[ \mathscr Q_{\mathbf P^1}\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_B. \tag{RSC.24} \] For completeness, a module's Postnikov limit is calculated degreewise by the fibre of \(1-\mathrm{shift}\) on products. Products of vector spaces are exact; its cohomology in a fixed degree is eventually constant along this tower. Solve a constant-tail difference equation successively to see that its degree-one inverse-limit correction is zero. Every compatible tower therefore recovers the module with those cohomologies and action maps. This also proves the full mapping-space comparison, since maps into a limit are compatible families of maps.

The additional objects are essential. For example \[ L=B[v^{-1}]\ne0,\qquad \operatorname{RHom}_B(\mathbf C,L)=0,\qquad L\notin\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}. \tag{RSC.25} \] The resolution (RSC.20) computes that Hom as the shifted cone of multiplication by \(u\). That operator is invertible on \(L\), with inverse \(uv^{-1}\), so the Hom is contractible in every degree. The first inequality follows from the nonzero constant word in the Laurent word algebra. The last assertion also follows from (RSC.23). Thus the unit is compact by its two-cell resolution, but it does not generate the completed target. Its actual compact generator is \[ B\in\mathscr Q_{\mathbf P^1},\qquad H^{-j}(B)=\mathbf C u^j\quad(j\geq0). \tag{RSC.26} \] Hom from that free module is the whole underlying complex. It preserves colimits and detects zero. This generator is unbounded below; replacing the completed target by the finite-lisse ind-category discards it.

The Hopf tensor is also the actual completed tensor. For two cohomologically bounded-above objects, a fixed tensor-cohomology degree uses only a finite interval of their lower degrees: if their upper bounds are \(a,b\), a contributing degree \(i\) in the first factor satisfies \(i\geq k-b\), and the second satisfies the analogous bound. Finite lower cuts therefore compute each such degree, using the already identified tensor in \(\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}\). Their compatible limits give precisely the Hopf diagonal tensor over the field. All association and symmetry comparisons are those same finite-cut maps; for any fixed collection and degree, choose a common cut and their coherence diagrams agree. For arbitrary objects take the colimit of their intelligent upper truncations and extend in both variables. Module cohomology commutes with these colimits, and every object is recovered. The unbounded field tensor has the same direct-sum Künneth computation used above. This constructs the entire completed symmetric tensor and its higher comparisons, including on the new generator and \(L\).

3.101. Full DG coefficients and the projective-line restricted functor

For any connective commutative DG coefficient algebra \(A\), the actual coefficient category is \[ \mathscr Q_{X,A}=\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X) \simeq\operatorname{Mod}_A\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathscr Q_X,\qquad \mathscr Q_{\mathbf P^1,A}\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{A\otimes_{\mathbf C}B}. \tag{RSC.27} \] The first comparison is the full free-action bar: a module action, its relations and higher homotopies are precisely an internal \(A\)-action; the unit insertion contracts its augmented free resolution. Continuous bilinear functors extend that same bar, giving the tensor-category universal property. In the projective-line model the two commuting scalar and \(B\)-actions are exactly a module over their tensor DG algebra. No negative coefficient group is discarded. The coefficient tensor uses the primitive Hopf action over \(A\); the positive-genus model uses the corresponding diagonal representation action.

Let \(H\) be any connected reductive complex group, with Lie algebra \(\mathfrak h\). Consider a restricted tensor functor from \(\operatorname{Rep}(H)\) to this completed projective-line category, whose underlying fibre is framed. Right t-exactness, including the dual and all tensor powers, forces its fibre values to be the degree-zero projective \(A\)-modules of the ordinary framed fibre functor, by the complete projective criterion (CSD.4). Its extra \(B\)-action is a closed degree-minus-one operator natural in every representation and satisfying the tensor derivation rule, because \(u\) is primitive.

We give the complete tensor-derivation comparison. Extend that operator to the regular coefficient algebra by its filtered finite representations. The tensor rule is exactly its graded Leibniz rule. The commuting regular right coaction is a representation intertwiner and hence is preserved. The resulting derivation is the invariant derivation determined by its value at the identity. If \(\mathfrak m\) is the augmentation ideal, that value is a map \(\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to A\); its negative gives \(\alpha\in\mathfrak h\otimes A\). On a finite representation the operator is \(d\rho(\alpha)\): use its coefficient embedding \(v\mapsto(g\mapsto\rho(g^{-1})v)\) and evaluate at the identity. Conversely this formula has the tensor Leibniz rule, preserves every intertwiner, and reconstructs precisely that regular derivation. The differential commutes exactly when \(\alpha\) is closed.

This comparison is between the whole derivation complexes and their paths. One can check the coherent tensor conditions by the square-zero algebra \(A[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\): \(1+\varepsilon D\) is a tensor automorphism exactly when \(D\) is the corresponding derivation. The full regular Hopf reconstruction of (TBF.3)–(TBF.5) identifies these automorphisms and all their higher maps with the group-valued automorphisms of the framed fibre functor. Its smooth augmentation cotangent space is \(\mathfrak h^\vee\), so the square-zero mapping comparison is precisely the complex just computed. It works with shifted square-zero coefficient modules too; it is not a calculation only on ordinary points.

The algebra \(B\) is free on its one closed associative generator. Once this tensor derivation is specified, all its powers and every bar action are forced. More explicitly, the free graded Lie algebra on an odd generator \(p\) has \(p\) and \(q=[p,p]/2\), with \(q\) even and central: graded Jacobi gives \(3[p,[p,p]]=0\), and an even element brackets with itself to zero. All longer Lie words are therefore zero. Its enveloping algebra has \(p^2=q\) and is exactly \(T(p)=B\), with the primitive coproduct already used. An odd tensor derivation \(D\) has \(D^2\) again a tensor derivation, because its two cross terms cancel; \([D,D^2]=0\) by associativity. A map from the free DG Lie generator to the full tensor-derivation complex thus imposes no extra independent relation. This is a free-generator mapping universal property in every DG degree, including its bar paths. The full framed mapping space is \[ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathbf C}} (\mathfrak h^\vee[1],A) =\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{CAlg}_{\mathbf C}} (\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h^\vee[1]),A). \tag{RSC.28} \] Its vertices are the closed \(\alpha\)'s, but the equality includes all the nullhomotopies and higher coefficient maps of the free-generator bar. Changing the frame conjugates by \(H\). The resulting full restricted spectral functor on the projective line is therefore \[ \mathcal Z^{\mathrm{restr}}_H(\mathbf P^1) \simeq [\,\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Sym} (\mathfrak h^\vee[1])/H\,]. \tag{RSC.29} \] This agrees with the actual full connection fibre and frame construction of (DCA.18)–(DCA.24) on this curve: the trivial underlying bundle has connection coefficient \(R\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P\otimes\Omega^1)=\operatorname{ad}P[-1]\), so its affine nullhomotopy algebra is exactly the displayed free algebra. Faithfully flat frame descent includes every unframed fibre functor and every nonflat base change. It does not identify the full and restricted targets on curves of positive genus.

In particular, \[ \mathcal Z^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\mathbf G_m}(\mathbf P^1) =B\mathbf G_m\times\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C[\xi], \qquad|\xi|=-1,\quad d\xi=0. \tag{RSC.30} \] Here the algebra on \(\xi\) is graded commutative and \(\xi^2=0\). It is different from the associative algebra \(B\) of (RSC.19), in which \(u^2\ne0\). Their different roles are fixed by the two mapping universal properties.

Figure 3.26. The positive-genus cofree acyclicity and three-column effectivity proofs are (RSC.4)–(RSC.14). The actual projective-line unit, resolution and full completion are (RSC.15)–(RSC.26). The associative generator \(u\) is drawn with its nonzero square; the separate commutative coordinate \(\xi\) has square zero. The full coefficient and tensor-derivation comparisons are (RSC.27)–(RSC.30). General-curve restricted spectral geometry and the nilpotent projector remain additional arguments.

3.102. Ordinary rank-one restricted variation is an actual condition

Let \(A\) now be an ordinary complex algebra and let \(L\) be a projective \(A\)-module of rank one with an \(A\)-linear \(\Gamma\)-action. Its endomorphism algebra is canonically \(A\), by local line trivializations and descent. Write \(a_\gamma\in A^\times\) for its monodromy. In positive genus the preceding actual derived-heart model makes the restricted condition precisely original-field local finiteness of this representation. We prove \[ L\text{ is }\mathbf C\text{-locally finite} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_0=\mathbf C[a_\gamma:\gamma\in\Gamma]\subset A \text{ is finite-dimensional}. \tag{RSC.31} \] Choose finitely many \(A\)-generators of \(L\). Under the left condition their finite orbit spans have a finite sum \(V\), invariant under all \(\gamma\), and \(V\) still generates \(L\) over \(A\). The monodromy algebra acts on \(V\). This action is faithful: an element killing \(V\) kills \(L\), and a rank-one projective module is faithful, as checked after its local trivializations. Thus \(A_0\) embeds in the finite-dimensional \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf C}(V)\). Conversely \(A_0\ell\) is a finite invariant span for every \(\ell\in L\). The inverses are already present because \(\gamma^{-1}\) also belongs to the group.

If \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) is nonempty and connected, this finite algebra has no nontrivial idempotent. Here is the finite-algebra decomposition needed. Each maximal-ideal residue field is \(\mathbf C\), by the algebraically closed finite-field-extension argument. The Chinese-remainder quotient for \(r\) distinct maximal ideals has dimension \(r\), so there are only finitely many such ideals. Their intersection \(J\) is the Jacobson radical. Its powers stabilize by finite dimension; Nakayama applied to the stabilized ideal gives \(J^N=0\). Distinct maximal ideals are comaximal, so their \(N\)-th powers are comaximal and their intersection is \(J^N\). Chinese remainder now expresses the algebra as the product of these Artinian local quotients. Without nontrivial idempotents only one factor remains. Its radical is nilpotent. Hence \[ a_\gamma=\chi(\gamma)(1+n_\gamma),\qquad \chi:\Gamma\to\mathbf C^\times,\qquad n_\gamma\in\mathfrak m,\quad \mathfrak m^N=0. \tag{RSC.32} \] For radical nilpotence, the descending power filtration of a finite-dimensional algebra stabilizes; Nakayama applied at its unique maximal ideal makes that stabilized ideal zero. Equivalently finitely many nilpotent generators give an explicit exponent bound. Reduction preserves the monodromy product, so \(\chi\) is a character independent of the point in this connected base.

There is a precise ordinary formal-point description whenever \(\Gamma\) is finitely generated. Put \(S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C[\Gamma_{\mathrm{ab}}]\); its group algebra is finite type, since the finitely many group generators and inverses generate it. A framed ordinary family as above gives its coefficient-algebra map. Equation (RSC.32) says it factors through the quotient by a power of the character maximal ideal. Conversely that quotient is finite-dimensional: its maximal ideal has finitely many generators, and their monomials of total degree below the chosen power span the quotient over its residue field. Its coefficient image therefore satisfies (RSC.31). For a disconnected affine base the finite algebra \(A_0\) supplies the finite idempotent partition and the characters of its factors. This proves the ordinary framed functor equality \[ (\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\mathbf G_m})_{\mathrm{fr}}(A) =\left(\coprod_{\chi\in S(\mathbf C)} \widehat S_\chi\right)(A) \quad\text{on ordinary coefficient algebras}. \tag{RSC.33} \] The completion here means maps factoring through a finite infinitesimal character neighbourhood, with the finite partition just described. This formula does not discard negative DG directions to assert a derived atlas: it is explicitly its ordinary coefficient statement. On all DG coefficients the definition remains (RSC.1) and (RSC.27), and the projective-line calculation (RSC.29) is already the full derived one.

3.103. Translation, missing completed objects and higher coefficient loops

Exercise 3.BX. For the polynomial translation \(Tf(z)=f(z+1)\), find a preimage of \(z^2\) under \(T-1\). Verify that no nonzero translation-invariant linear functional exists on \(\mathbf C[z]\).

Solution 3.BX. Direct subtraction gives \[ (T-1)\left(\frac{z^3}{3}-\frac{z^2}{2}+\frac z6\right)=z^2. \tag{RSC.34} \] For any degree-\(d\) polynomial, subtract a multiple of \((T-1)z^{d+1}\), whose leading term is \((d+1)z^d\), and induct on degree. Constants are \((T-1)z\). Thus \(T-1\) is onto, and an invariant functional annihilates its whole image, so is zero. This is the polynomial part of the full generalized-eigenvalue argument in (RSC.8).

Exercise 3.BY. Check the resolution (RSC.20), its endomorphism and its Hopf diagonal. Why is replacing \(B\) by a graded-commutative odd algebra invalid?

Solution 3.BY. For each \(j\geq0\), \[ d(u^j\tau)=(-1)^j u^{j+1},\qquad e(u^j\tau)=u^j,\quad e(u^j)=0,\quad e^2=0. \tag{RSC.35} \] Every positive word is exactly such a differential, with a unique preimage, and the constant word survives. The displayed endomorphism has degree two and commutes with \(d\) on both summands. Its augmentation Hom has basis in degrees zero and two. The diagonal of \(d\tau\) is \(u\otimes1+1\otimes u\), the differential of the primitive diagonal of \(\tau\). In particular \[ \Delta(u^2) =(u\otimes1+1\otimes u)^2=u^2\otimes1+1\otimes u^2. \tag{RSC.36} \] The cross terms cancel because \(u\) is odd; neither square vanishes in the free associative algebra. In a graded-commutative algebra they would vanish, destroying the word resolution, its even localization and the completed module model.

Exercise 3.BZ. Exhibit a compatible tower in the finite-lisse ind-category of the projective line which is not effective there, and identify its actual completed limit.

Solution 3.BZ. Let \(L=B[u^{-2}]\), and set \(L_n=\tau^{\geq-n}L\). It has basis \(u^j\) for all integers \(j\leq n\), with \(u^{n+1}\) killed; its differential is zero. Each vector is killed by a power of \(u^2\), so each \(L_n\) belongs to (RSC.23). The quotient maps form the compatible Postnikov tower. The full completed limit is the Laurent word module \(L\): every degree eventually stabilizes, and the difference-operator computation of (RSC.24) proves effectivity.

Hom from the compact unit into \(L_n\) has only the kernel of its \(u\)-operator, represented by \(u^n\). Its degree is \(-n\), and the next quotient kills that class. Thus \[ \operatorname{RHom}_B(\mathbf C,L_n) \simeq\mathbf C[n],\qquad \lim_n\operatorname{RHom}_B(\mathbf C,L_n)=0. \tag{RSC.37} \] If the tower were effective in \(\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}\), mapping out of its generator would give zero on its effective limit. That limit would be zero, whose truncations cannot be the nonzero \(L_n\). It is therefore not effective there. This uses the mapping-space and action tower, rather than just the list of ordinary cohomology dimensions.

Exercise 3.CA. In (RSC.29), take the square-zero coefficient algebra \(A=\mathbf C[\delta]/(\delta^2)\), \(|\delta|=-2\), \(d\delta=0\), and a trivial frame. Compute the components and the first higher homotopy group of the framed restricted functor, for any \(H\).

Solution 3.CA. The free algebra mapping space is the mapping space of \(\mathfrak h^\vee[1]\) into \(A\). Hence \[ \pi_i=\mathfrak h\otimes_{\mathbf C}H^{-i-1}(A)\quad(i\geq0). \tag{RSC.38} \] There is one component, the zero derivation, because \(H^{-1}(A)=0\). Its first loop group is \(\mathfrak h\delta\); the higher positive groups vanish. On a generator \(\lambda\in\mathfrak h^\vee[1]\), the loop represented by \(a\in\mathfrak h\) is the actual closed coefficient \(\lambda(a)\delta\,dt\) in \(A\otimes\mathbf C[t,dt]\). Its degree is minus one and it vanishes at both endpoints. The polynomial interval contraction identifies its class with \(\lambda(a)\delta\), so these are all the loops. This is the full coefficient homotopy missing from an ordinary-heart point calculation.

Free further reading is the AGKRRV preprint The stack of local systems with restricted variation and geometric Langlands theory with nilpotent singular support, §1.5 and the projective-line example in “Ind-constructible sheaves on schemes,” under “Categorical \(K(\pi,1)\)'s,” for the definition and the completion phenomenon. The full applicable arguments here are (RSC.1)–(RSC.33), with the complete checked solutions (RSC.34)–(RSC.38). RBC.22–RBC.25 give the general-curve effective framed presentation, and RSE.37–RSE.38 give its full restricted Hecke-lisse image. GFP.55–GFP.56 prove original-complex full-image regularity and nilpotent-support containment. GZR.33 gives equality with all independent nilpotent support over the complex numbers. The other geometric ground fields and the tempered and full supported microlocal comparisons retain their separate requirements.

3.104. The general-curve restricted tensor functor

Keep the smooth projective complex curve \(X\), its chosen point \(x\), and the complete symmetric monoidal coefficient category \(\mathscr Q_X\) of (RSC.1)–(RSC.30). Let \(H\) be any connected reductive complex group. For a connective commutative DG algebra \(A\), define the entire space \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) =\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm L,\otimes,\mathrm{rt}} \bigl(\operatorname{Rep}(H),\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X)\bigr)^\simeq . \tag{RSP.1} \] The functors are \(\mathbf C\)-linear. The superscript retains the space of functors and invertible coherent transformations, with every higher path. “rt” means right t-exact. The target has the internal \(A\)-actions and their full free-action bars from (RSC.27). Scalar change is the actual derived extension of those actions. This defines a functor on all connective coefficient algebras; composition and its higher comparisons are the multiplication and unit maps of the same scalar bars.

There is an actual fibre functor \[ \varepsilon_x:\mathscr Q_X\longrightarrow\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf C}, \qquad \varepsilon_{x,A}:\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_A. \tag{RSP.2} \] For positive genus, (RSC.14) describes it by the exact underlying-vector-space functor on the ind-connection heart and its unbounded derived extension. It is conservative, because its cohomology is the underlying vector space of each cohomology representation. For genus zero it is the underlying complex of a module over the actual Hopf algebra \(B\), by (RSC.22)–(RSC.27). It is again conservative and t-exact. The diagonal representation action, or the primitive Hopf action, proves that both are symmetric monoidal. The free-action bar proves these assertions after any DG scalar extension as well. Thus the t-structure and zero objects in the internal coefficient category are detected by \(\varepsilon_{x,A}\).

The finite-dimensional representations generate \(\operatorname{Rep}(H)\) under shifts and colimits. The coaction argument and exact Reynolds projection (HN.18) express its heart as filtered unions of finite representations and split every finite representation into simples. Its entire derived category is consequently generated by these degree-zero objects, with all their morphisms retained. A continuous tensor functor is specified by its restriction to that small tensor DG category and its full free-module bar. Right t-exactness is equivalent to requiring all its finite degree-zero representation values to be connective. The tensor, representation-map and unit diagrams must still be supplied; this is not a prescription only on their isomorphism classes.

3.105. Finite coefficient windows and convergence on DG algebras

We prove convergence of (RSP.1) without replacing an unbounded coefficient algebra by its ordinary ring. Write \(A_n=\tau^{\geq-n}A\). The category \(\mathscr Q_X\) is left-complete, by the full positive-genus argument (RSC.14) and the projective-line module argument (RSC.24). Limits of internal \(A\)-modules are computed in \(\mathscr Q_X\): all action maps on that limit are induced by the projections, and the limit of their relation diagrams supplies every coherence. The forgetful functor to \(\mathscr Q_X\) is conservative and t-exact. In particular the internal module category is left-complete.

The following finite-window calculation fixes the transition functors. For \(r\geq0\), a module whose underlying cohomology lies in \([-r,0]\) has its entire action determined by \(A_r\): \[ \operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X)^{[-r,0]} \simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{A_r}(\mathscr Q_X)^{[-r,0]}. \tag{RSP.3} \] This is an equivalence of window categories, not of the whole module categories. The transition from an \(A\)-module to this window means intelligent truncation after scalar extension. To prove it, let \(J\) be the fibre of \(A\to A_r\); it is in degrees at most \(-r-1\). For a connective \(M\), the tensor \(J\otimes_A M\) lies in those same degrees. Compute it by the relative free scalar bar: all coefficient and module factors are connective, and realization only lowers their cohomological upper bounds. Its augmentation triangle proves that \(M\to A_r\otimes_A M\) is an equivalence after truncation to this window.

For the action itself, use a nonpositive coefficient model. A coefficient of degree below \(-r\), multiplied with a connective module input, has output below \(-r\). Any map from those discarded degrees to a target in \([-r,0]\) has contractible mapping space by t-structure orthogonality; the same holds after every nonnegative path shift. The full free-action diagram consists of maps out of tensors of coefficient factors with that module input. A term containing a discarded factor has this same upper bound. It therefore supplies no action or higher-relation choices in the window. The remaining diagrams are exactly the \(A_r\)-action diagrams, and their mapping spaces are the same limits. This proves (RSP.3), including all higher maps. It also shows directly that the two inverse window functors are restriction and intelligent truncation of extension.

Now take a compatible family of connective \(A_n\)-modules \(M_n\), where compatibility means \(A_n\otimes_{A_{n+1}}M_{n+1}\simeq M_n\), with its higher data. Restrict its actions to \(A\). The preceding triangle shows that its window \([-r,0]\) is constant as soon as \(n\geq r\). Those stabilized windows form an actual compatible Postnikov tower. Left completeness reconstructs its module \(M\), and the compatible maps to the \(M_n\)'s identify it with their limit: maps from any test object are precisely the limits of the same compatible window maps.

We check the scalar recovery rather than assume tensor commutes this limit. Fix \(n\), and then choose \(r\geq n\). The lower discarded part of \(M\) cannot affect the window \([-r,0]\) of \(A_n\otimes_A M\), because relative tensor with the connective \(A_n\) preserves that upper bound. Replacing \(A\) by \(A_r\) in this window also changes only terms below \(-r\), by the same scalar-bar calculation. Thus this window is the window of \(A_n\otimes_{A_r}M_r=M_n\). Since \(r\) can be arbitrarily large, left completeness proves the actual scalar recovery equivalence. Conversely this construction recovers a connective \(M\) from its scalar changes. Maps are recovered by the same limits of window mapping spaces. We have proved \[ \operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X)^{\leq0} \simeq \lim_n\operatorname{Mod}_{A_n}(\mathscr Q_X)^{\leq0}. \tag{RSP.4} \]

The tensor comparisons also converge. A tensor of connective inputs is connective, and a discarded lower-degree input cannot affect a fixed window of that tensor. Define the tensor in a window by truncating the actual relative tensor; association and symmetry descend because the discarded terms remain below the window. Every fixed finite tensor diagram is therefore recovered from these compatible windows. Its full coherent diagram is a limit of such operation and relation diagrams, so it is recovered as well. Applying this calculation to all finite representation values and all their tensor and morphism diagrams gives \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) \xrightarrow{\sim} \lim_n \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A_n). \tag{RSP.5} \] The map is the actual scalar-change map. No exchange of an infinite colimit of representation windows with a Postnikov limit is used: each finite representation and each operation is handled first, and then limits of these functor diagrams commute with limits. In particular all negative coefficient degrees and every higher functor transformation survive.

3.106. Faithfully flat descent of the complete target

Call \(A\to A'\) derived faithfully flat when \(H^0(A')\) is faithfully flat over \(H^0(A)\) and \[ H^j(A')=H^j(A)\otimes_{H^0(A)}H^0(A') \quad(j\leq0). \tag{RSP.6} \] The whole unbounded scalar-module descent proof in (TBF.3)–(TBF.6) applies to this condition. We recall the steps relevant here. Flat scalar extension computes cohomology by the degree-zero flat extension and is conservative. Its augmented Amitsur complex on an ordinary module becomes split after this faithfully flat extension, by inserting the first unit. Its exactness descends. A bounded-below complex has only finitely many cosimplicial degrees contributing to any fixed total degree, so the same argument gives its full derived descent and all derived Hom comparisons. For an arbitrary complex take the inverse limit of its intelligent lower truncations. Flat extension commutes these particular Postnikov limits: both sides have the same eventually constant cohomology in each fixed degree. The difference-operator computation for ordinary modules proves effectivity, and limits of the two tower directions commute. This proves unbounded scalar descent without asserting that tensor commutes an arbitrary infinite product totalization.

To transport it to \(\mathscr Q_X\), use its actual compact-module model. In positive genus the small DG category \(\mathscr L_X\) compactly generates by (RSC.14). In genus zero the free module \(B\) compactly generates by (RSC.26). For a small full DG category \(\mathcal D\) of compact generators and their finite cones and retracts, the representable free bar gives \[ \mathscr Q_X\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal D},\qquad \operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X) \simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{A\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal D}. \tag{RSP.7} \] The first statement is the full Hom/coend comparison already proved in (GSL.9); its detection argument uses the just-listed actual generators. The second identifies the commuting \(A\)-action and \(\mathcal D\)-action, and its entire free bar. Test descent on each object of \(\mathcal D\). It is exactly the unbounded \(A\)-module descent just proved. Each \(\mathcal D\)-action map then descends by the full Hom comparison; the equations and higher paths descend by their limits of mapping spaces. Thus, with \(A'^p\) denoting the \((p+1)\)-fold derived tensor over \(A\), \[ \operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr Q_X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0} \operatorname{Mod}_{A'^p}(\mathscr Q_X). \tag{RSP.8} \] This descent calculation is objectwise on a full DG generator model. It does not assume that the underlying-vector-space functor on the ind-connection heart preserves arbitrary products.

These comparisons preserve the tensor, unit and braiding, since they are the original scalar-change functors and the fully faithful mapping comparisons preserve their defining diagrams. The connective condition is local: the fibre functor (RSP.2) detects it, and the ordinary faithfully flat coefficient extension detects every cohomology degree of that fibre. Finally, functors with specified tensor structure are limits of their object, map, tensor-operation and relation diagrams. Taking these limits in (RSP.8), and imposing the local connective condition on finite representation values, proves actual faithfully flat descent for (RSP.1).

3.107. The genuine framed quotient, without a representability shortcut

Compose \(z\in\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A)\) with (RSP.2). Its finite representation values are dualizable connective \(A\)-modules, with duals and all tensor powers connective. The full projective criterion (CSD.4) makes each a finite projective derived \(A\)-module. Its rank is the original representation dimension: symmetric tensor functors preserve the coevaluation–symmetry–evaluation trace, which is that dimension over \(\mathbf C\). At any residue field the trace of the identity of a projective module is its ordinary rank. Characteristic zero makes equality of these integer scalars equality of their ranks.

Apply the regular Hopf reconstruction (TBF.2)–(TBF.5), now on \(\operatorname{Spec}A\). It constructs the actual affine derived \(H\)-torsor \(\mathcal P_{z,x}\) from the regular representation algebra. Its scalar algebra is faithfully flat with every negative cohomology group retained; its two-fold tensor identity is the right torsor identity; its associated representation bundles are precisely these fibre values.

Let \(\mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)\) be the fibre of the point evaluation over the neutral fibre functor, with the frame isomorphism included. For every actual derived affine \(z\), Hopf reconstruction and its complete naturality give the Cartesian comparison \[ \mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X) \times_{\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)}\operatorname{Spec}A \simeq\operatorname{Isom}_A^H (H_A,\mathcal P_{z,x}). \tag{RSP.9} \] The right side is the actual frame torsor. The equivariant matrix comparisons in (TBF.5) prove the equality on all representation maps, tensor maps and higher transformations; it is not a statement just about ordinary isomorphism classes. It is representable affine, smooth, faithfully flat and of finite presentation over \(A\). Indeed after the same faithfully flat trivialization it is \(H_A\); the full torsor-descent proof used in (TBF.4) descends precisely those properties. The group acts by changing the frame.

The two-fold fibre product of this cover is therefore \(\mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)\times H\), with the action-nerve maps. The entire higher fibre products are its corresponding iterated products, by the same torsor identity and its associativity. Apply the faithfully flat descent of §3.106 to the functor and its frame. The augmentation of this full action nerve gives \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X) \simeq [\,\mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)/H\,]_{\mathrm{fpqc}}. \tag{RSP.10} \] It identifies every object, arrow and higher path, and commutes with arbitrary scalar changes because all its bars and Cartesian frames do. This proves a genuine general-curve framed quotient of prestacks. It does not prove that the framed prestack is an affine scheme, an ind-affine ind-scheme, or a finite connection atlas. The finite full de Rham atlas of (DCA.23) is not a substitute for those missing restricted representability arguments.

3.108. Exactly what bounded coefficients permit

Let \(A\) have cohomology in \([-N,0]\), for some finite \(N\). Any point in (RSP.1) takes a finite representation to an object whose fibre is projective over \(A\), by the preceding criterion. Its fibre therefore has cohomology in that same interval, and t-exact conservativity of (RSP.2) gives that bound in \(\mathscr Q_X\).

For positive genus the completed and ind targets are already equal by (RSC.14). For genus zero their full inclusion identifies all bounded-below objects, by the torsion proof (RSC.23)–(RSC.24). Hence every finite representation value lies in \(\mathscr I_X\). Its entire internal \(A\)-action lifts through that fully faithful continuous inclusion: all action maps, relations and higher homotopies lift uniquely, using their original mapping spaces. The tensor and representation maps lift in the same way. Extending from finite representations by the full continuous bar gives \[ \operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm L,\otimes,\mathrm{rt}} (\operatorname{Rep}(H),\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr I_X))^\simeq \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) \quad(H^j(A)=0\text{ for }j<-N). \tag{RSP.11} \] For bounded coefficients the comparison is (RSP.11), including all functor transformations. The bounded derived-affine presentation and universal-coefficient descent in §§3.194–3.201 prove the normalized tensor-functor comparison for all connective DG coefficients. The entire completed category still has additional objects, as in Solutions 3.BZ and 3.DL; the ind-category need not be left-complete.

3.109. Original-field local finiteness in a faithful representation

For an ordinary coefficient algebra \(A\) and positive genus, the heart of the actual internal category is the category of \(A\)-module objects in the ind-connection heart. An internal module in the heart is exactly a locally finite complex \(\Gamma\)-representation with commuting \(A\)-action: in the cohomological model all degree-zero action maps and their associativity are the ordinary heart maps, whose positive path spaces vanish. This identifies the actual ordinary meaning of the restricted point condition.

Let \(P\) be a finite projective \(A\)-module, with a commuting \(A\)-linear \(\Gamma\)-action. If it is locally finite over \(\mathbf C\), choose finitely many \(A\)-generators and take the sum \(V\) of their finite \(\Gamma\)-orbit spans. The image algebra \(\mathcal A_\Gamma\) of \(\mathbf C[\Gamma]\) in \(\operatorname{End}_A(P)\) preserves \(V\). Restriction to \(V\) is injective: an \(A\)-linear operator killing those generators kills all of \(P\). Conversely if \(\mathcal A_\Gamma\) is finite-dimensional, \(\mathcal A_\Gamma p\) is a finite invariant span for every \(p\). We have therefore proved the exact ordinary criterion \[ P\text{ is locally finite over }\mathbf C \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \dim_{\mathbf C}\operatorname{im} \bigl(\mathbf C[\Gamma]\to\operatorname{End}_A(P)\bigr)<\infty. \tag{RSP.12} \] It does not require \(P\) to be a line or the image algebra to be commutative.

For an \(H\)-torsor, it suffices to check this condition on one faithful representation and its dual. A faithful closed representation presents every finite \(H\)-representation as a subquotient of finite sums of tensor products of that representation and its dual: its matrix entries and inverse determinant generate the regular coefficient algebra, and a finite comodule embeds in finite copies of its finite coefficient span. This is the same concrete coefficient argument used in (GSL.10). Local finiteness is closed under finite tensors, sums, subobjects and quotients. It is also preserved by dualizing a finite projective \(A\)-module with locally finite action: the finite-dimensional image algebra is generated by finitely many invertible monodromy operators; their inverses lie in it, and their transposes act through its finite-dimensional opposite algebra. The transpose action on \(P^\vee\) consequently has finite-dimensional image. The coefficient subquotient argument therefore gives the criterion for every finite representation. This tests original-field local finiteness, not only finite rank over \(A\).

3.110. A coefficient extension which fails the restricted test

Take \(A=\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}]\), \(\Gamma=\mathbf Z\), and \(P=A\), with its generator acting by multiplication by \(t\). This is a free rank-one \(A\)-representation, but \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathbf C[\mathbf Z]\to\operatorname{End}_A(A)\bigr) =\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}] \tag{RSP.13} \] is infinite-dimensional over \(\mathbf C\). The orbit of \(1\) consists of the linearly independent Laurent monomials. Every closed complex specialization \(t=c\ne0\) is a finite-dimensional complex representation, so ordinary closed coefficient points do not detect the original-field local-finiteness failure of this family.

The same argument holds over \(K=\overline{\mathbf C(t)}\): the powers of the distinguished transcendental element are still linearly independent over \(\mathbf C\). The resulting rank-one \(K\)-representation is finite over \(K\) and fails the restricted coefficient condition relative to \(\mathbf C\). This is the coefficient-level distinction also visible in the explicit operator submodule calculation (KF.14). It explains why generic field points of the full de Rham stack cannot be inserted into a restricted projector proof without their original-field condition.

Figure 3.27. The full finite-window and scalar-recovery comparisons are (RSP.3)–(RSP.5); the unbounded coefficient descent is (RSP.6)–(RSP.8). The Cartesian torsor and the full quotient are (RSP.9)–(RSP.10), with bounded-coefficient replacement in (RSP.11). The bottom examples preserve the degree-minus-three tensor class, the original-field monodromy condition and the degree-two frame path of Solutions 3.CB–3.CD. The framed prestack has not here been proved affine or ind-affine.

3.111. Derived windows, a flat cover and a higher frame path

Exercise 3.CB. Put \(A=\mathbf C[z]\), \(|z|=-2\), \(dz=0\), so that \(A_1=\mathbf C\). Compute the actual derived scalar change of the augmentation module \(\mathbf C\). Explain the precise window equivalence of (RSP.3) and why it does not assert full DG equivalence of unrestricted module categories.

Solution 3.CB. The finite semifree resolution is \[ Q=A\oplus A\theta,\qquad|\theta|=-3,\quad d\theta=z, \qquad Q\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C. \tag{RSP.14} \] Multiplication by \(z\) injects the second summand, with the differential sign of its homogeneous coefficient. Its image is the positive-\(z\) ideal, leaving exactly the constant class. Thus \[ \mathbf C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\mathbf C =\mathbf C\oplus\mathbf C\theta,\qquad H^{-3}=\mathbf C\theta,\quad d\theta=0. \tag{RSP.15} \] Truncating this module to \([-1,0]\) gives just \(\mathbf C\), exactly the window comparison. For \(\mathbf C\oplus\mathbf C[1]\), the extra scalar-change classes have degrees \(-3,-4\), still outside that window. On the other hand the same resolution gives \[ \operatorname{RHom}_A(\mathbf C,\mathbf C) =\mathbf C\oplus\mathbf C[-3],\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathbf C,\mathbf C[3])=\mathbf C. \tag{RSP.16} \] The target shift in the second assertion is outside \([-1,0]\). It detects the missing higher morphism of the whole module category, and so does not contradict the equivalence of window infinity-categories. This calculation tests both the derived tensor and the mapping-degree direction.

Exercise 3.CC. For the family (RSP.13), make the faithfully flat coefficient change \[ \mathbf C[s,s^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}], \qquad s\longmapsto t^2 . \tag{RSP.17} \] Can it make the rank-one family, with monodromy \(s\), locally finite over the original field?

Solution 3.CC. The target is free of rank two with basis \(1,t\): every Laurent monomial has a unique even or odd exponent, giving this decomposition over the source. Projection onto the even part is a source-linear retraction of the unit, so flatness is faithful. The changed monodromy acts on \(1\) by the distinct powers \(t^{2j}\), \(j\in\mathbf Z\). Their Laurent linear independence proves that its image algebra is still infinite-dimensional over \(\mathbf C\). Thus this genuinely faithfully flat cover does not repair the restricted-condition failure. Every further closed complex specialization has finite-dimensional monodromy; those pointwise specializations are not a faithfully flat cover of the original family.

Exercise 3.CD. Take the neutral restricted \(GL_2\) fibre functor and \(A=\mathbf C[\delta]/(\delta^2)\), \(|\delta|=-2\), \(d\delta=0\). Compute the whole frame space in (RSP.9), including its positive homotopy groups at the identity.

Solution 3.CD. A frame is an invertible endomorphism of \(A^2\). Its full mapping complex is \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{RHom}_A(A^2,A^2)=\operatorname{Mat}_2(A),\\ \pi_0\operatorname{GL}_2(A)=GL_2(\mathbf C),\\ \pi_i\operatorname{GL}_2(A)_{\mathrm{id}} =\operatorname{Mat}_2H^{-i}(A)\quad(i>0). \end{gathered} \tag{RSP.18} \] Indeed an endomorphism is invertible exactly when its degree-zero cohomology matrix is invertible: multiplying by a lift of that inverse leaves a nullhomotopic difference, so the underlying derived endomorphism is an equivalence. Invertibility selects those components of the full endomorphism mapping space; it changes none of their higher homotopy groups. Hence the first loop group is zero, the second is \(\operatorname{Mat}_2(\mathbf C)\delta\), and all higher groups vanish. For \(C\in\operatorname{Mat}_2(\mathbf C)\), a representative of this second loop, with both parameter directions constant on their boundary, is \[ I_2+C\delta\,du\wedge dv . \tag{RSP.19} \] It is a closed degree-zero matrix in the polynomial two-parameter de Rham path algebra, with inverse \(I_2-C\delta\,du\wedge dv\). Restriction to every boundary edge kills one of the displayed differentials and gives the identity. The two successive relative interval integrations identify its class with \(C\delta\); their one-variable contraction is the one used in Solution 3.CA. These are all its second loops. They are the actual frame homotopies, distinct from the first-loop coefficient-point homotopies in (RSC.38).

The construction and comparisons proved here are (RSP.1)–(RSP.12), with the full coefficient example (RSP.13) and complete solutions (RSP.14)–(RSP.19). RBC.22–RBC.25 give the framed derived ind-affine presentation; the subsequent diagonal and localization constructions lead to RSE.37–RSE.38 and NTR.16. GFP.55–GFP.56 give the full original-complex restricted projector image and its chartwise regularity and nilpotent-support containment. Equality with every independently nilpotent-supported object, the other geometric ground fields and the tempered and supported microlocal comparisons retain their stated requirements. The free AGKRRV preprint, The stack of local systems with restricted variation and geometric Langlands theory with nilpotent singular support, in “The prestack” and “Convergence,” gives the defining convergence and deformation framework; the finite-window, complete-module descent and full frame arguments above supply the claims used here.

3.112. Ordinary framed points and their actual coefficient coalgebra

Retain \(X,x,H,\mathscr Q_X\) and the entire restricted prestack of (RSP.1). The finite coefficient charts below represent its restriction to ordinary coefficient algebras, including nonreduced algebras. A derived thickening includes additional homotopy data.

For positive genus put \(\Gamma=\pi_1(X,x)\), in the complex local-system realization of (RSC.14), and let \(C_X=C_\Gamma\) be the representative-function Hopf algebra of §3.97. For genus zero put \(C_X=\mathbf C\), using the trivial finite-connection heart proved in §3.98. For every ordinary commutative complex algebra \(A\), we claim the natural identification \[ \mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) =\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Hopf}/A} \bigl(A\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal O(H),\,A\otimes_{\mathbf C}C_X\bigr). \tag{SCI.1} \] The left side is the full framed point space; on these tests it is a set.

Indeed its finite representation values have fibre \(A\otimes V\), by the frame. That fibre is concentrated in degree zero. The conservative t-exact functor (RSP.2) therefore puts the values in the heart of the internal category. The heart is precisely \(A\)-module objects in the locally finite connection heart, by §3.109. Equivalently they are \(A\)-linear right \(C_X\)-comodules. Finite representations generate the whole source by the full continuous bar of §3.104, so this retains the original functor. Mapping spaces between heart objects have no positive homotopy groups; a transformation compatible with the fixed frame is the identity after forgetting and hence is itself the identity. Thus there are no residual automorphisms or higher paths on an ordinary test.

Here is the coefficient reconstruction of (SCI.1). For a representation \(V\), a vector \(v\), and a covector \(\ell\), send its matrix coefficient \(c_{\ell,v}\in\mathcal O(H)\) to \[ \phi(c_{\ell,v}) =(\ell\otimes\mathrm{id})\,\delta_{F(V)}(v) \in A\otimes C_X . \tag{SCI.2} \] The frame identifies the vector and covector in this expression with their constant \(A\)-extensions. Naturality gives all coefficient relations; tensor compatibility gives multiplication, and the unit gives the constant coefficient. One can verify that these are all relations without imposing an additional reconstruction theorem: every finite-dimensional subcomodule of the regular representation embeds by its coaction into finitely many copies of its coefficient space. Applying this to a linear relation between finitely many coefficients reduces it to a representation-map relation, which the functor respects. Conversely evaluating a coefficient on that regular representation recovers it. This is the same regular-coefficient argument used in (TBF.2)–(TBF.5).

In a basis, coassociativity of \(\delta\) says exactly that \(\phi\) preserves the coproduct; its counit says that \(\phi\) preserves the Hopf counit. It then preserves the antipode too. In the convolution algebra of \(A\)-linear maps from \(A\otimes\mathcal O(H)\) to \(A\otimes C_X\), both \(S_{C_X}\phi\) and \(\phi S_H\) are inverses of \(\phi\); associativity and the unit make such an inverse unique. Conversely a Hopf map gives every representation its associated \(C_X\)-coaction by its matrix coefficients. This respects tensor products, duals and representation maps, has the fixed underlying frame, and extends by the same full continuous bar. The two constructions are inverse, over every ordinary \(A\). No reducedness, finite generation, or flatness of \(A\) was used.

3.113. Finite stages cut out by explicit polynomial identities

Every finite collection in \(C_X\) lies in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra. For \(C_\Gamma\), write its elements as finite sums of finite-representation matrix coefficients and take the sum of their coefficient spaces. Coproduct of a matrix coefficient is the finite sum of the two coefficient matrices, so this is a subcoalgebra. Enlarging it by its antipode and by \(\mathbf C1\) gives a subcoalgebra \(E\) with \[ 1\in E,\qquad \Delta E\subset E\otimes E,\qquad S(E)=E. \tag{SCI.3} \] Here \(S^2=1\), directly from inversion of the argument of a representative function. Such \(E\)'s form a filtered set under inclusion: the sum of two is again such a subcoalgebra. For genus zero take \(E=\mathbf C\). We do not require \(E\) to be a subalgebra.

Choose the faithful closed representation \(H\hookrightarrow GL_n\) already constructed in Lesson 2. Its matrix coordinates and inverse determinant give a finite presentation \[ \mathcal O(H)=\mathbf C[b_1,\ldots,b_m]/(r_1,\ldots,r_s). \tag{SCI.4} \] Finiteness of the relation ideal uses the following polynomial argument. If \(R\) is Noetherian and \(I\subset R[t]\), the assertion is immediate when \(I=0\). Otherwise the leading coefficients of members of \(I\), together with zero, form an ideal: align degrees by powers of \(t\) to check addition. Choose finitely many polynomial witnesses generating that ideal, and let \(N\) bound their degrees. Members of \(I\) of degree at least \(N\) can have their leading term removed by those witnesses. The members of degree less than \(N\) form a submodule of the finite Noetherian module \(R^N\), hence have finitely many module generators. These generators and the witnesses generate \(I\), by degree reduction. A finite direct sum of Noetherian modules is Noetherian, by the projection exact sequence and induction, so the module assertion follows from the ideal assertion over \(R\). Starting with the field and inducting over variables proves the needed finite generation.

Fix a basis \(e_1,\ldots,e_d\) of \(E\). In \[ P_E=\mathbf C[x_{i\alpha}:1\leq i\leq m,\ 1\leq\alpha\leq d], \qquad q_i=\sum_{\alpha=1}^d x_{i\alpha}\otimes e_\alpha \in P_E\otimes C_X, \tag{SCI.5} \] impose first \(r_j(q_1,\ldots,q_m)=0\). Each is a finite expression in the finite-dimensional span of products of at most \(\deg r_j\) elements of \(E\). Vanishing means vanishing of its finitely many scalar polynomial coefficients in a basis of that span.

Next express \(\Delta_H(b_i)\) by a polynomial \(D_i(b\otimes1,1\otimes b)\) and impose \[ \Delta_{C_X}(q_i)=D_i(q\otimes1,1\otimes q), \qquad \varepsilon_{C_X}(q_i)=\varepsilon_H(b_i). \tag{SCI.6} \] These again give finitely many polynomial coefficient equations. On the left, \(\Delta E\subset E\otimes E\); on the right only the finitely many products in \(D_i\) occur. The relation equations make evaluation on \(\mathcal O(H)\) well-defined. Since the two coproduct composites are algebra maps, checking their equality on the \(b_i\)'s checks it on every element. The counit check is equally sufficient, and the convolution argument supplies the antipode. Define \[ I_E=(\text{all the coefficient equations just specified})\subset P_E, \qquad Y_E=\operatorname{Spec}(P_E/I_E). \tag{SCI.7} \] This is an ordinary affine scheme of finite type. Its \(A\)-points are precisely the Hopf maps in (SCI.1) with \(\phi(b_i)\in A\otimes E\) for every generator. This equality is functorial on all ordinary algebras, including arbitrary nilpotents.

3.114. Closed transitions, the filtered presentation and the ordinary quotient

For \(E\subset E'\), the linear condition that every generator image lie in \(A\otimes E\) cuts out a closed linear subspace of \((E')^m\). On this subspace the equations defining \(Y_{E'}\) are exactly the same coefficient identities that define \(Y_E\): equality in \(A\otimes C_X\) or in \(A\otimes C_X^{\otimes2}\) is independent of an enlarged coefficient basis. Thus \[ Y_E\hookrightarrow Y_{E'} \quad\text{is a closed embedding}. \tag{SCI.8} \] More explicitly, extend a basis of \(E\) to one of \(E'\). Quotient the larger coordinate ring by the extra coordinates. Its relation, coproduct and counit polynomials reduce to the previous ones; a change of basis in their finite coefficient spans does not change their ideal. This gives the asserted quotient map of rings.

Any Hopf map in (SCI.1) has only finitely many coefficient functions among its \(m\) generator images. They lie in some \(E\) of (SCI.3). Conversely every \(Y_E\)-point gives that Hopf map. The transitions are inclusions on these sets, so equality at a larger stage is exactly equality of the original maps. We have therefore constructed, rather than assumed, the ordinary prestack presentation \[ \left.\mathcal Y_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)\right|_{\mathrm{CAlg}^{\heartsuit}} \simeq\underset{E}{\operatorname{colim}}\,Y_E . \tag{SCI.9} \] All transitions are closed and all stages are affine of finite type. The presentation is unchanged by a different finite presentation of \(\mathcal O(H)\): both identify with the same functor (SCI.1), and the images of any finite alternative list of generators lie at some enlarged finite coefficient stage.

The chosen generator space can be made stable under conjugation by \(H\): take all matrix coordinates of the faithful representation together with its inverse determinant. Conjugation acts linearly on the matrix coordinates and fixes the determinant. Consequently it preserves the condition \(\phi(b_i)\in A\otimes E\), over every ordinary \(A\). Thus each \(Y_E\) is \(H\)-stable. The actual frame-torsor descent of (RSP.9)–(RSP.10) gives the ordinary presentation \[ \left.\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)\right|_{\mathrm{CAlg}^{\heartsuit}} \simeq\underset{E}{\operatorname{colim}}\,[Y_E/H]_{\mathrm{fpqc}} . \tag{SCI.10} \] Here is effectivity at a finite stage, which is needed for this assertion. Trivialize an ordinary point's actual affine frame torsor on its own faithfully flat affine coordinate algebra \(A'\). The resulting framed point has finitely many generator coefficients, hence belongs to one \(Y_E(A')\). Its descent transition changes the frame by \(H\), so the \(H\)-stability just proved descends this finite-stage condition. Equality and all torsor isomorphisms are the corresponding descent equalities. Closedness of each quotient transition can be checked after this same faithfully flat trivialization: it is (SCI.8); its defining ideal descends with its original relations. This proves a representable closed transition. It does not supply the derived thickening of these ordinary charts.

3.115. An exact coefficient-stage model for one monodromy generator

Consider the coefficient group \(\Gamma=\mathbf Z\) and \(H=\mathbf G_m\); this is not an identification of \(\Gamma\) with the fundamental group of every curve. A framed ordinary point is a unit \(a\in A^\times\) acting as its rank-one monodromy. By (RSP.12), its restricted condition is \[ \dim_{\mathbf C}\mathbf C[a,a^{-1}]<\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\text{ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over }\mathbf C. \tag{SCI.11} \] The forward implication is linear dependence of the powers. For the reverse, choose the monic polynomial of least degree vanishing on \(a\). Its constant term is nonzero: otherwise cancel one factor \(a\), using its invertibility, to obtain a smaller such polynomial. Its relation expresses both higher powers and \(a^{-1}\) in a finite span of nonnegative powers.

Factor this polynomial over \(\mathbf C\). Its roots are a finite subset \(\Lambda\subset\mathbf C^\times\), with finite multiplicities. Thus the functor is represented by the explicit system \[ T_{\Lambda,d} =\operatorname{Spec} \left(\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}] \Big/\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(t-\lambda)^{d+1}\right), \qquad |\Lambda|<\infty,\quad d\geq0. \tag{SCI.12} \] When \(\Lambda\subset\Lambda'\) and \(d\leq d'\), the new polynomial is divisible by the old one, giving the closed embedding \(T_{\Lambda,d}\hookrightarrow T_{\Lambda',d'}\). Every algebraic unit factors through one stage; all stage points are algebraic units. Hence \[ Y_{\mathbf Z,\mathbf G_m}^{\mathrm{cl}} =\underset{\Lambda,d}{\operatorname{colim}}\,T_{\Lambda,d} =\coprod_{\lambda\in\mathbf C^\times} \underset{d}{\operatorname{colim}}\, \operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbf C[u]/u^{d+1}\bigr), \qquad t=\lambda+u. \tag{SCI.13} \] The last expression includes the condition that an affine test meets only finitely many of the displayed components. To check it on a general, possibly disconnected \(A\), the relatively prime factors of the annihilating polynomial admit polynomial Bezout identities. Their images give orthogonal idempotents summing to \(1\); on each associated factor of \(A\), \(a-\lambda\) is nilpotent with a uniform finite bound. Conversely finitely many such idempotent pieces give the product annihilating polynomial. Thus no connectedness or Noetherian assumption on \(A\) is hidden in (SCI.13). The word “formal” for one component means exactly this filtered system of nilpotent thickenings, not a replacement of its points by just the label \(\lambda\).

3.116. A varying matrix family inside one finite coefficient stage

Exercise 3.CE. For \(\Gamma=\mathbf Z\), \(A=\mathbf C[s]\), and a fixed \(\lambda\in\mathbf C^\times\), set \[ M(s)=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&s\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}. \tag{SCI.14} \] Decide its original-field local-finiteness condition, for the faithful \(GL_2\)-representation and its dual. Exhibit one finite coefficient subcoalgebra containing the entire family, without specializing \(s\).

Solution 3.CE. Put \(N=sE_{12}\); then \(N^2=0\). Multiplication, or induction followed by the same calculation for the inverse, gives for every integer \(k\) \[ M(s)^k=\lambda^k I_2+k\lambda^{k-1}sE_{12}, \qquad M(s)^{-1}=\lambda^{-1}I_2-\lambda^{-2}sE_{12}. \tag{SCI.15} \] Hence the image algebra \(\mathbf C[M,M^{-1}]\) is the two-dimensional span of \(I_2\) and \(sE_{12}\). They are independent over \(\mathbf C\): diagonal entries first kill the coefficient of \(I_2\), then the nonzero polynomial entry kills the other coefficient. Its action is locally finite by (RSP.12); the inverse transpose has the same property on the dual.

Writing \(f_\mu(k)=\mu^k\) and \(h_\mu(k)=k\mu^k\), one common coefficient subcoalgebra is \[ E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf C} \{1,f_\lambda,h_\lambda,f_{\lambda^{-1}},h_{\lambda^{-1}}\}. \tag{SCI.16} \] Repeated listed functions, for example when \(\lambda=\lambda^{-1}\), are simply included once when choosing a basis. The identities \(\Delta f_\mu=f_\mu\otimes f_\mu\) and \(\Delta h_\mu=h_\mu\otimes f_\mu+f_\mu\otimes h_\mu\) prove the subcoalgebra assertion. Inversion gives \(Sf_\mu=f_{\mu^{-1}}\), \(Sh_\mu=-h_{\mu^{-1}}\), and the counit values are \(1,0\), respectively. Matrix coefficients of (SCI.15) lie in \(A\otimes E\); the inverse determinant is the constant coefficient \(\lambda^{-2}\). Thus the full polynomial family factors through \(Y_E\). A varying off-diagonal polynomial entry does not force varying original-field semisimple monodromy; the finite image algebra is the actual test.

Figure 3.28. The ordinary coefficient equations and their closed transitions are (SCI.1)–(SCI.10). The first nilpotent stage is (SCI.17)–(SCI.18), and the varying matrix family is (SCI.14)–(SCI.16). The final panel compares the ordinary projective-line point with the genuine derived loop space (SCI.19)–(SCI.20). All displayed coefficient degrees and bases are those of the three solutions.

3.117. Computing the first ordinary nilpotent coefficient stage

Exercise 3.CF. For \(\Gamma=\mathbf Z\) and \(H=\mathbf G_m\), take \(E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf C}\{1,n\}\), where \(n(k)=k\). Compute the whole ordinary coefficient stage \(Y_E\), retaining nonreduced test algebras.

Solution 3.CF. The function \(n\) is a coefficient of the two-dimensional representation with monodromy \(I_2+E_{12}\). Its coproduct is primitive, its counit is zero, and its antipode is \(-n\), so \(E\) is one of the allowed subcoalgebras. Write \(\mathcal O(\mathbf G_m)=\mathbf C[t,u]/(tu-1)\). The counit equations for its two generator images give \[ \phi(t)=1+bn,\qquad \phi(u)=1+dn. \tag{SCI.17} \] The two group-like equations give \(b^2=0\) and \(d^2=0\): their only missing terms are respectively \(b^2 n\otimes n\) and \(d^2 n\otimes n\). The relation \(tu=1\) gives \(b+d=0\) and \(bd=0\). Here \(1,n,n^2\) are linearly independent functions, as evaluation at \(0,1,2\) verifies, so comparison of these scalar coefficients is valid after tensoring with every \(A\). Thus the exact coordinate ring is \[ \mathcal O(Y_E) =\mathbf C[b,d]/(b^2,d^2,b+d,bd) \simeq\mathbf C[b]/b^2 . \tag{SCI.18} \] Conversely every square-zero \(b\in A\) gives the Hopf map with \(d=-b\); hence no equations or points are missing. Evaluating at the monodromy generator gives \(t=1+b\), and its \(k\)-th power is \(1+kb\) for every integer \(k\), including negative \(k\). This is exactly \(T_{\{1\},1}\) of (SCI.12). Replacing the stage by its reduced point would discard its actual ordinary nilpotent families.

3.118. Why these ordinary charts are not the required derived charts

Exercise 3.CG. For \(X=\mathbf P^1\), \(H=\mathbf G_m\), and \(A=\mathbf C[\delta]/(\delta^2)\), \(|\delta|=-2\), compute the framed restricted point space. Compare it with the ordinary model (SCI.9).

Solution 3.CG. The ordinary finite-connection heart has \(C_X=\mathbf C\). A Hopf map from any group coordinate algebra to the trivial group's coordinate algebra is its counit, so the ordinary framed prestack in (SCI.9) is a point. The actual completed projective-line target, however, gives the full derived framed space (RSC.31)–(RSC.33), \[ \mathcal Y_{\mathbf G_m}^{\mathrm{restr}}(\mathbf P^1)(A) =\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{CAlg}_{\mathbf C}} \bigl(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbf C[1]),A\bigr) =\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathbf C}}(\mathbf C[1],A). \tag{SCI.19} \] Its underlying mapping complex is \(A[-1]\). It has one component and precisely \[ \pi_1=\mathbf C\delta,\qquad \pi_i=0\quad(i>1). \tag{SCI.20} \] For a generator \(v\) of degree \(-1\), the nonzero loop \(v\mapsto\delta\,dt\) in the polynomial interval de Rham algebra has the required degree and vanishes at both endpoints. Integration gives \(\delta\). This detects every loop: in the relative interval complex a degree-zero polynomial vanishes at both endpoints, and a one-form is its differential exactly when its integral is zero, by taking its polynomial primitive. This is the full interval contraction already used in Solution 3.CA.

Consequently the terminal derived affine extending that ordinary point has different values on this \(A\) from the genuine derived framed prestack. The construction (SCI.1)–(SCI.18) supplies finite ordinary coefficient charts and closed transitions, with arbitrary ordinary nilpotents retained; it does not establish the full DG ind-affine presentation. A DG presentation additionally requires infinitesimal lifting and coherent deformation arguments, compact cotangent bounds, effective derived charts and the convergence comparison with (RSP.5). Restricted localization, the Hecke action and their full restricted projector are constructed subsequently; GFP.55–GFP.56 give original-complex full-image regularity and nilpotent-support containment. These are not consequences of the ordinary presentation alone. Equality with all independent nilpotent support and the other geometric ground fields retain their requirements.

For the ordinary coefficient framework, see AGKRRV, The stack of local systems with restricted variation and geometric Langlands theory with nilpotent singular support, “Proof of ind-representability” and “Proof in the case of algebraic groups.” Equations (SCI.1)–(SCI.10) give the coefficient equations, closed transitions and ordinary-base descent; (SCI.11)–(SCI.20) describe the rank-one, matrix and derived examples.

3.119. A uniform odd-operator bound on the projective line

Let \(X\) be a smooth projective connected complex curve, \(x\in X(\mathbf C)\), and \(H\) a connected reductive complex group. Retain the actual categories \(\mathscr I_X\subset\mathscr Q_X\) and restricted prestack of (RSC.1) and (RSP.1). All coefficient algebras below are connective commutative DG \(\mathbf C\)-algebras; no lower cohomological bound is imposed unless stated.

For \(X=\mathbf P^1\), the full framed comparison (RSC.28) identifies a point with a closed degree-minus-one element \[ \alpha=\sum_{j=1}^{h}e_j a_j,\qquad h=\dim\mathfrak h,\qquad a_j\in A^{-1}. \tag{DRD.1} \] Here \(e_1,\ldots,e_h\) is a complex basis of \(\mathfrak h\). Work in a commutative DG model of \(A\); the free-generator mapping comparison in (RSC.28) also supplies all paths in that model. On any finite representation \(V\), the associative generator \(u\) of \(B=T_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C[1])\) acts by \(d\rho(\alpha)\). In characteristic zero, graded commutativity gives \(a_j^2=0\). Every word of length \(h+1\) in the \(a_j\)'s repeats an index. Moving the repeated factors together, with their Koszul signs, kills that word. The matrix factors need not commute, since the scalar factors commute past them. Consequently \[ u^{h+1}|_{A\otimes V}=0,\qquad v^N|_{A\otimes V}=0,\qquad v=u^2,\quad N=\lfloor h/2\rfloor+1 . \tag{DRD.2} \] This is a uniform bound over all finite representations and all DG coefficient degrees. In a polynomial simplex or iterated interval model, each coefficient of \(\alpha\) is still odd of total degree minus one, so precisely the same word calculation holds for every higher path. The bound includes \(h=0\), when the operator is zero.

The torsion characterization (RSC.23) now puts each such value in \(\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}\). This assertion is independent of a chosen frame. For an unframed point, take its actual faithfully flat frame algebra \(A'\) from (RSP.9). For its finite representation value \(M\), localization is the scalar-linear telescope \[ M[v^{-1}]\otimes_A A' \simeq (M\otimes_A A')[v^{-1}]=0 . \tag{DRD.3} \] Scalar extension commutes with that telescope, since it is a colimit. Faithful flatness detects vanishing of every underlying cohomology group by (RSP.6). Thus \(M[v^{-1}]=0\) already over \(A\). Its underlying \(B\)-module lies in \(\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}\).

3.120. The ind-target comparison on every DG base

For positive genus, \(\mathscr I_X=\mathscr Q_X\) by (RSC.14). For genus zero, the preceding argument applies after the chosen-point identification \(X\simeq\mathbf P^1\) in §3.98. Every finite representation value of every restricted point therefore lies in \(\mathscr I_X\), on every connective \(A\).

The full continuous inclusion \(\mathscr I_X\to\mathscr Q_X\) lifts its internal \(A\)-action uniquely: a free \(A\)-action bar consists of colimits and maps between objects of \(\mathscr I_X\). All action maps, relations and higher homotopies retain their original mapping spaces. Tensor comparisons and representation maps lift in the same way. The finite representations generate \(\operatorname{Rep}(H)\) by the full continuous bar of §3.104. Hence \[ \operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm L,\otimes,\mathrm{rt}} \bigl(\operatorname{Rep}(H),\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathscr I_X)\bigr)^\simeq \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) \qquad(A\text{ connective}). \tag{DRD.4} \] Right t-exactness is the same on both sides, since the inclusion has the truncation and fibre compatibility proved in (RSC.23)–(RSC.24). Full faithfulness on the functor spaces follows by taking limits of their unchanged representation and tensor mapping spaces.

Equation (DRD.4) concerns these finite-representation tensor functors. It is compatible with the strict inclusion \(\mathscr I_{\mathbf P^1}\subsetneq\mathscr Q_{\mathbf P^1}\): the free module \(B\) and its periodic localization in (RSC.25)–(RSC.26) are still additional objects of the completed target. They are not made into finite representation values by (DRD.4).

The operator embedding (RSC.3) is fully faithful, continuous and symmetric monoidal on \(\mathscr I_X\). Its tensor assertion follows on finite connections and then by the two-variable colimit extension; its internal \(A\)-module comparison uses the same free-action bar. Apply the actual Hopf reconstruction with connection (TBF.2)–(TBF.7). The resulting natural map \[ i:\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X) \longrightarrow\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X) \tag{DRD.5} \] is fully faithful on every connective coefficient algebra, including all higher transformations. Here the right side is the full derived flat-torsor prestack already constructed in (DCA.21)–(DCA.24). A full flat-torsor point belongs to its image exactly when its finite associated operator values lie in \(\mathscr I_X\).

3.121. Square-zero lifting inside the stable operator image

Let \(B\to A\) be a derived square-zero coefficient extension with fibre \(J\). Thus \(J\), as a \(B\)-module, has its action through \(A\), and \[ J\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow A \tag{DRD.6} \] is the corresponding triangle of scalar modules. The extension need not split. Fix a restricted point \(z\) over \(A\) and a full flat-torsor lift \(\widetilde z\) over \(B\), with its specified reduction to \(i(z)\).

For a finite representation \(V\), let \(E_V\) and \(\widetilde E_V\) be its normalized operator values. Tensor (DRD.6) with \(\widetilde E_V\) over \(B\). Associativity of the actual relative tensor bar gives \[ J\otimes_A E_V\longrightarrow \operatorname{oblv}_B\widetilde E_V \longrightarrow E_V . \tag{DRD.7} \] Here \(\operatorname{oblv}_B\) forgets the coefficient action and retains the underlying complex of complex operator modules. The first term is \(J\otimes_B\widetilde E_V=J\otimes_A(A\otimes_B\widetilde E_V)\).

The value \(E_V\) lies in \(\mathscr I_X\), by (DRD.4). The object \(J\otimes_A E_V\) lies there too: compute it by the relative scalar bar in the full continuous image of \(\mathscr I_X\). That image is stable, so (DRD.7) puts \(\widetilde E_V\) in it. Its internal \(B\)-action, tensor maps and all coherent transformations lift uniquely through the full inclusion. The fibre is a finite projective \(B\)-module by the flat-torsor construction; it is connective, so the lifted tensor functor is right t-exact. Consequently \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(B) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(A) \mathop{\times}_{\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(A)} \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(B). \tag{DRD.8} \] Essential surjectivity is the construction just given. Full faithfulness is (DRD.5), and therefore includes every choice of reduction and every higher path. Finite composites of derived square-zero extensions have the same property by iterating these Cartesian comparisons.

3.122. Ordinary nilpotent reduction and unbounded convergence

Call \(B\to A\) a nilpotent coefficient thickening when \(H^0(B)\to H^0(A)\) is surjective with nilpotent kernel. The negative cohomology groups can be arbitrary.

First let \(D\to D/K\) be an ordinary coefficient quotient with \(K^m=0\). Suppose a full flat-torsor point over \(D\) has restricted reduction over \(D/K\). Each finite associated bundle \(E_D\) is coefficient-flat: locally it is finite projective over \(\mathcal O_X\otimes D\), hence is flat over \(D\). Its connection preserves the filtration by \(K^j\). Its successive operator quotients are \[ K^jE_D/K^{j+1}E_D \simeq (K^j/K^{j+1})\otimes_{D/K}E_{D/K}. \tag{DRD.9} \] Coefficient flatness makes the ordinary and derived tensors in this formula agree; this can be checked on the displayed locally free bundle and is natural for its connection. Every right side belongs to \(\mathscr I_X\) by the scalar bar. The finite filtration therefore puts \(E_D\) in \(\mathscr I_X\). No finite-dimensionality of \(D\), \(K\), or \(K^j/K^{j+1}\) is required.

Next let \(D\) be cohomologically bounded and connective. For a coefficient-flat associated bundle, its local finite projective presentation gives the canonical connection-compatible identity \[ H^r(E_D) \simeq H^r(D)\otimes_{H^0(D)}E_{H^0(D)} . \tag{DRD.10} \] Multiplication of coefficients defines this identity locally, and its naturality for the scalar-linear operator action makes it glue. The tensor is derived-exact on the coefficient-flat connection \(E_{H^0(D)}\). If the latter lies in \(\mathscr I_X\), so does every right side. The finite cohomology filtration of \(E_D\) then puts \(E_D\) in \(\mathscr I_X\).

For the general map \(B\to A\), start with a restricted point over \(A\) and a full lift over \(B\). Its reduction over \(H^0(A)\) is restricted by scalar change. Apply (DRD.9) to \(H^0(B)\to H^0(A)\), and then (DRD.10) to \(B_n=\tau^{\geq-n}B\). Each full \(B_n\)-point is restricted. These lifts and their transition equivalences form an actual compatible tower, since (DRD.5) is fully faithful. Restricted convergence (RSP.5) reconstructs its \(B\)-point. Full flat-torsor convergence is the torsor, associated-module and connection effectivity proved in (DCA.19)–(DCA.23): finite projective coefficient modules, their transition matrices and the proper connection complexes are recovered through the same Postnikov tower. Its full \(B\)-point is therefore the specified original lift. We obtain (DRD.8) for every nilpotent coefficient thickening.

In particular \(i\) is formally étale in the following exact sense: it identifies the full spaces of all nilpotent coefficient lifts over each of its points. This does not assert that every full flat connection over an arbitrary base is restricted. The original-field finite-monodromy condition (RSP.12) is still required on its ordinary reduction.

Taking \(A=H^0(B)\) gives the useful full comparison \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(B) \simeq \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)(H^0B) \mathop{\times}_{\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(H^0B)} \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(B). \tag{DRD.11} \] The maps and fibre products here retain their whole infinity-spaces. The equality specifies the negative coefficient directions over each restricted ordinary point; it does not delete them.

3.123. Finite projective gluing on the actual derived scalar square

Let \(B\to C\leftarrow D\) be connective DG algebras, with \(H^0(B)\to H^0(C)\) surjective and kernel of nilpotence exponent \(m\). Put \(R=B\times_C D\), the homotopy pullback of commutative DG algebras. Its underlying scalar triangle is \[ R\longrightarrow B\oplus D \xrightarrow{\,f-g\,}C. \tag{DRD.12} \] Surjectivity makes \(R\) connective. Write \(B_0=H^0(B)\), and similarly for the others. The long exact sequence gives a surjection \[ R_0\twoheadrightarrow S:=B_0\times_{C_0}D_0 \tag{DRD.13} \] with square-zero kernel. To verify its multiplicative assertion, compute the pullback using the polynomial interval algebra \(C[t,dt]\). A kernel class can be represented with zero \(B,D\) components: subtract boundaries lifting their zero cohomology classes. The remaining closed path has zero endpoints. Relative polynomial integration identifies its degree-zero class with \(c\,dt\), for a closed \(c\in C^{-1}\). The product of two such representatives is zero because \(dt^2=0\). The same interval contraction proves that these account for the entire kernel. In particular \(R_0\to D_0\) is a nilpotent quotient: its kernel has \(m\)-th power in the preceding square-zero kernel, hence has \(2m\)-th power zero.

Let \(\operatorname{Proj}(T)\) denote the full DG category of finite projective \(T\)-modules, namely retracts of finite free modules without shifts. There is an equivalence \[ \operatorname{Proj}(R)\xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Proj}(B) \mathop{\times}_{\operatorname{Proj}(C)} \operatorname{Proj}(D). \tag{DRD.14} \] For full faithfulness, tensor (DRD.12) with the finite projective Hom complex. A finite projective is a retract of a finite free module, so its Hom commutes with all these scalar changes. The resulting fibre triangle of Hom complexes is exactly the mapping complex of the right-hand fibre product. It preserves composition, units and all mapping degrees.

Here is essential surjectivity, including the underlying projective existence. First glue ordinary finite projectives \(P_B,P_D\) with their specified \(C_0\)-isomorphism over the ordinary square defining \(S\). Choose complements \(Q_B,Q_D\) with \(P_B\oplus Q_B=B_0^a\) and \(P_D\oplus Q_D=D_0^b\). The complements \(Q_B\oplus B_0^b\) and \(Q_D\oplus D_0^a\) have an isomorphism over \(C_0\), since each becomes \(Q_B\oplus Q_D\) plus the common \(P\). Adding this complement makes the two modules free of rank \(a+b\). Their transition matrix lifts to an invertible matrix over \(B_0\): lift the matrix and its inverse, and invert the error by the finite geometric series in the nilpotent kernel. Changing this lifted basis makes the enlarged gluing the free module \(S^{a+b}\). The original summands give a compatible pair of idempotent matrices, hence an idempotent over \(S\).

Lift that idempotent across the square-zero kernel of \(R_0\to S\). For a matrix lift \(e\), put \(\delta=e^2-e\). It commutes with \(e\), has square zero, and \[ e'=e+(1-2e)\delta,\qquad (e')^2=e'. \tag{DRD.15} \] Indeed \((2e-1)^2=1+4\delta\), so its error is \(\delta-(1+4\delta)\delta=0\).

An ordinary \(R_0\)-idempotent lifts to an actual finite projective DG module as follows. Choose a closed matrix \(f:R^n\to R^n\) representing it. Form the two sequential mapping telescopes \(P=\operatorname{tel}(f)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{tel}(1-f)\). Filtered colimits commute with module cohomology; the induced endomorphisms on \(H^*(R^n)\) are the complementary idempotents \(e',1-e'\). Thus \(H^*(P)=e'H^*(R^n)\) and \(H^*(Q)=(1-e')H^*(R^n)\). The two initial telescope maps give an equivalence \(R^n\to P\oplus Q\), since on cohomology it is \(v\mapsto(e'v,(1-e')v)\). Hence \(P\) is a retract of \(R^n\), and \(H^0(P)\) is the required ordinary projective. This construction requires no strict idempotent matrix in the DG algebra.

Its restrictions have the required ordinary projectives. Maps between finite projective DG modules are retracts of finite matrix complexes, so their degree-zero maps are precisely the ordinary projective maps over \(H^0\). A map lifting an ordinary isomorphism acts invertibly on all cohomology, by the same retract description, and is an equivalence. Choose these equivalences on \(B,D\). Their \(C\)-comparison has the same degree-zero isomorphism as the specified transition, so a path between the two exists in the full \(C\)-mapping space. This identifies the triple with the required image. Together with the Hom-complex comparison it proves (DRD.14), including its higher paths. The argument restricts to any fixed rank.

The analogous statement for all unbounded modules is not asserted. Solution 3.CI gives an explicit failure even when \(R\) is an ordinary square-zero ring.

3.124. Nilpotent gluing of the full and restricted point functors

The full flat-torsor prestack has the actual atlas \(\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)=[W/GL_b]\) of (DCA.23). Here \(W\) is a quasi-compact derived scheme, not assumed affine. A point consists of a finite projective rank-\(b\) module, its frame torsor and the corresponding equivariant map to \(W\).

Apply (DRD.14) to compatible points over \(B,D\). It glues their finite projective frame modules over \(R\), with every comparison. Trivialize that one module on its faithfully flat affine frame scheme over \(R\); its changes of frame and overlaps are the original \(GL_b\)-action. Scalar change preserves (DRD.12), because derived tensor is exact on underlying scalar modules.

The maps to \(W\) glue on that scalar square. To see this for a scheme, the ordinary spectra of \(R\to D\) and \(B\to C\) are nilpotent thickenings and have the same open sets. Choose principal opens of the coefficient base on which the \(D\)-map lands in an affine open of \(W\); these opens lift across the surjection \(R_0\to D_0\). The \(B\)-map lands in that same affine open, since its restriction to \(C\) does and \(B\to C\) is nilpotent on ordinary spectra. On an affine open of \(W\), the assertion is precisely that maps from its coordinate algebra preserve the homotopy limit \(R=B\times_C D\). Zariski descent then glues these affine comparisons. This also proves the comparison on every overlap and every higher path.

Apply it on the faithfully flat frame cover and its entire Čech nerve. Changes of frame are respected, and the full flat-torsor descent of (TBF.2)–(TBF.7) reconstructs the point and all its arrows. Thus \[ \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(R) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(B) \mathop{\times}_{\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(C)} \mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{dR}}(X)(D). \tag{DRD.16} \] For the restricted functor, first use this equivalence to glue the compatible full points.
