Therefore the entire automorphism fibre is \[ \operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C[t^{\pm1},w], \qquad |w|=-2,\quad dw=0 . \tag{RDI.22} \] On \(A\) its underlying space is \(\mathbb G_m(A)\times\Omega^\infty(A[-2])\). The first factor is the union of the invertible components of \(\Omega^\infty A\), while the second has \(i\)-th homotopy group \(H^{-i-2}(A)\). It follows that \[ \begin{gathered} \pi_0=\mathbf C^\times\times\mathbf C z,\\ \pi_{2r}=\mathbf C z^r\oplus\mathbf C z^{r+1}\quad(r\geq1), \qquad \pi_{2r-1}=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{RDI.23} \] The homotopy groups are based at \(t=1,w=0\); the displayed product for components is an identification of sets. Over ordinary \(\mathbf C\), only the ordinary multiplicative group is visible. Over the unbounded DG coefficient, the additional degree-minus-two coordinate already contributes distinct components. Ordinary matrix intertwiners alone therefore do not describe this diagonal.

3.156. The elliptic automorphism fibre

Exercise 3.CU. At \(u=\lambda,v=\mu,\xi=0\) in the elliptic \(\mathbb G_m\)-chart (RBC.27), compute the full automorphism fibre and its homotopy groups on the same \(A\).

Solution 3.CU. The ordinary coordinates \(u-\lambda,v-\mu\) form a regular sequence in the Laurent polynomial ring. Their Koszul resolution has two odd generators \(a,b\). The independent odd \(\xi\)-coordinate has the even resolution (RDI.21). Tensor the three semifree resolutions and then evaluate at the point. Together with the trivial conjugation factor, this gives \[ D=\mathbf C[t^{\pm1},a,b,w], \qquad |a|=|b|=-1,\quad |w|=-2,\quad d=0 . \tag{RDI.24} \] The generators \(a,b\) are exterior and \(w\) is polynomial. The corresponding underlying mapping space is \[ \mathbb G_m(A)\times \bigl(\Omega^\infty A[-1]\bigr)^2 \times\Omega^\infty A[-2]. \tag{RDI.25} \] This is an assertion about the whole underlying space; it does not specify a Hopf-coordinate splitting of its composition law. Each factor is computed by its displayed free generator. Consequently, at the identity point, \[ \begin{gathered} \pi_0=\mathbf C^\times\times\mathbf C z,\\ \pi_{2r}=\mathbf C z^r\oplus\mathbf C z^{r+1},\qquad \pi_{2r-1}=(\mathbf C z^r)^2\quad(r\geq1). \end{gathered} \tag{RDI.26} \] The two odd families are the additional one-cycle directions of the elliptic curve. The even family from \(w\) is present already on the projective line. Both computations concern actual diagonal fibres, so they include all higher automorphisms, rather than only a first-order tangent complex.

3.157. Nonflat reduction and a missing homotopy

Exercise 3.CV. Let \(A=\mathbf C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\) be ordinary. In the elliptic line chart compare \((u,v,\xi)=(\lambda,\mu,0)\) and \((\lambda+\epsilon,\mu,0)\), where \(\lambda\mu\ne0\). Compute their diagonal fibre, decide whether it has an \(A\)-point, and compare its full reduction with reduction after discarding negative cohomology.

Solution 3.CV. Conjugation is trivial. The two ordinary \(u\)-values differ by the nonzero element \(\epsilon\), so no \(A\)-isomorphism exists. The full affine fibre is nevertheless nonempty as a derived scheme. Resolve the equality of the two Laurent coordinates by their regular Koszul generators, and resolve the odd equality by (RDI.21). Up to changing the sign of \(a\), its algebra is \[ D=A[t^{\pm1},a,b,w], \qquad |a|=|b|=-1,\quad |w|=-2,\qquad da=\epsilon,\quad db=dw=0 . \tag{RDI.27} \] An \(A\)-algebra map to \(A\) would send \(a\) to zero and its differential to \(\epsilon\), which is impossible. After the nonflat map \(A\to\mathbf C\), however, the actual derived base change in (RDI.8) gives \[ D\otimes_A^L\mathbf C =\mathbf C[t^{\pm1},a,b,w],\qquad d=0 . \tag{RDI.28} \] The semifree \(A\)-algebra in (RDI.27) is an admissible derived base-change model, so this is an equality of that model, not an underived replacement for a required resolution.

The discrepancy is already visible in \(K=A[a]\), \(da=\epsilon\). Its underlying two-term free \(A\)-complex gives \[ \begin{gathered} H^0(K)=\mathbf C,\qquad H^{-1}(K)=\mathbf C\,\epsilon a,\qquad H^j(K)=0\ (j\ne0,-1),\\ K\otimes_A^L\mathbf C=\Lambda_{\mathbf C}(a),\qquad |a|=-1. \end{gathered} \tag{RDI.29} \] The old cycle \(\epsilon a\) reduces to zero, while the new class \(a\) is not the reduction of a cycle in \(K\). Thus reduction does not commute with this cohomology calculation.

Even using a derived tensor after first replacing \(K\) by \(H^0(K)\) gives a different answer. Resolve \(\mathbf C\) over \(A\) by one copy of \(A\) in each nonpositive degree, with every differential multiplication by \(\epsilon\). It is exact below degree zero since the kernel and image of multiplication by \(\epsilon\) are both \(\mathbf C\epsilon\). Tensoring with \(\mathbf C\) makes every differential zero, so \[ H^{-n}\bigl(H^0(K)\otimes_A^L\mathbf C\bigr) =\mathbf C\quad(n\geq0), \qquad H^{-n}(K\otimes_A^L\mathbf C)=0\quad(n\geq2). \tag{RDI.30} \] The full diagonal algebra is therefore indispensable for arbitrary derived base change. Neither the ordinary intertwiner scheme nor its derived scalar extension recovers the discarded homotopy.

3.158. Relative semifree models and the actual power thickenings

Let \(B\) be any connective commutative complex DG algebra, let \(f_1,\ldots,f_r\) be closed degree-zero elements, and allow modules unbounded in both cohomological directions. Let \(\widehat Y\subset\operatorname{Spec}B\) be the full subfunctor where the ideal generated by the images of the \(f_i\) in ordinary coefficient cohomology is nilpotent. The completion calculation (RBC.14)–(RBC.19) applies to every finite generating list, not only the coefficient loci in that construction.

We first give a relative semifree model. Put \(P=\mathbf C[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\), with \(t_i\mapsto f_i\). There is a factorization \[ P\longrightarrow Q\xrightarrow{\sim}B \tag{KTC.1} \] in which \(Q\) is a nonpositive commutative DG algebra, free as a graded commutative \(P\)-algebra on successively attached generators, each having differential in the earlier generators. Here is its construction. Start with degree-zero generators mapping to all closed degree-zero elements needed to surject onto \(H^0(B)\). For each cycle in the kernel of this cohomology map attach a degree-minus-one generator whose differential is that cycle, and map the new generator to a chosen primitive in \(B\). Also attach closed degree-minus-one generators mapping onto the next cohomology group. Continue: after surjecting in degree \(-a\), attach degree \(-a-1\) generators killing all kernel classes and attach closed generators to surject in degree \(-a-1\). These attachments do not change the already identified higher cohomology. The map to \(B\) prevents killing a class with nonzero image, and choosing every kernel class kills the entire kernel. Each fixed cohomology group is therefore identified after finitely many steps. Filtered colimits of complexes are exact, so the union is the asserted quasi-isomorphism.

The same attachment construction works over any connective base DG algebra: the coefficients then carry that base differential. The underlying \(P\)-module in (KTC.1) is semifree, hence tensoring it with an acyclic \(P\)-complex is acyclic. To check this last assertion, order the generators by attachment, and order their finite monomials so that replacing a generator by a term of its differential lowers the order. Such a well-founded order is given by finite sums of ordinal weights \(\omega^\alpha\) for the generator indices. The differential lowers this order apart from the coefficient differential. Its resulting exhaustive filtration has successive quotients sums of shifts of \(P\). Tensoring with an acyclic complex makes these quotients acyclic; transfinite induction, using exact filtered unions at limit stages, proves the assertion. Degree-zero polynomial monomials have zero differential and cause no exception. This proves that the model computes derived scalar extension; the same filtration proof applies over the general connective base. In particular a derived tensor product of connective algebras is connective, since its relative semifree model has only nonpositive generators and coefficients.

For \(N\geq1\) write \(P_N=P/(t_1^N,\ldots,t_r^N)\) and use the strict model \[ B_N=Q\otimes_P P_N \simeq B\underset P{\otimes^L}P_N \simeq \bigl(B[\eta_{1,N},\ldots,\eta_{r,N}], \ |\eta_{i,N}|=-1,\ d\eta_{i,N}=f_i^N\bigr). \tag{KTC.2} \] The last equivalence is the Koszul resolution of the polynomial regular sequence \(t_i^N\); its monomial proof is (RBC.14). All the models and transition maps are maps of DG algebras. From \(N'\) to \(N\), where \(N'\geq N\), the Koszul model sends \(\eta_{i,N'}\) to \(f_i^{N'-N}\eta_{i,N}\), whereas the strict model is ordinary quotient in the polynomial variables. These comparisons agree through the polynomial Koszul resolutions and their augmentations. Replacing \(B\) by \(Q\) changes none of the derived module categories or point functors: a semifree module resolution and its augmented bar give inverse scalar-extension/restriction comparisons for a quasi-isomorphism of DG algebras.

When using strict quotients we henceforth replace \(B\) by this equivalent relative model \(Q\). The strict model has a useful finite filtration. Filter \(B_N\) by the total degree in the ideal \((t_1,\ldots,t_r)\). Its associated graded pieces are finite sums of \(B_1\), with multiplicities the monomials of that degree whose exponents are less than \(N\). Indeed \(Q\) is graded-free over \(P\), and on a quotient of consecutive filtration levels its differential is the differential modulo the \(t_i\). Consequently \[ B_N\in\operatorname{thick}_{\operatorname{Mod}_{B_N}}(B_1), \qquad (-)\otimes_{B_N}^L B_1\ \text{is conservative}. \tag{KTC.3} \] The filtration has length at most \(r(N-1)+1\). For conservativity, if \(M\otimes_{B_N}^LB_1=0\), tensor that finite filtration with \(M\). Every quotient is zero, hence so is \(M\). There is no cohomological bound on \(M\).

3.159. The whole inverse limit of module categories

The effective completion presentation and the affine-point definition of quasicoherence give \[ \mathcal Q=\operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y) \simeq \lim_{N}\operatorname{Mod}_{B_N}, \tag{KTC.4} \] with transition functors derived pullback. To justify the limit, a Cartesian module on a prestack assigns a module to each affine point with its scalar comparisons on every simplex. A colimit of point spaces turns the categories of such assignments into limits. Taking their compatibility limit over affine maps commutes with this limit. Applying that observation to the actual full colimit of the power thickenings proves (KTC.4), including morphisms and higher paths.

An object of this limit is a coherent system \(M_N\), with specified equivalences \(M_{N'}\otimes_{B_{N'}}^LB_N\simeq M_N\). Restriction from \(B\) has the full adjunction \[ \begin{gathered} F:\operatorname{Mod}_B\rightleftarrows\mathcal Q:G,\\ F(M)_N=M\otimes_B^LB_N,\qquad G((M_N))=\lim_N M_N . \end{gathered} \tag{KTC.5} \] The arrows of the last inverse system are the underlying \(B\)-module maps induced by the displayed scalar comparisons. The adjunction follows on whole mapping spaces: maps of coherent systems are the compatibility limit of the level mapping spaces; scalar adjunction changes these to \(\operatorname{Map}_B(M,M_N)\), and their limit is \(\operatorname{Map}_B(M,\lim_NM_N)\).

We prove that the counit \(FG\to1_{\mathcal Q}\) is an equivalence. Use the strict relative model of §3.158. Since every \(t_i\) is zero on \(B_1\), the polynomial Koszul model gives \[ D_{N,1}=B_N\otimes_B^LB_1 \simeq B_1[\eta_{1,N},\ldots,\eta_{r,N}], \qquad d\eta_{i,N}=0 . \tag{KTC.6} \] For \(N'>N\), the transition \(D_{N',1}\to D_{N,1}\) kills every displayed generator. More precisely the composite from \(B_{N'}\) factors through \(B_1\): \[ B_{N'}\longrightarrow B_1\longrightarrow D_{N,1}, \qquad \eta_{i,N'}\longmapsto t_i^{\,N'-N}\eta_{i,N}=0 . \tag{KTC.7} \] These formulas are interpreted on the relative Koszul resolutions; their maps from \(Q\) factor through the same strict quotient \(B_1\). Thus the factorization is a factorization of full DG algebra maps, not only on cohomology.

For a coherent module system, take any \(L>N\). Its transition to level \(N\), followed by associative scalar extension and (KTC.7), gives \[ \begin{aligned} M_N\otimes_B^LB_1 &\simeq M_L\otimes_{B_L}^LD_{N,1}\\ &\simeq (M_L\otimes_{B_L}^LB_1)\otimes_{B_1}^LD_{N,1}\\ &\simeq M_1\otimes_{B_1}^LD_{N,1}. \end{aligned} \tag{KTC.8} \] These comparisons describe the entire inverse diagram. For any arrow or higher simplex of indices, choose a common \(L\) larger than its indices. All comparisons then use the same module-system coherence and the identical strict algebra factorizations (KTC.7). Changing \(L\) uses its specified transition equivalence. Faces and degeneracies are the associative scalar-extension comparisons from the full module bar, so their higher identities hold too. Under this diagram comparison, transitions preserve the \(M_1\) summand and kill every summand with a positive exterior degree.

The module \(B_1\) is perfect over \(B\), by its finite Koszul resolution. Its tensor functor therefore commutes with inverse limits: tensoring a dualizable module is also a right adjoint, with left adjoint tensoring its dual. The inverse limit of the extra summands in (KTC.8) is zero. Explicitly, the homotopy inverse limit of a sequence of complexes is the fibre of \(1-\mathrm{shift}\) on their product; for a zero-transition system this is the fibre of the identity. The constant summand has limit \(M_1\). It follows that \[ (G((M_N)))\otimes_B^LB_1 \simeq \lim_N(M_N\otimes_B^LB_1) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }M_1 . \tag{KTC.9} \] The last map is the counit at level one: the augmentation kills the same positive exterior summands. Thus it is the actual counit, not an unspecified isomorphism. At every level \(N\), reduce the counit modulo \(B_1\). Its reduction is (KTC.9) by the module-system comparisons. Conservativity (KTC.3) now proves \[ FG\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal Q}, \qquad G\ \text{fully faithful}. \tag{KTC.10} \] The finite exterior splitting and the perfectness used in this argument do not impose an upper or lower cohomological bound on the system.

3.160. Koszul telescopes and modules with support

Let \(K_N\) denote the underlying finite perfect \(B\)-module of the Koszul algebra in (KTC.2). Dualize its transition maps. In one variable its dual is the two-term complex with multiplication by \(f^N\), in degrees zero and one, after changing the sign of the odd dual basis. The transition is identity in degree zero and multiplication by \(f^{N'-N}\) in degree one. Mapping the latter term at level \(N\) to \(B[f^{-1}]\) by \(b\mapsto b/f^N\) identifies its colimit differential with localization. For several variables, finite tensor products commute with filtered colimits, and the diagonal sequence of exponents is cofinal. Therefore \[ C_f:=\operatorname*{colim}_N K_N^\vee \simeq \bigotimes_{i=1}^r \operatorname{fib}(B\longrightarrow B[f_i^{-1}]). \tag{KTC.11} \] This equivalence includes the natural counit \(C_f\to B\), dual to the algebra units. All localizations here are derived localizations. Their underlying modules are the telescope of multiplication by the indicated degree-zero element: mapping the telescope to a module is the limit imposing its successive inverse multiplication comparisons. This is precisely the universal localization module, and multiplication supplies its localization algebra.

Define two functors on the entire module category: \[ \Gamma_f(M)=C_f\otimes_B^LM, \qquad \Lambda_f(M)=\operatorname{RHom}_B(C_f,M), \qquad \Gamma_f\dashv\Lambda_f . \tag{KTC.12} \] For one variable \(C_i=\operatorname{fib}(B\to B[f_i^{-1}])\) vanishes after inverting \(f_i\). Tensor its defining triangle with \(C_i\); its last term is zero, so \(C_i\otimes_B^LC_i\to C_i\) is an equivalence. The different factors commute by the symmetric tensor constraints. Hence \[ C_f\otimes_B^LC_f\xrightarrow{\sim}C_f, \qquad \Gamma_f^2\simeq\Gamma_f,\qquad \Lambda_f^2\simeq\Lambda_f . \tag{KTC.13} \] The last identity follows by the full tensor–Hom adjunction. The maps are induced by the same counit, so its two idempotence maps and their iterated compatibilities are the associative ones.

Let \(\mathcal T_f\) be the full subcategory of \(M\) for which every \(M[f_i^{-1}]\) vanishes. The finite product of the localization fibre triangles shows that this is exactly the image of \(\Gamma_f\). It is also \[ \mathcal T_f =\operatorname{Loc}_{\operatorname{Mod}_B}(K_1), \qquad K_1\ \text{a compact generator of }\mathcal T_f . \tag{KTC.14} \] Here \(\operatorname{Loc}\) means closure under all colimits, shifts and cones. For a direct proof, the cone of \(f^{a+b}\) is a finite extension of the cones of \(f^a\) and \(f^b\): factor the two multiplication maps and use their three mapping cones. The cone maps have the identity and the intervening multiplication as their entries; their cone triangle follows by cancelling the duplicate middle module. Thus each one-variable power Koszul module is built by finite extensions of the first one. Tensoring these finite constructions in the \(r\) variables proves that every \(K_N^\vee\) belongs to the thick subcategory generated by \(K_1\); dual Koszul modules differ from their original modules by a shift and a basis sign. Formula (KTC.11) puts \(C_f\) in \(\operatorname{Loc}(K_1)\). Every module is built from shifted free modules by its semifree resolution and augmented module bar, so \(C_f\otimes_B^LM\) belongs there too. Conversely \(K_1\) becomes contractible after any indicated localization, with contraction multiplication by \(\eta_i/f_i\). The supported category is localizing, proving equality. Finally, its colimits are ambient colimits and \(K_1\) is finite perfect over \(B\); its Hom therefore preserves them, giving compactness.

3.161. Torsion, derived completion and quasicoherent sheaves

Finite perfect duality in (KTC.11) computes the monad of (KTC.5): \[ GF(M)=\lim_N(K_N\otimes_B^LM) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_B(C_f,M) =\Lambda_f(M). \tag{KTC.15} \] Its unit is the map induced by \(C_f\to B\). In particular the complete subcategory is \[ \mathcal C_f =\{M:M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_f(M)\} =\{M:\operatorname{RHom}_B(B[f_i^{-1}],M)=0 \text{ for every }i\}. \tag{KTC.16} \] For the second equality, in one variable apply Hom into \(M\) to the localization fibre triangle. In several variables the completion functors commute by tensor–Hom adjunction. If all the displayed Homs vanish, each one-variable unit and hence their composite is an equivalence. Conversely if \(M\) is the composite completion, each Hom vanishes because \(B[f_i^{-1}]\otimes_B^LC_f=0\), again by that adjunction.

Each \(f_i\) is nilpotent on the strict \(B_N\), so its localization there is zero. Consequently the natural map \(\Gamma_f(M)\to M\) becomes an equivalence at every level of \(F\): \[ F\Gamma_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F . \tag{KTC.17} \] For \(M,N\in\mathcal T_f\), use (KTC.5), (KTC.15) and the full tensor–Hom adjunction: \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Q}(FM,FN) &\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(M,\Lambda_fN)\\ &\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(\Gamma_fM,N) \simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(M,N). \end{aligned} \tag{KTC.18} \] Thus \(F\) is fully faithful on the supported category. It is essentially surjective there: for \(A\in\mathcal Q\), (KTC.17) and the actual counit (KTC.10) give \(F\Gamma_fGA\simeq FGA\simeq A\). All these maps come from adjunctions and their bars, so the equivalence includes entire mapping complexes and natural transformations. Since \(G\) is fully faithful and its essential image is the fixed subcategory of \(GF=\Lambda_f\), we have the exact equivalences \[ \mathcal T_f \xrightarrow[\ F\ ]{\sim}\operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y) \xrightarrow[\ G\ ]{\sim}\mathcal C_f, \qquad F^{-1}=\Gamma_fG,\quad G^{-1}=F|_{\mathcal C_f}. \tag{KTC.19} \] The torsion–complete equivalence is \(\Lambda_f:\mathcal T_f\to\mathcal C_f\), with inverse \(\Gamma_f|_{\mathcal C_f}\). It also gives the natural identities on all modules \[ \Lambda_f\Gamma_f\simeq\Lambda_f,\qquad \Gamma_f\Lambda_f\simeq\Gamma_f . \tag{KTC.20} \] The first is \(G\) applied to (KTC.17). For the second, apply \(F\) to the natural map \(\Gamma_fM\to\Gamma_f\Lambda_fM\). Its image is an equivalence by (KTC.17), the adjunction unit and (KTC.10). Both objects are in \(\mathcal T_f\), where \(F\) is fully faithful, so the map is an equivalence.

The first equivalence in (KTC.19) is symmetric monoidal. Its tensor is the ambient tensor of supported modules, and its unit is \(C_f\): idempotence gives its unit constraints, and support is closed under tensor. The functor \(F\) preserves tensor pointwise and sends \(C_f\) to the actual quasicoherent unit by (KTC.17). On complete modules the corresponding operations are \[ \mathbf1_{\mathcal C_f}=\Lambda_f(B),\qquad M\widehat\otimes_B N=\Lambda_f(M\otimes_B^LN), \qquad \operatorname*{colim}_{\mathcal C_f}M_\alpha =\Lambda_f\!\left(\operatorname*{colim}_{\operatorname{Mod}_B}M_\alpha\right). \tag{KTC.21} \] These formulas follow by applying the fully faithful \(G\) to the pointwise tensor and colimits under \(F\). The unit need not be compact. If \(r=0\), all tensor products of localization fibres are empty products, so \(C_f=B\) and every category in (KTC.19) is \(\operatorname{Mod}_B\). If some \(f_i\) is a unit in \(H^0(B)\), its fibre is zero, the completion prestack is empty and all three categories are zero. Neither boundary case requires a convergence convention.

3.162. The exterior tensor equivalence for formal affine charts

Let \(B'\) be a second connective commutative complex DG algebra with a finite list \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\). Put \(D=B\otimes_{\mathbf C}B'\), and regard the two lists as a combined list \(h\) in \(D\). The actual point functors satisfy \[ \widehat Y_f\times\widehat Y_g \simeq\widehat Y_h\subset\operatorname{Spec}D . \tag{KTC.22} \] Indeed a \(D\)-point is a pair of points of the two affines. If the image ideals have exponents \(a,b\), their sum has exponent at most \(a+b-1\), since every such product has at least \(a\) factors from the first ideal or \(b\) from the second. Nilpotence of the sum implies nilpotence of each ideal. These are conditions on full unions of components, so the comparison retains all DG paths.

The external Koszul module \(K_f\otimes_{\mathbf C}K_g\) is the combined Koszul module \(K_h\), hence compactly generates \(\mathcal T_h\). For any four finite perfect modules of the indicated two rings, finite duality gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\operatorname{RHom}_{D} (P\otimes_{\mathbf C}Q,P'\otimes_{\mathbf C}Q')\\ &\qquad\simeq \operatorname{RHom}_B(P,P') \otimes_{\mathbf C} \operatorname{RHom}_{B'}(Q,Q'). \end{aligned} \tag{KTC.23} \] For finite free modules this is the matrix Hom identity with its total-complex Koszul signs; finite cones and retracts preserve it and prove the perfect case. No interchange of an infinite Hom limit with tensor is being used.

The compact-generator/free-module-bar proof (GSL.9), now applied to the single Koszul generator in each supported category, proves \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal T_f\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal T_g \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T_h,\\ \operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y_f) \otimes_{\mathbf C}\operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y_g) \xrightarrow[\ \mathrm{ext}\ ]{\sim} \operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y_f\times\widehat Y_g). \end{gathered} \tag{KTC.24} \] Explicitly, restricted Yoneda takes values in right DG modules over the full endomorphism algebra of the compact generator, with action by precomposition. The two free-module bars identify the tensor category with right modules over the tensor of these algebras. Equation (KTC.23) is the full endomorphism comparison for the external generator, and that generator detects the target category by (KTC.14). The unit comparison holds on a free representable and on its bar; the counit is detected by the target generator. This constructs inverse functors and their entire mapping-space comparisons.

The first functor in (KTC.24) is ordinary exterior tensor of the supported modules. Its units agree because \(C_f\otimes_{\mathbf C}C_g=C_h\), by the finite localization-fibre formula. Under (KTC.19), its value at the product of power stages is exactly the derived restriction of that exterior tensor. These power-stage products present (KTC.22), and equal exponents are a cofinal subdiagram. Thus the second functor is the canonical exterior functor on the actual product, with the actual monoidal comparison. This proves the formal-affine comparison, without asserting that a filtered union of such charts or its \(H\)-quotient has the same global tensor property.

Figure 3.33. The strict power thickenings and their conservative first reduction are (KTC.1)–(KTC.3). Over the first thickening, the extra exterior generators in (KTC.6) are killed by every later transition, which identifies the actual counit in (KTC.8)–(KTC.10). The Koszul telescope and the inverse equivalences are (KTC.11)–(KTC.21). The formal-chart exterior equivalence is (KTC.22)–(KTC.24). The examples below distinguish complete modules, the noncompact unit and genuinely derived module-system comparisons.

3.163. A zero equation with unbounded module coefficients

Exercise 3.CW. Take \(B=\mathbf C[z]\), \(|z|=-2\), with zero differential, and \(f=0\). Describe the strict relative models, the negative cohomology of every thickening, and the compatible module system obtained from \(M=B[z^{-1}]\). Is \(M\) bounded above or below?

Solution 3.CW. A relative semifree model and its strict quotients are \[ Q=\mathbf C[t,z,s],\qquad |s|=-1,\quad ds=t,\qquad B_N=Q/(t^N),\qquad Q\xrightarrow{\sim}B . \tag{KTC.25} \] The contraction of the regular pair \(t,s\) identifies \(Q\) with \(B\): the two-term polynomial Koszul complex for \(t\) has cohomology \(\mathbf C\) in degree zero. Tensoring its two terms with \(\mathbf C[z]\) proves the statement in every negative degree.

In the quotient, multiplication by \(t\) on \(\mathbf C[t]/t^N\) has kernel \(\mathbf C t^{N-1}\) and cokernel \(\mathbf C\). Consequently the whole cohomology algebra is \[ H^*(B_N)=\mathbf C[z]\otimes \Lambda(\bar\eta_N),\qquad \bar\eta_N=[s t^{N-1}],\quad|\bar\eta_N|=-1 . \tag{KTC.26} \] The map from the zero-equation Koszul model \(B[\eta_N]\) sending \(\eta_N\) to \(s t^{N-1}\) is a quasi-isomorphism. It respects products since \(s^2=0\), and its displayed basis computes every cohomology degree. If \(N'>N\), the transition sends this class to zero, since \(t^{N'-1}=0\) in \(B_N\). Thus the negative class exists at every individual stage but not in its transition limit.

The completion prestack is the whole affine, and \(C_f=B\), since localization at zero is the zero algebra. For \(M=B[z^{-1}]\), its stage modules in the Koszul models and their limit are \[ F(M)_N\simeq M\otimes_{\mathbf C}\Lambda(\eta_N), \qquad GF(M)\simeq M . \tag{KTC.27} \] Transitions fix \(M\) and kill the odd summand. The product-fibre calculation of §3.159 therefore computes the limit, even though \(M\) has a nonzero cohomology group in every even integer degree. In particular it is bounded neither above nor below. This is an actual unbounded module system; no bounded-window replacement is involved.

3.164. The formal disc and its noncompact unit

Exercise 3.CX. For \(B=\mathbf C[t]\), \(f=t\), compute the torsion unit, the complete unit and the compact generator. Prove that the quasicoherent unit of the formal completion is not compact.

Solution 3.CX. The torsion unit is the localization fibre \[ C_t=[\,\mathbf C[t]\longrightarrow\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}]\,], \qquad H^1(C_t)=t^{-1}\mathbf C[t^{-1}],\quad H^j(C_t)=0\ (j\ne1). \tag{KTC.28} \] The terms are in degrees zero and one. The localization inclusion is injective; its quotient has the stated basis of negative monomials. The compact generator is the two-term Koszul module for \(t\), quasi-isomorphic to \(\mathbf C=B/(t)\).

The complete unit is \[ \Lambda_t(B)=\lim_N\mathbf C[t]/t^N =\mathbf C[[t]] \tag{KTC.29} \] in degree zero. Compatible polynomial truncations are exactly formal power series. The maps of this degree-zero inverse system are surjective; the map \(1-\mathrm{shift}\) on their product is surjective too, by successively lifting its prescribed coordinates. Its fibre therefore has no degree-one cohomology, proving the displayed derived limit assertion.

If \(C_t\) were compact in \(\mathcal T_t\), its identity would factor through one term of its filtered presentation \(\operatorname{colim}_N K_N^\vee\). Every degree-one class of \(K_N^\vee\) is killed by \(t^N\), so the factorization would make \(t^N\) kill all of \(H^1(C_t)\). But \[ t^N[\,t^{-N-1}\,]=[\,t^{-1}\,]\ne0 \quad\text{in }\mathbf C[t,t^{-1}]/\mathbf C[t] . \tag{KTC.30} \] This contradiction proves noncompactness. The equivalence (KTC.19) transfers it to the quasicoherent unit and to the complete unit in its actual complete category. Thus this category is not the ordinary module category of \(\mathbf C[[t]]\) with its usual tensor and unit: that ordinary free rank-one module is compact. The difference is also visible in the nonzero ordinary module \(\mathbf C((t))\): \[ \Lambda_t(\mathbf C((t)))=0,\qquad F(\mathbf C((t)))=0 . \tag{KTC.31} \] Multiplication by \(t\) is invertible there, so its derived tensor with every \(K_N\) is zero. Hence it is not a nonzero object in the complete image. Complete-category colimits and tensor use (KTC.21), rather than the corresponding ordinary module operations.

3.165. Two variables and the product formal chart

Exercise 3.CY. For \(B=\mathbf C[t,u]\) and the ideal \((t,u)\), compute the torsion and complete units. Compute \(\Gamma_{t,u}(B/(t))\) and \(\Lambda_{t,u}(B/(t))\), and identify the compact generator.

Solution 3.CY. Tensoring the two localization fibres gives the actual complex \[ C_{t,u}= [\,B\longrightarrow B[t^{-1}]\oplus B[u^{-1}] \longrightarrow B[t^{-1},u^{-1}]\,], \tag{KTC.32} \] in degrees zero, one and two. The first map is \(b\mapsto(b,b)\), and the second is \((a,b)\mapsto b-a\); changing one tensor-basis sign gives this convention. Its degree-zero kernel vanishes. The intersection of the two single-localization rings inside the double-localization ring is \(B\), as their Laurent monomials show, so degree-one cohomology vanishes too. The remaining monomials give \[ \begin{gathered} H^2(C_{t,u})= \bigoplus_{a,b\geq1}\mathbf C\,t^{-a}u^{-b}, \qquad H^j(C_{t,u})=0\ (j\ne2),\\ \Lambda_{t,u}(B)=\mathbf C[[t,u]] . \end{gathered} \tag{KTC.33} \] For completion, the quotients by \((t^N,u^N)\) are ordinary and surject onto one another. Compatible truncations specify one coefficient for each monomial, and the same product-fibre argument as in (KTC.29) eliminates the higher inverse-limit term. The rectangular and total-degree truncations are cofinal, so these are the usual two-variable formal series.

On \(M=B/(t)=\mathbf C[u]\), the \(t\)-localization vanishes, while the \(u\)-localization is \(\mathbf C[u,u^{-1}]\). Thus \[ \begin{gathered} H^1(\Gamma_{t,u}M)=u^{-1}\mathbf C[u^{-1}], \qquad H^j(\Gamma_{t,u}M)=0\ (j\ne1),\\ \Lambda_{t,u}M=\mathbf C[[u]] . \end{gathered} \tag{KTC.34} \] The completion assertion can also be read from the stage complex. Tensor the \(t^N\)-Koszul factor with \(M\), where \(t=0\); it is an exterior factor with zero differential whose positive-exterior transition is zero. The \(u^N\)-factor resolves \(\mathbf C[u]/u^N\). The inverse limit discards the first extra summand and completes the second one, giving exactly the displayed series.

The combined Koszul module resolves \(\mathbf C=B/(t,u)\) and is a compact generator. Its two factors are the compact generators for the two one-variable supported categories. Their actual exterior tensor realizes (KTC.24). Hence the full formal-chart tensor comparison includes the principal-parts complex in degree two and the completed series unit; it does not require either unit to be compact.

3.166. Why a constant ordinary module is not a coherent system

Exercise 3.CZ. In the formal-disc example, describe the compact generator as a system of derived modules. Would taking the ordinary module \(\mathbf C\) at every stage give that object?

Solution 3.CZ. Apply \(F\) to the \(B\)-module \(\mathbf C\). The regular polynomial resolution of \(B_N\) over \(B\) gives \[ F(\mathbf C)_N =\mathbf C\otimes_B^L B_N \simeq\Lambda_{\mathbf C}(\eta_N),\qquad|\eta_N|=-1 . \tag{KTC.35} \] The right side describes the underlying complex. Its full \(B_N\)-module structure is transported from the Koszul algebra \(B[\eta_N]\), \(d\eta_N=t^N\), on which \(\eta_N\) acts by exterior multiplication. This action must not be replaced by the trivial ordinary action on its cohomology. For \(N'>N\), the underlying transition kills \(\eta_{N'}\), because \(t\) is already zero on \(\mathbf C\). The scalar comparison required of a system is over \(B_{N'}\), not over \(B\); its equivalence follows from the associative base-change identity defining \(F\), retaining that full action. The extra negative class is therefore compatible with the system. Its limit is \[ GF(\mathbf C)=\mathbf C,\qquad \Gamma_t\mathbf C=\Lambda_t\mathbf C=\mathbf C . \tag{KTC.36} \] The first equality is the same constant-plus-zero-transition limit, and the other two follow since the module is killed by \(t\). The image \(F(\mathbf C)\) is compact by (KTC.14) and (KTC.19), despite its negative class at each stage.

By contrast, the putative constant system of ordinary modules already fails from level two to level one. There \(B_2=\mathbf C[t]/t^2\) and \(B_1=\mathbf C\), and \[ H^{-n}\bigl(\mathbf C\otimes_{B_2}^L\mathbf C\bigr) =\mathbf C\quad(n\geq0). \tag{KTC.37} \] Resolve \(\mathbf C\) over \(B_2\) by copies of \(B_2\) in all nonpositive degrees, with multiplication by \(t\) as every internal differential. Kernel and image are both \(\mathbf C t\), so this is an exact augmented free resolution. Tensoring with \(\mathbf C\) makes all differentials zero and proves (KTC.37). It cannot be equivalent to the proposed ordinary module at level one. The missing coherence is a mathematical obstruction to that proposed system, rather than a choice of a more convenient presentation.

The formal-affine equivalences (KTC.19)–(KTC.24) extend to the restricted framed union by the supported-category comparison in §§3.167–3.170. The \(H\)-quotient and its global tensor comparison are §§3.171–3.174, and the relative tensor multiplication is §3.175. The nilpotent projector, its Hecke realization, singular-support image and original-field regularity require further arguments. The formal-completion framework is discussed in AGKRRV, The stack of local systems with restricted variation and geometric Langlands theory with nilpotent singular support, in the discussion of quasicoherent sheaves on formal affine schemes.

3.167. Intrinsic support and continuous coreflection

Continue over \(\mathbf C\), with the actual framed restricted functor \(Y_{\mathrm r}\subset Y_{\mathrm B}=\operatorname{Spec}B\) and connected reductive \(H\). Put \(R=H^0(B)\). The coefficient coalgebras of (SCI.3) form a filtered set. Equations (RBC.11)–(RBC.13) give closed ordinary loci with finitely generated ideals \(I_E\subset R\), and \(E\subset F\) implies \(I_F\subset I_E\). Their actual full formal completions satisfy \[ Y_{\mathrm r}\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_E\widehat Y_E, \qquad \mathcal T_E=\operatorname{Loc}(K_E),\quad \Gamma_E=C_E\otimes_B^L(-). \tag{SUL.1} \] Here a finite list of closed degree-zero lifts of generators of \(I_E\) defines the Koszul module \(K_E\) and the localization-fibre tensor \(C_E\) of (KTC.11). The equivalence \(\mathcal T_E\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y_E)\) is (KTC.19). All module categories include complexes unbounded in both directions.

These categories and projectors depend on the ordinary closed locus, rather than on its chosen generating list. Derived localization has cohomology \(H^*(M)[f^{-1}]\), by its exact filtered multiplication telescope. Thus its vanishing says that each cohomology class is killed by some power of \(f\). If the chosen generators \(f_i\) have this property and \(g=\sum a_i f_i\) in \(R\), fix a class and exponents \(n_i\) killing it. Expanding \(g^{\,1+\sum_i(n_i-1)}\) shows that it kills the class: each monomial has one exponent at least \(n_i\). Boundaries act trivially on cohomology, so equality in \(R\) suffices. Consequently \[ \mathcal T_E =\{M:M[g^{-1}]=0\text{ for every }g\in I_E\}, \qquad \mathcal T_E\subset\mathcal T_F\quad(E\subset F). \tag{SUL.2} \] The same reasoning handles radical equality by taking a power of each generator.

Inclusion \(j_E:\mathcal T_E\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_B\) has right adjoint \(\Gamma_E\), with its original counit. To prove it, filter the cofibre of \(\Gamma_EM\to M\) by the successive localization-fibre factors. Each quotient is a localization at one generator, tensored with some earlier factors, so is local for that generator. For such \(L\), finite perfect duality identifies \(\operatorname{RHom}_B(K_E,L)\) with \(K_E^\vee\otimes_B^LL=0\); the localized Koszul contraction proves the vanishing. The class of sources with zero Hom into \(L\) is closed under source colimits, shifts and cones. Since \(\mathcal T_E=\operatorname{Loc}(K_E)\), every source \(N\) in it has zero Hom into every quotient of that finite filtration. Hence \[ \operatorname{Map}_B(N,\Gamma_EM) \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_B(N,M), \qquad N\in\mathcal T_E . \tag{SUL.3} \] This is the entire mapping-space adjunction; shifts give every derived mapping degree. The right adjoint is continuous because it is tensor with \(C_E\). If \(E\subset F\), the adjunction and (SUL.2) give the canonical counit comparisons \[ \Gamma_E\Gamma_F\simeq\Gamma_E,\qquad \Gamma_F\Gamma_E\simeq\Gamma_E . \tag{SUL.4} \] For the first, test (SUL.3) from \(\mathcal T_E\subset\mathcal T_F\); both objects coreflect the same map to \(M\). For the second, \(\Gamma_EM\) already lies in \(\mathcal T_F\). These comparisons are coherent: the space of factorizations in the adjunction is contractible, and their compositions are the same factorizations of the counit.

3.168. The filtered supported category and its unit

For \(E\subset F\), (SUL.4) and its counits supply a coherent map \(\Gamma_EM\to\Gamma_FM\) over \(M\). Define \[ \mathcal T=\operatorname{Loc}\{K_E:E\},\qquad C_S=\operatorname*{colim}_E C_E,\qquad \Gamma_SM=C_S\otimes_B^LM=\operatorname*{colim}_E\Gamma_EM . \tag{SUL.5} \] Every \(\Gamma_EM\) lies in \(\mathcal T\), by (KTC.14). For a fixed \(K_E\), the tail of \(F\) containing \(E\) is cofinal and has \(\Gamma_FK_E\simeq K_E\), compatibly with its counit. Thus \(\Gamma_SK_E\simeq K_E\). Since \(\Gamma_S\) is continuous, the fixed subcategory of its natural counit contains the localizing category generated by these objects. Its image is therefore exactly \(\mathcal T\), and \[ \Gamma_S|_{\mathcal T}\simeq1,\qquad C_S\otimes_B^LC_S\simeq C_S . \tag{SUL.6} \] The second identity is also the diagonal cofinality calculation in the filtered product of coefficient indices, using (SUL.4). All its maps are the original tensor counits.

The category has the ambient colimits and tensor product, with unit \[ \mathbf1_{\mathcal T}=C_S,\qquad \mathcal T\text{ compactly generated by the finite perfect }K_E . \tag{SUL.7} \] Each \(K_E\) is compact because it is finite perfect over \(B\) and the inclusion preserves these colimits. For supported \(M,N\), tensor idempotence gives \(C_S\otimes_B^L(M\otimes_B^LN)\simeq M\otimes_B^LN\), so support is closed under tensor. The counits give its unit constraints. There is no assertion that \(C_S\) is compact.

3.169. The actual quasicoherent category of the framed union

The full prestack colimit (SUL.1) and the affine-point argument in (KTC.4) give \[ \operatorname{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm r}) \simeq\lim_E\operatorname{QCoh}(\widehat Y_E) \simeq\lim_E(\mathcal T_E,\Gamma_E|_{\mathcal T_F}). \tag{SUL.8} \] The indicated transition really is pullback. An ambient \(B\)-module \(M\) restricts first to \(\widehat Y_F\) and then to \(\widehat Y_E\) by the same derived scalar extension as direct restriction to \(\widehat Y_E\). By (KTC.17)–(KTC.19), that last restriction corresponds to \(\Gamma_EM\). These are the natural restriction comparisons on whole diagrams, so their higher compositions agree.

There are explicit inverse functors \[ U(M)=(\Gamma_EM)_E,\qquad V((M_E)_E)=\operatorname*{colim}_E M_E . \tag{SUL.9} \] For \(V\), use the map \(M_E\simeq\Gamma_EM_F\to M_F\) when \(E\subset F\). It is coherent by the specified limit-object comparisons and the counits in (SUL.3). Each term lies in \(\mathcal T\). At a fixed \(E\), continuity and the cofinal tail \(F\supset E\) give the actual comparison \[ \Gamma_E\operatorname*{colim}_F M_F \simeq\operatorname*{colim}_F\Gamma_EM_F \xrightarrow{\sim}M_E . \tag{SUL.10} \] On that tail the system is the constant \(M_E\) by its specified compatibilities. This proves \(UV\simeq1\). Conversely \(VU(M)=\Gamma_SM\simeq M\) for \(M\in\mathcal T\). The same natural maps act on mapping complexes and all coherent transformations, so these are inverse functors of full categories. In particular restriction gives \[ F_{\mathrm r}:\mathcal T\xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm r}). \tag{SUL.11} \] It is symmetric monoidal. Indeed \(\Gamma_E(M\otimes_B^LN)\simeq\Gamma_EM\otimes_B^L\Gamma_EN\) by \(C_E^2\simeq C_E\), and \(\Gamma_EC_S\simeq C_E\). Thus the actual tensor and unit at every level are exactly the restrictions of (SUL.7).

3.170. The framed exterior equivalence

Finite products of spaces commute with filtered colimits, by the finite-simplex proof in (RBC.19). Thus the product \(Y_{\mathrm r}\times Y_{\mathrm r}\) is the filtered colimit of \(\widehat Y_E\times\widehat Y_F\). By (KTC.22), these are the completions inside \(\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{\mathbf C}B)\) along the combined ideals on the two factors. Applying (SUL.8)–(SUL.11) to this family identifies its quasicoherent category with the supported category \(\mathcal T_2\), compactly generated by \(K_E\otimes_{\mathbf C}K_F\).

The full finite-perfect Hom identity (KTC.23) holds for every pair of these external generators and respects composition. The two-variable multi-object free-module bars of (GSL.9) therefore prove \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal T\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal T \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T_2,\\ \operatorname{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm r})\otimes_{\mathbf C} \operatorname{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm r}) \xrightarrow[\ \mathrm{ext}\ ]{\sim} \operatorname{QCoh}(Y_{\mathrm r}\times Y_{\mathrm r}). \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.12} \] Its generator functor is fully faithful by that Hom identity; its image generates the target. The Yoneda bar gives the unit on representables and every free-module realization; the target generators detect its counit. At each pair of power stages its value is the exterior derived scalar extension of the original two modules, so the displayed functor is the canonical exterior functor. Its unit is \(C_S\otimes_{\mathbf C}C_S\), the filtered colimit of the exterior level units. This is the actual product supported unit, which also checks the monoidal comparison.

3.171. Finite equivariant Koszul generators

The ideals \(I_E\) are scheme-theoretically \(H\)-stable by (SCI.10): conjugation acts linearly on faithful matrix coordinates and fixes their inverse determinant over every coefficient ring. The same action preserves their full formal completions. Choose finitely many ordinary ideal generators. The rational coaction places each in a finite-dimensional stable subspace, and stability of the ideal keeps those subspaces inside it. Their sum gives \[ W_E\subset I_E\subset R,\qquad \dim_{\mathbf C}W_E<\infty,\qquad (W_E)=I_E . \tag{SUL.13} \] Here \(W_E\) is a finite rational representation, not a tuple assumed fixed by \(H\).

Let \(\mathcal E=\operatorname{QCoh}(BH)\), the category of derived rational representations. Its invariant projection and full unbounded group-cobar contraction are the earlier bundle lesson, §4.5, and (GSL.5)–(GSL.6), with \(H\) in place of the frame group. The proof applies verbatim: projection onto the trivial isotypic summand of \(\mathcal O(H)\), followed by evaluation of its constant value, is bi-invariant and has value one on the unit. The same contraction uses only adjacent cobar columns, so is valid for an unbounded complex. In particular \[ H^0\operatorname{RHom}_H(W_E,B) =\operatorname{Hom}_H(W_E,H^0(B)). \tag{SUL.14} \] Indeed the left mapping complex is the exact invariant projection of \(W_E^\vee\otimes B\), and finite dual tensor commutes with cohomology. This also proves projectivity of the finite representation in the rational heart.

Lift the inclusion in (SUL.13) through (SUL.14) to a point of the whole mapping space \(W_E\to B\) in \(\mathcal E\). The lift can have higher choices; none are discarded. Free commutative algebra adjunction and derived scalar extension construct the actual equivariant algebra and module \[ P_E=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal E}(W_E)\longrightarrow B, \qquad K_E^H=B\underset{P_E}{\otimes^L}\mathbf C . \tag{SUL.15} \] The augmentation of \(P_E\) sends \(W_E\) to zero. The finite equivariant Koszul complex \(P_E\otimes\Lambda(W_E[1])\), with differential the identity \(W_E\to P_E\), resolves that augmentation: in any basis it is the polynomial regular-sequence resolution proved in (RBC.14). Its differential is equivariant because the inclusion of the entire representation is equivariant. Extending scalars along the actual algebra map in (SUL.15) retains all action coherences. Explicitly its two-sided algebra bar has terms \(B\otimes P_E^{\otimes n}\otimes\mathbf C\); faces are multiplication and the action maps, and degeneracies insert units. They are all maps in \(\mathcal E\). The full bar and its extra-degeneracy comparisons compute the derived extension, so this construction supplies a coherent \(H\)-action on the full object, without imposing equivariance on the individual power-generator tuples of (RBC.14).

After forgetting the action it is a finite perfect Koszul \(B\)-module whose degree-zero generating ideal is \(I_E\). The intrinsic support proof (SUL.2) and (KTC.14) imply \[ \operatorname{Loc}(K_E^H|_B)=\mathcal T_E . \tag{SUL.16} \] Thus the equivariant generator has the full ordinary support required, independently of its chosen lift.

3.172. The quotient category and compact generators

The intrinsic projectors above are compatible with the whole \(H\)-action nerve. Their localization-fibre formulas commute with derived scalar extension; the pulled-back ideals are the same stable ideals. The coreflection property (SUL.3) identifies the resulting functors and all their compositions. Thus (SUL.11) is an equivalence with its full rational action.

The frame torsor of (RBC.23) and full faithfully flat descent (RSP.8)–(RSP.10) identify the quotient category: \[ \mathcal A:=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r}) \simeq\mathcal T^H . \tag{SUL.17} \] Here \(\mathcal T^H\) is the full category of equivariant \(B\)-modules whose underlying module belongs to \(\mathcal T\). This means the entire action-nerve totalization, not equivariance only on \(H^0\). For example its affine ambient category is \(\operatorname{Mod}_B(\operatorname{QCoh}(BH))\): the relative affine-map module equivalence (CSD.21) applied to \([\operatorname{Spec}B/H]\to BH\) proves that identification. The full subcategory is stable under the action because every coefficient locus is \(H\)-stable. Taking its action-nerve limit therefore gives precisely the supported equivariant objects. The equivariant restriction equivalence gives (SUL.17) on each nerve level, hence on its totalization.

Let \(V\) range over finite rational \(H\)-representations and put \(P_{E,V}=K_E^H\otimes_{\mathbf C}V\). For any supported equivariant \(M\), equivariant finite duality and the same cobar contraction give the full formula \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{B,H}(P_{E,V},M) \simeq \bigl(V^\vee\otimes_{\mathbf C} \operatorname{RHom}_B(K_E^H|_B,M|_B)\bigr)^H . \tag{SUL.18} \] The inner complex is rational: it is the underlying scalar complex of the equivariant module \((K_E^H)^\vee\otimes_B^LM\). Exact rational invariants commute with colimits, by the natural isotypic projection. Since the underlying Koszul module is finite perfect, (SUL.18) proves compactness of every \(P_{E,V}\).

These objects detect zero. If every displayed complex vanishes, each cohomology representation of the inner complex has zero Hom from every finite \(V\). Any nonzero rational vector belongs to a finite representation; complete reducibility supplies a simple summand and a nonzero such Hom. Exactness of invariants makes it a genuine cohomology test. Hence the inner complexes vanish for every \(E\). Equation (SUL.16) and generation of \(\mathcal T\) make \(M|_B=0\), and the conservative frame pullback makes \(M=0\). We have proved \[ \mathcal A\text{ is compactly generated by the }P_{E,V}. \tag{SUL.19} \] This proof does not make the quasicoherent unit compact.

3.173. The global quotient exterior equivalence and its categorical dual

The product stack is \([Y_{\mathrm r}\times Y_{\mathrm r}/(H\times H)]\), since both torsors and their maps form products on every test ring. Its supported description is (SUL.17) for the product. The external \(P_{E,V}\boxtimes P_{F,W}\) compactly generate it. To verify detection, use (SUL.18) for the product and the combined Koszul generators. Finite representations of \(H\times H\) are generated by external ones: decompose for the first reductive factor; its finite multiplicity spaces carry the commuting second action, and decompose those as well. Schur's scalar lemma identifies the multiplicity action. This is the complete argument of §3.91 applied to \(H\).

For external perfect supported objects, (KTC.23) and the two independent rational invariant projections give \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r}^2} (P\boxtimes Q,P'\boxtimes Q') \simeq \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(P,P') \otimes_{\mathbf C}\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(Q,Q'). \tag{SUL.20} \] The invariant identity follows by applying the two commuting Reynolds projections to the two tensor factors; their image is the tensor of their images. This holds on all internal cohomological degrees. It is a natural Hom comparison, so respects composition and the graded tensor signs. Full multi-object free-module bars and the actual product generators now give \[ \mathrm{ext}:\mathcal A\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal A \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r}^2). \tag{SUL.21} \] The units and counits are proved on representables by the Hom comparison, extended by the free bars, and detected by the product generators. On the actual torsor nerve this functor is exterior pullback and tensor, so it is the canonical exterior equivalence with its monoidal structure.

For completeness the compact-generator model also gives a categorical dual. Let \(\mathscr D\) be the small full DG category of the chosen generators and their finite cones, shifts and retracts. Restricted Yoneda takes values in right DG modules; the evaluation free bar gives \[ \mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathscr D}, \qquad \mathcal A^\vee\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathscr D^{\mathrm{op}}}. \tag{SUL.22} \] The evaluation is the full right/left-module tensor coend. The coevaluation is the diagonal bimodule with value \(\mathscr D(d,e)\), contravariant in \(d\) and covariant in \(e\). Its two triangle contractions are \[ \int^{e}\mathscr D(d,e)\otimes M(e)\simeq M(d), \qquad \int^{d}N(d)\otimes\mathscr D(d,e)\simeq N(e). \tag{SUL.23} \] In their enriched two-sided bars, composition is the interior face and the two module actions are the endpoint faces; inserting the identity at the represented object is the contracting extra degeneracy. The contractions agree with all module maps, so prove both duality triangles on every module realization. This asserts dualizability of the presentable DG category. It does not identify its dual with itself by an unproved integration functor.

3.174. The full tensor-category diagonal algebra

Combine the actual affine diagonal and projection formula (RDI.9)–(RDI.13) with (SUL.21). Multiplication and its right adjoint are \[ m_{\mathcal A}=\Delta^*\mathrm{ext}, \qquad \delta_{\mathcal A}=\mathrm{ext}^{-1}\Delta_*, \qquad m_{\mathcal A}\dashv\delta_{\mathcal A}. \tag{SUL.24} \] The right adjoint is continuous and \(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\)-linear: these are exactly the actual affine forgetful functor and its projection formula. The full regular-algebra comparison (RDI.16), now under the exterior equivalence, is the canonical algebra identity \[ (\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\otimes\mathsf L_{\mathrm r})(R_{\mathcal R}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \delta_{\mathcal A}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}). \tag{SUL.25} \] It preserves the multiplication and unit because its pullback to each affine pair is the same tautological isomorphism algebra as in (RDI.16)–(RDI.19). The full derived mapping-space comparison there determines the map, not only an isomorphism class of the object. Equation (RDI.9) consequently reads \[ \mathcal A\simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{\delta_{\mathcal A}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal A})} (\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A). \tag{SUL.26} \] Under this equivalence multiplication is free module formation and its right adjoint forgets the algebra action.

3.175. The actual relative tensor multiplication

We prove the required relative comparison with its functor. The full Ran category \(\mathcal R\) has compact unit and dualizable compact generators by (KG.19)–(KG.23). Its multiplication \(m_{\mathcal R}\) sends compact external generators to compact objects: for compact dualizable \(T\), the functor \(\operatorname{RHom}(S,T^\vee\otimes-)\) preserves colimits when \(S\) is compact. Its actual right adjoint is \[ \delta_{\mathcal R}(M)= \int^{S,T\in\mathcal R^c} \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal R}(S\otimes T,M) \otimes(S\boxtimes T). \tag{SUL.27} \] The coend is over the full compact DG category. Testing compact external generators and contracting its Yoneda bar proves the adjunction; their compactness proves continuity of this right adjoint. For compact dualizable acting objects, moving their duals across those Hom tests proves bimodule linearity of its adjunction mate. Arbitrary acting objects are colimits of compacts, and both sides preserve those colimits, so the mate is linear for all objects. Its value at the unit is the same regular algebra \(R_{\mathcal R}\) of (KG.23).

The right adjoint is conservative. If \(\delta_{\mathcal R}(M)=0\), adjunction tests from \(\mathbf1\boxtimes X\) give \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal R}(X,M)=0\) for every \(X\), so \(M=0\). Its monad on \(\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\) is tensoring with \(R_{\mathcal R}\), by bimodule linearity, with multiplication and unit the adjunction mates of those in (KG.23). The full free-module comparison therefore gives \[ \mathcal R\simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{R_{\mathcal R}} (\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R). \tag{SUL.28} \] Here is the monadic argument explicitly. For a module over that tensor algebra, realize its augmented free-module bar using \(m_{\mathcal R}\) on the free terms. Applying \(\delta_{\mathcal R}\) commutes with this realization and recovers the original module, because its bar has the contracting extra degeneracy. The comparison counit for an object of \(\mathcal R\) becomes an equivalence after \(\delta_{\mathcal R}\); conservativity proves it was already an equivalence. The other comparison is the same free-module contraction. Thus the comparison includes all action maps and coherent transformations.

We also need its change of coefficients. If \(\mathcal C\to\mathcal B\) is a continuous symmetric monoidal functor and \(a\) a commutative algebra object of \(\mathcal C\), the free/forgetful \(a\)-module adjunction is continuous and \(\mathcal C\)-linear on both sides. Tensoring this adjunction by \(\mathcal B\) over \(\mathcal C\) retains its two triangle maps. The resulting monad is tensoring with the image algebra \(a_{\mathcal B}\). Its right adjoint is conservative: the objects obtained from free modules generate the balanced tensor category, since every pure tensor with a module is the realization of its free-module bar; a pure tensor with a free module is one of these free generators by balancing. Adjunction tests from them detect zero. The preceding explicit bar comparison therefore proves this change-of-coefficients equivalence, with no compact-unit assumption on \(\mathcal B\).

Apply it to \(\mathcal C=\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\) and \(a=R_{\mathcal R}\). Associative balancing and (SUL.28) give \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal A\underset{\mathcal R}{\otimes}\mathcal A &\simeq (\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A) \underset{\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R}{\otimes}\mathcal R\\ &\simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\otimes\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}) (R_{\mathcal R})} (\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A). \end{aligned} \tag{SUL.29} \] For the first comparison, a balanced triple \((a,b,r)\) maps to \(a\boxtimes_{\mathcal R}(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}(r)\otimes_{\mathcal A}b)\) in the relative category; its inverse sends \(a\boxtimes_{\mathcal R}b\) to the triple with \(r=\mathbf1_{\mathcal R}\). Moving the two source actions across the balancing gives the two inverse comparisons. Their identities are associativity and the unit identities in the full two-sided tensor bars, so include all higher comparisons.

Now (SUL.25) and (SUL.26) identify the last category with \(\mathcal A\). The resulting equivalence is precisely the multiplication functor: \[ \mathcal A\underset{\mathcal R}{\otimes}\mathcal A \xrightarrow[\ a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes b\ ]{\ \sim\ }\mathcal A . \tag{SUL.30} \] To verify this map, the free module attached to \(b\in\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\) in the middle of (SUL.29) corresponds to the balanced tensor of \(b\) with the Ran unit. The indicated multiplication sends it to \(m_{\mathcal A}(b)\), exactly the free diagonal-module functor in (SUL.26). Their free action maps agree by the canonical algebra map (SUL.25); their full module bars therefore agree on every object. This proves (RDI.20) with its actual functor. It does not by itself construct the geometric nilpotent projector or prove continuity of the right adjoint of \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\).

Figure 3.34. The support projectors and the filtered unit are (SUL.1)–(SUL.7). The two inverse functors for the actual union are (SUL.8)–(SUL.11). Equivariant generators are constructed by the full derived pushout (SUL.13)–(SUL.16), and their Hom tests give (SUL.17)–(SUL.21). The regular algebra and module bars identify the actual relative tensor multiplication in (SUL.24)–(SUL.30). The examples below retain the infinite-component unit, equivariant differential weights and nonflat derived intersections.

3.176. All closed points of an affine line

Exercise 3.DA. Take \(B=\mathbf C[t]\), with coefficient loci indexed by finite subsets \(F\subset\mathbf C\), and \(I_F=(p_F)\), where \(p_F=\prod_{\lambda\in F}(t-\lambda)\). Describe the supported category of their formal union and its unit. The empty subset has \(p_F=1\).

Solution 3.DA. Every rational denominator factors into finitely many linear factors. Thus the localization-fibre formula gives \[ C_S=\operatorname{fib}(\mathbf C[t]\longrightarrow\mathbf C(t)), \qquad H^1(C_S)=\mathbf C(t)/\mathbf C[t],\quad H^j(C_S)=0\ (j\ne1). \tag{SUL.31} \] The localization inclusion is injective. Polynomial division first removes the polynomial part of a fraction. Bézout identities for distinct powers of the linear factors then split its remaining fraction into principal parts. The expansion is unique: the highest pole at any fixed \(\lambda\) cannot be cancelled by fractions regular there. Hence \[ \begin{gathered} H^1(C_S)= \bigoplus_{\lambda\in\mathbf C,\ j\geq1} \mathbf C\,(t-\lambda)^{-j},\\ \mathcal T\simeq\prod_{\lambda\in\mathbf C}\mathcal T_\lambda, \qquad \mathcal T_\lambda=\operatorname{Loc}(B/(t-\lambda)). \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.32} \] For the categorical assertion, partial fractions identify \(C_S\) with the sum of the individual fibre units \(C_\lambda\). Tensoring with a supported module gives its sum of primary components. The cross projectors vanish for \(\lambda\ne\mu\): the two linear factors generate the unit ideal, so their joint Koszul support is empty by (SUL.2). The coreflection adjunction also makes all cross mapping complexes zero. Conversely the sum of any tuple of primary supported modules has precisely that tuple of projections. These two functors and their counits are inverse, proving the product description on all unbounded complexes.

The actual tensor unit has a nonzero component at every \(\lambda\). Its finite-component truncations satisfy \[ \mathbf1_{\mathcal T} \simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{F\ \mathrm{finite}} \mathbf1_F,\qquad \mathbf1_{\mathcal T}\ \text{is not compact}. \tag{SUL.33} \] If its identity factored through a finite truncation, its component outside that finite set would factor through zero, contradicting the nonzero identity there. This proves noncompactness directly. The category includes arbitrary tuples; only its compact objects have finite component support, by the same identity-factorization argument applied to any compact object.

3.177. An equivariant differential and its weight tests

Exercise 3.DB. Let \(H=\mathbf G_m\) act on \(B=\mathbf C[x]\) with \(x\) of weight one. For the stable ideal \((x)\), construct an equivariant Koszul generator. Write \(\mathbf C(n)\) for the representation \(a\mapsto a^n\), and compute \(\operatorname{Ext}^j_{B,H}(\mathbf C(n),\mathbf C(m))\). Does the untwisted Koszul object alone generate the equivariant supported category?

Solution 3.DB. The finite coordinate space is \(W=\mathbf C(1)\). Its equivariant Koszul module is \[ \begin{gathered} K=B[\eta],\qquad|\eta|=-1,\quad d\eta=x,\quad \mathrm{wt}(\eta)=1,\\ K(n)=[\,B\otimes\mathbf C(n+1)\xrightarrow{x} B\otimes\mathbf C(n)\,]. \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.34} \] The two terms of \(K(n)\) are in degrees minus one and zero. The augmentation to \(\mathbf C(n)\) is a quasi-isomorphism, since multiplication by \(x\) on \(B\) is injective with that quotient. The odd generator must have weight one: otherwise the differential would not commute with the action. Thus (SUL.15) carries actual differential data.

Apply the full Hom complex of this two-term resolution to \(\mathbf C(m)\). The differential is zero, since \(x\) acts by zero on the target. Taking exact invariants in its two degrees gives \[ \operatorname{Ext}^j_{B,H}(\mathbf C(n),\mathbf C(m)) = \begin{cases} \mathbf C,&j=0,\ m=n,\\ \mathbf C,&j=1,\ m=n+1,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{SUL.35} \] In particular the nonzero supported object \(\mathbf C(2)\) satisfies \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{B,H}(K(0),\mathbf C(2))=0 . \tag{SUL.36} \] Thus the untwisted object does not generate. All twists in (SUL.19) supply the missing weight tests. They also retain the degree-one maps between adjacent weights, which an ordinary invariant-fibre calculation would omit.

3.178. A quotient for which relative tensor multiplication fails

Exercise 3.DC. Let \(\mathcal R_0=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathbf C[t,u]}\), \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathbf C}\), and let the monoidal functor be scalar extension along \(t,u\mapsto0\). Compute \(\mathcal A_0\otimes_{\mathcal R_0}\mathcal A_0\). Is its multiplication to \(\mathcal A_0\) an equivalence?

Solution 3.DC. The free/forgetful change-of-coefficients argument in §3.175 for ordinary module algebras gives \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal A_0\underset{\mathcal R_0}{\otimes}\mathcal A_0 \simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{D},\\ D=\mathbf C\underset{\mathbf C[t,u]}{\otimes^L}\mathbf C =\Lambda_{\mathbf C}(\epsilon_t,\epsilon_u), \quad|\epsilon_t|=|\epsilon_u|=-1,\quad d=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.37} \] The equality is the regular polynomial Koszul resolution of the two coordinates. Its cohomology is \[ \begin{gathered} H^0(D)=\mathbf C,\qquad H^{-1}(D)=\mathbf C\epsilon_t\oplus\mathbf C\epsilon_u,\\ H^{-2}(D)=\mathbf C\epsilon_t\epsilon_u, \qquad H^j(D)=0\ (j\ne0,-1,-2). \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.38} \] Multiplication is scalar extension along the augmentation \(D\to\mathbf C\). On the full endomorphism complex of the free rank-one module it induces \[ \operatorname{RHom}_D(D,D)=D \longrightarrow \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C,\mathbf C)=\mathbf C . \tag{SUL.39} \] It kills both degree-minus-one generators and their nonzero degree-minus-two product. It is therefore not fully faithful and not an equivalence. Equivalently the image of the source regular algebra is \(D\), whereas the target diagonal algebra is \(\mathbf C\), so the hypothesis (SUL.25) fails. The ordinary tensor product would give only \(\mathbf C\) and conceal the obstruction.

3.179. The elliptic unit and a noncontinuous right adjoint

Exercise 3.DD. For an elliptic curve and \(H=\mathbf G_m\), decide whether the unit of \(\mathcal A=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r})\) is compact. What does this imply about continuity of the right adjoint of \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\)?

Solution 3.DD. The full framed chart and root-pair decomposition are (RBC.27)–(RBC.29). Conjugation is trivial, so the unframed stack adds \(B\mathbf G_m\). The finite-root-pair presentations, with their full DG clopen decompositions, give \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal A\simeq \prod_{(\lambda,\mu)\in(\mathbf C^\times)^2}\mathcal A_{\lambda,\mu},\\ \mathcal A_{\lambda,\mu}=\operatorname{QCoh}\!\left( \widehat{(\mathbf G_m)^2}_{(\lambda,\mu)} \times\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C[\xi]\times B\mathbf G_m \right),\qquad |\xi|=-1 . \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.40} \] One obtains this product by taking the inverse limit of the finite-root-pair product categories. The underlying finite unions are actual clopen decompositions on all affine tests, as proved in §3.146, including disconnected coefficients. Thus no restriction to connected tests is implicit.

The unit has nonzero component at every root pair, since its pullback to the corresponding ordinary point is the nonzero scalar unit. Its finite-component truncations have colimit the unit, and \[ \mathbf1_{\mathcal A} =\operatorname*{colim}_{F\ \mathrm{finite}}\mathbf1_F, \qquad \mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\ \text{is not compact}. \tag{SUL.41} \] The proof is the identity-factorization argument of (SUL.33). In contrast the full Ran unit is compact by (KG.23).

There is an actual right adjoint, constructed without a continuity assumption: \[ \begin{gathered} \mathsf U_{\mathrm r}(M)= \int^{T\in\mathcal R^c} \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}(T),M) \otimes T,\\ \mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\dashv\mathsf U_{\mathrm r}. \end{gathered} \tag{SUL.42} \] Testing compact source objects and contracting the enriched Yoneda bar gives its mapping-space adjunction; arbitrary source objects follow from their compact free-module bars. If this right adjoint preserved colimits, that adjunction would make \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\) carry each compact object to a compact object. Its value on the compact Ran unit is the noncompact unit (SUL.41), a contradiction. Thus the right adjoint is not continuous in this example. This does not contradict the relative tensor equivalence (SUL.30), which asserts a different functor and was proved by its actual algebra-module bars.

The restricted global exterior comparison, categorical dual and relative tensor multiplication above are over the complex numbers. RSE.37–RSE.38 and NTR.16 give the compatible restricted geometric projector. GFP.55–GFP.56 prove its original-complex full-image regularity and nilpotent-support containment. GZR.33 gives equality with all independent nilpotent support over the complex numbers. The other geometric ground fields retain their separate requirements. For the relative tensor formulation see AGKRRV, The stack of local systems with restricted variation and geometric Langlands theory with nilpotent singular support, “Tensor products over representations versus quasicoherent sheaves.”

3.180. Supported perfect objects and their tensor duals

Retain the actual category \(\mathcal A=\mathcal T^H\) of (SUL.17), over \(\mathbf C\). Write \(j\) for its forgetful inclusion into equivariant \(B\)-modules. Its colimits and its tensor product are computed on the underlying modules; its tensor unit is the equivariant \(C_S\) of (SUL.5). The unit generally is not a perfect \(B\)-module.

In contrast, every compact object has a finite perfect underlying module and belongs to one finite support category \(\mathcal T_E\). Here is the required compact-object argument. The full generator bars of (SUL.22) present every object as a colimit of cells on the \(P_{E,V}\). Each coefficient complex is a filtered colimit of finite-dimensional total subcomplexes: the differential closure of finitely many vectors is finite, because the differential squares to zero. A finite skeleton of the simplicial free bar uses finitely many attaching steps. Restricting to finite coefficient subcomplexes and finitely many summands, and closing under their finitely many face and differential images, therefore gives finite cell approximations to that skeleton. The skeleta and these approximations form a filtered system with the original bar as colimit. A compact object's identity factors through one such finite cell object, so it is a retract of it. Finite sums, cones, shifts and retracts of the generators have finite perfect underlying modules. Their finitely many support indices are dominated by a single \(E\), by filteredness. This proves the assertion without a bound on the cohomology of \(B\).

For a finite perfect equivariant supported object define \[ P^*=\operatorname{RHom}_B(jP,B). \tag{SDU.1} \] The finite perfect dual has the induced full rational action: its evaluation and coevaluation are maps in equivariant modules. Its support is the same. Indeed localization commutes with finite perfect duality, so \(P[g^{-1}]=0\) implies \(P^*[g^{-1}]=0\). Equation (SUL.2) then puts it in the same \(\mathcal T_E\). Equivariant finite duality and exact rational invariants give \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(P,M) \simeq\bigl(P^*\otimes_B^LjM\bigr)^H. \tag{SDU.2} \] The right side preserves colimits in \(M\). Thus every equivariant supported object with finite perfect underlying module is compact, in particular \(P^*\). This also proves the converse characterization needed above.

The filtered projector also has the full coreflection adjunction. For a fixed compact Koszul generator, mapping into \(\Gamma_SM=\operatorname*{colim}_F\Gamma_FM\) commutes with that colimit. On its cofinal support tail the comparisons are the equivalences (SUL.3). The class of sources for which the mapping comparison is an equivalence is closed under source colimits, shifts and cones, hence contains all supported modules. The same natural comparisons on the action nerve prove the equivariant statement. Alternatively its compact tests are \(P_{E,V}\), which are compact even in the ambient equivariant module category by finite perfect duality and exact invariants. Thus every map from a supported equivariant source to an ambient target factors uniquely, in its whole mapping space, through that target's \(\Gamma_S\).

These are duals for the supported monoidal structure itself. Compose the ambient coevaluation \(B\to P\otimes_B^LP^*\) with \(C_S\to B\) to obtain its supported coevaluation. The ambient evaluation \(P^*\otimes_B^LP\to B\) has supported source, so the full coreflection adjunction (SUL.3), extended by (SUL.5), factors it uniquely through \(C_S\). Both triangle identities become the usual finite perfect duality triangles after the conservative inclusion into \(B\)-modules: the inserted \(C_S\to B\) acts as the unit equivalence on each supported factor. Their coherences are the same coreflection factorizations. Consequently \[ \begin{gathered} (P^*)^*\simeq P,\qquad (P\otimes_{\mathcal A}Q)^*\simeq Q^*\otimes_{\mathcal A}P^*,\\ (\mathcal A^c)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow[\ P\mapsto P^*\ ]{\sim}\mathcal A^c. \end{gathered} \tag{SDU.3} \] The derived evaluation formulas include the graded tensor signs. Finite perfect biduality proves full faithfulness of the last functor on mapping complexes; biduality also proves essential surjectivity. Tensor products of compact objects remain compact, by the finite perfect characterization and their supported underlying tensor product. Compactness of the unit is not used.

3.181. Completion tests on compact objects

Fix a compact \(P\), a support index \(E\) for it, and \(F\supset E\). If \(g\in I_F\), then \(P[g^{-1}]=0\). Compactness of \(jP\) in \(\operatorname{Mod}_B\) applied to the multiplication telescope gives \[ \operatorname*{colim}_{n} \operatorname{RHom}_B(jP,jP) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_B(jP,jP[g^{-1}])=0. \tag{SDU.4} \] The transition is multiplication by \(g\) on the target. Filtered colimits commute with cohomology of complexes. Thus the identity class becomes zero at some stage: \(g^N:jP\to jP\) is nullhomotopic for one finite \(N\). This exponent acts on the whole object, even when its cohomology is unbounded.

There is consequently a full vanishing \[ \operatorname{RHom}_B(B[g^{-1}],jP)=0. \tag{SDU.5} \] Indeed the left side is the inverse limit of \(jP\) with transition \(g\). Its explicit inverse-limit complex is the fibre of \(1-T\) on the product of the terms, where \(T\) shifts one position and applies \(g\). The chosen nullhomotopy of \(g^N\), applied in every coordinate, makes \(T^N\) nullhomotopic. The finite geometric sum \(1+T+\cdots+T^{N-1}\) is therefore an inverse of \(1-T\) in the homotopy category, by the identities with \(1-T^N\). An invertible morphism there is an equivalence, so its fibre vanishes. No boundedness or Mittag–Leffler hypothesis enters this finite homotopy calculation.

For a finite generating list of \(I_F\), apply (SDU.5) successively to its localization-fibre tensor factors. The canonical map induced by the counit \(C_F\to B\) is an equivalence \[ jP\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{RHom}_B(C_F,jP). \tag{SDU.6} \] For one factor this follows by applying Hom to its fibre triangle, using (SDU.5). Iterated tensor/Hom adjunction proves the statement for all factors. This is the actual counit-induced comparison, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

The same argument works at each level of the \(H\)-action nerve. Derived base change retains finite perfectness, the supported object and each chosen nullhomotopy. The counit-induced maps in (SDU.6) are natural in that nerve; taking its full mapping-complex totalization gives the equivariant assertion. Finally \(C_S=\operatorname*{colim}_F C_F\), and the tail \(F\supset E\) is cofinal. On that tail the maps from the fixed equivariant \(P\) in (SDU.6) are compatible equivalences. We obtain \[ (jP)^H\xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal A},P), \qquad P\in\mathcal A^c. \tag{SDU.7} \] The source on the left is the full derived rational invariant complex. The unbounded cobar contraction is (GSL.5)–(GSL.6); ordinary fixed vectors alone would not justify the preceding nerve argument.

3.182. Continuous global sections and their precise meaning

Define a continuous functor by the supported module description: \[ \Gamma_!(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r},M):=(jM)^H. \tag{SDU.8} \] Forgetting to the underlying module preserves colimits. The exact rational invariant projection also preserves them, by the reductive Reynolds proof in §3.171. Thus this formula defines the functor on every unbounded object. There is a canonical natural transformation from it to ordinary global sections, induced by \(C_S\to B\), and (SDU.7) identifies that transformation on all compact objects.

It is the unique continuous extension of ordinary global sections from the compact subcategory. To verify uniqueness with its maps, use the compact-generator bar (SUL.22): a continuous functor is the realization of its values on the free representables and their full coefficient/action diagrams. Specifying its enriched restriction to the compact category specifies precisely those values and diagrams. The comparison on representables extends through that bar, and the two bar contractions give the unique compatible equivalence. This also proves that (SDU.8) is independent of the chosen equivariant Koszul generators and framing presentation: the intrinsic tensor unit, its ordinary global-section functor and the full compact subcategory determine that restriction.

The functor has a natural non-unital right-lax symmetric monoidal structure. For underlying equivariant modules the canonical derived balancing map and the invariant projections give \[ (jM)^H\otimes_{\mathbf C}(jN)^H \longrightarrow (jM\otimes_B^LjN)^H. \tag{SDU.9} \] The balancing map is the map from the degree-zero term to the full two-sided \(B\)-module bar. The actions, face maps and graded symmetry give associativity and symmetry, including their higher comparisons. This construction supplies no map from \(\mathbf C\) to \((C_S)^H\), so no unital structure is asserted. Neither the definition nor its compact-object characterization identifies \(\Gamma_!\) with a left adjoint of the unit functor.

3.183. Canonical tensor self-duality and its diagonal kernel

Consider the continuous pairing \[ \mathcal A\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathcal A \xrightarrow{\ \otimes_{\mathcal A}\ }\mathcal A \xrightarrow{\ \Gamma_!\ }\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf C}. \tag{SDU.10} \] Equation (SDU.2) identifies its value on \((P^*,M)\), for compact \(P\), with \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal A}(P,M)\). These representable continuous functionals are the compact generators of the dual DG category in (SUL.22). The anti-equivalence (SDU.3) identifies all their Hom complexes and composition maps with those of the compact generators on the first factor. The full two-sided module bars therefore extend this generator identification to an equivalence \[ \mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A^\vee, \qquad M\longmapsto \bigl[N\longmapsto\Gamma_!(M\otimes_{\mathcal A}N)\bigr]. \tag{SDU.11} \] This is the canonical tensor self-duality. The proof identifies the actual pairing, rather than merely an abstract equivalence with an opposite-module category. Its continuous dual of the unit functor \(u:\operatorname{Vect}\to\mathcal A\) is exactly \(\Gamma_!\), because inserting \(u(\mathbf C)=\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\) into the first factor of (SDU.10) gives (SDU.8). Duality of continuous functors is the assertion here; an adjunction to \(u\) is a different assertion.

Its coevaluation object, under the actual exterior equivalence (SUL.21), is \[ \begin{gathered} K_{\mathrm{coev}}=\delta_{\mathcal A}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}),\\ K_{\mathrm{coev}}\simeq(\mathsf L_{\mathrm r}\otimes\mathsf L_{\mathrm r})(R_{\mathcal R}) \simeq\Delta_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r}}. \end{gathered} \tag{SDU.12} \] The last expression is read in \(\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm r}^2)\), the first two in \(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\); the intervening exterior equivalence is understood. To prove this identification and both triangles, test compact external objects.
