Every finite cohomology piece has the same isolated characteristic test, and continuity carries the bounded computation to the displayed sum. Its odd cohomology vanishes and each even cohomology has dimension \(a-1\). The maps of ICR.5 are the actual point adjunction maps. The ambient nonzero normal component \(dt\) does not alter the degenerate tangential germ \(s^a\).

3.516. Separated powers and both infinite tails

Exercise 3.GO. On \(\mathbf A^r\), \(r\geq1\), let \(a_i\geq2\), \(h=\sum_{i=1}^r z_i^{a_i}\), and take a constant rank-\(q\) connection, \(q\geq1\). Compute the rank and degree of the normalized cycle at zero, and its point retract for the sum of all even shifts. Use an isolated perturbation rather than a tensor-product theorem for Milnor fibres.

Solution 3.GO. The only critical point is zero. The gradient ideal and a basis for its local quotient are

\[ J_h=(a_1z_1^{a_1-1},\ldots,a_rz_r^{a_r-1}),\qquad z_1^{b_1}\cdots z_r^{b_r},\quad 0\leq b_i<a_i-1 . \tag{ICR.27} \]

For a generic small linear perturbation \(h-\sum\alpha_i z_i\), the independent equations \(a_i z_i^{a_i-1}=\alpha_i\) have exactly

\[ \mu=\prod_{i=1}^r(a_i-1) \tag{ICR.28} \]

solutions in the whole critical cluster. Every diagonal Hessian entry is nonzero at those solutions, including the entries with \(a_i=2\). The values can be made distinct by the parameter discriminant argument IH13. Thus ICR.9 has \(\mu\) quotients, each equal to the rank-\(q\) coefficient in degree zero, and

\[ (\Phi_h\mathbf C^q[r])_0\in D^{[0,0]}(\mathbf C), \qquad \dim H^0(\Phi_h\mathbf C^q[r])_0=q\mu . \tag{ICR.29} \]

The monomial basis in ICR.27 gives the same complete-intersection multiplicity. The filtration retains the actual restriction arrows and proves the degree assertion without a Thom–Sebastiani formula or a chosen splitting. If \(A=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^r}^{\oplus q}\) and \(E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A[2n]\), the characteristic set is the zero section and its intersection with \(\operatorname{graph}(dh)\) is isolated. Write \(V_h=(\Phi_h\mathbf C^q[r])_0\). Continuity and ICR.5 give

\[ \begin{gathered} i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E\simeq \bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}V_h[2n],\\ \dim H^{2m}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=q\mu,\quad H^{2m+1}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{ICR.30} \]

Each cohomology module of \(E\) is finite regular holonomic, so every required finite-subobject isolation condition follows from the zero-section bound. The resulting nonzero retract handles a zero source covector and arbitrarily degenerate powers while retaining both infinite cohomological tails.

3.517. Isolation in the actual characteristic set

Let \(M\) be a complex manifold, \(K\) any field, and \(P\) a finite-rank complex-constructible perverse \(K\)-sheaf near \(x\). Fix its original locally finite connected complex Whitney strata. Write \(\Sigma_P\) for its complex microsupport, using the real-part identification with real cotangents. Let \(h(x)=0\) and suppose, after shrinking,

\[ \operatorname{graph}(dh)\cap\Sigma_P\subset\{p\}, \qquad p=(x,dh_x). \tag{CIS.1} \]

Then the normalized supported test

\[ M_h(P)_x=(R\Gamma_{\{\operatorname{Re}h\geq0\}}P)_x \simeq(\Phi_hP)_x \tag{CIS.2} \]

is in ordinary degree zero. It is nonzero if and only if \(p\in\Sigma_P\). Zero covectors, singular conormals and degenerate Hessians are allowed. There is no critical-point condition on invisible original strata.

Here and below \(\Phi_h\) means the fibre convention ICR.1. The critical-support supplement uses an unshifted cone; its supported object \(M_h\) is that cone shifted by \([-1]\), hence is precisely CIS.2. The actual coefficient map is ICR.2–ICR.3.

For an original visible stratum \(S\), retain its normal object and the local intersection integer

\[ \begin{gathered} \mu_S(P)=N_S(P)[-\dim_{\mathbf C}S],\\ n_S=I_p\bigl(C_S,\operatorname{graph}(dh)\bigr), \qquad C_S=\overline{T^*_SM}. \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.3} \]

If \(p\notin C_S\), put \(n_S=0\). Only visible labels enter this definition; their intersections are isolated by CIS.1. The proof below gives the integer equality

\[ \dim_K H^0M_h(P)_x =\sum_{S\ {\rm visible}}n_S\dim_K\mu_S(P). \tag{CIS.4} \]

Each nonempty local intersection contributes a positive integer. We prove this using the original boundary, pair and restriction maps. The scholarly antecedent is Massey, A Little Microlocal Morse Theory, version 2, §5.

3.518. A radial boundary controlled by visible conormals

Work in a coordinate ball \(B_R\) centered at \(x=0\), meeting finitely many original strata. For each visible \(S\) on which \(h\) is nonconstant, take the actual relative-conormal closure

\[ \begin{gathered} S^\circ=\{z\in S:h(z)\ne0,\ d(h|_S)_z\ne0\},\\ D_S=\overline{\{(z,\xi):z\in S^\circ, \xi|_{\ker d(h|_S)_z}=0\}},\qquad D_S^0=D_S\cap\pi^{-1}(h=0). \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.5} \]

The relative-conormal proof RC0–RC2 makes \(D_S^0\) closed analytic, complex conic and isotropic, including all its singular and zero pieces. Its mechanism is useful here. On the dense relative-conormal bundle the canonical form satisfies \(\alpha=\lambda\,d(h\pi)\), with a meromorphic multiplier. On a finite normalization, near a generic divisor of \(h\pi=0\), one has

\[ \nu^*(h\pi)=t^a,\qquad \nu^*\alpha=a\lambda t^{a-1}\,dt . \tag{CIS.6} \]

The form on the left is holomorphic, so it kills every tangent to that divisor even when \(\lambda\) has a pole. Finite generic tangent lifting and singular-piece pullback give isotropy on the entire zero fibre. This uses no normal-crossing assumption on \(h\).

For \(z\in h^{-1}(0)\), approximate a covector of \(C_S\) by conormals over the dense \(S^\circ\). Adding a fixed complex multiple of \(dh\) before taking the limit proves

\[ (\Sigma_P)_z+\mathbf C\,dh_z\subset(\Lambda_0)_z, \qquad \Lambda_0=\bigcup_{S\ {\rm visible},\,h|_S\ {\rm nonconstant}}D_S^0 \ \cup\ T_x^*M \tag{CIS.7} \]

where the last fibre is included only if the original point stratum \(\{x\}\) is visible. A visible positive-dimensional stratum on which \(h=0\) would give graph points away from \(x\), contradicting CIS.1. Nonzero constant strata do not approach \(x\). Thus these are all relevant cases. The cone \(\Lambda_0\) is closed isotropic with closed base in \(B_R\).

Put \(\rho=|z|^2\). The characteristic-values proof CV0–CV5 applies to

\[ \varphi=\frac{\rho}{R^2-\rho},\qquad d\varphi=\frac{R^2}{(R^2-\rho)^2}\,d\rho . \tag{CIS.8} \]

This exhaustion is proper on the actual closed base of \(\Lambda_0\). Its characteristic values are closed and locally finite, so an entire sufficiently small positive interval contains none. Positive conicity then gives, for every sufficiently small \(r>0\),

\[ J^{-1}(d\rho_z)\notin(\Lambda_0)_z \quad\text{if }|z|=r,\ h(z)=0 . \tag{CIS.9} \]

Here \(J\) is the real-part cotangent map. Over the closed support of \(P\), write \(u=\operatorname{Re}h\), \(v=\operatorname{Im}h\). On that zero-level sphere the three rows \(du,dv,d\rho\) are independent. Adjoining any unit covector of \(\operatorname{SS}(P)\) preserves independence: a relation with nonzero radial coefficient violates CIS.7–CIS.9; one with zero radial coefficient puts a nonzero complex multiple of \(dh\) in \(\Sigma_P\), violating CIS.1. A zero differential away from \(x\) is excluded because the zero covector belongs to microsupport over its closed base.

Compactness of the zero-level sphere and its unit microsupport covectors gives a positive uniform row margin. If the unit-covector set is empty, the three-row argument still applies; if the sphere misses the support, a whole value neighbourhood misses it. Consequently the margin extends to \(|h|\leq2\eta\) on that sphere and to sufficiently small \(C^1\) perturbations, for some \(\eta>0\). At the fixed sides \(v=\pm\eta\), graph exclusion and compactness give the corresponding value-row margin. These are the simultaneous boundary bounds RB0–RB3. No radius or boundary hypothesis on an invisible stratum has been introduced.

3.519. The original supported test as a relative compact band

Fix such a closed ball \(C\), take \(0<\epsilon<\eta\) sufficiently small, and put

\[ X=C\cap\{|v|\leq\eta\},\qquad B_\pm=X\cap\{u\leq\pm\epsilon\}. \tag{CIS.10} \]

Retain the ordinary closed restriction of \(P\) to \(X\), extended to the ambient manifold. Its proper height map is \(u\), since \(X\) is compact. Near the band, the signed closed-face estimate adds only the inward normal rays of the active faces: \(-d\rho\) at the radial face, \(-dv\) at \(v=\eta\), and \(+dv\) at \(v=-\eta\). CIS.9 and its uniform margin exclude cancellation with \(du\) on those faces and their corners. In the interior the only possible graph point is \(x\).

Apply the between-level and local-jump proof MO31–MO36 on this band. Proper base change and support localization identify the jump at height zero with the supported complex on the compact zero-height fibre. Every stalk except the one at \(x\) is zero by the preceding microsupport exclusions. Its sections are therefore that one stalk. The actual endpoint restrictions give

\[ \operatorname{Fib}\bigl(R\Gamma(B_+;P) \longrightarrow R\Gamma(B_-;P)\bigr) \simeq M_h(P)_x . \tag{CIS.11} \]

This is a relative band comparison. The cohomology below the band is retained and need not vanish. The point \(x\) is interior to all artificial faces, so its support test is the original one. The proof does not flow the coefficient sheaf along critical invisible strata or identify the full ball with a sublevel.

3.520. Proper parameter continuation of the pair map

Let \(\ell(z)=a\cdot z\), with \(a\) a sufficiently small constant complex covector, and \(h_s=h+s\ell\). Work on an open interval \(I=(-\tau,1+\tau)\), \(\tau>0\), choosing \(a\) small enough for the uniform margins throughout \(I\). Keep \(X\) and \(v=\operatorname{Im}h\) fixed, and set

\[ E^\pm=\{(z,s)\in X\times I: \operatorname{Re}h_s(z)\leq\pm\epsilon\}. \tag{CIS.12} \]

Take the ordinary closed restrictions of the pulled-back coefficient to these sets, extended into \(M\times I\). Their projection \(\pi_I\) is proper on support: over a compact time set the support is closed in \(C\) times that set. Away from a moving height face each coefficient is empty or the fixed product, whose covectors have zero time component by the exact submersion formula MO10.

Near a moving face, \(|h|\) is small. The face estimate is valid there with all fixed active faces and the additional inward ray \(-d_{z,s}(\operatorname{Re}h_s)\). A nonzero pure time covector would require cancellation of its spatial part against a microsupport covector and the active radial and side rows. The simultaneous margins exclude exactly those cancellations. Hence the proper-image estimate MO8 gives

\[ \begin{gathered} G^\pm=R\pi_{I,*}\bigl((\operatorname{pr}_M^{-1}P)_{E^\pm}\bigr),\\ \operatorname{SS}(G^\pm)\subset T_I^*I . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.13} \]

There is no estimate at an artificial time endpoint, because \(I\) is open. A possibly characteristic distant fixed face is also harmless: away from a moving face the sheaf is the fixed product. Only the neighbourhoods just described require the face estimate.

Whole-complex interval descent makes \(G^\pm\), their actual restriction morphism and its fibre constant derived objects on \(I\). Proper base change identifies their fibres with the section complexes of the two endpoint pairs. For the relative fibre \(G\), the resulting maps are

\[ G|_{s=0}\ \xleftarrow{\ \sim\ }\ R\Gamma(I;G)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ G|_{s=1}. \tag{CIS.14} \]

They form the endpoint square of the actual pair restrictions and are natural in \(P\). This is the compact-band continuation IV1–IV2. It transports the whole pair fibre, without identifying the original test with a perturbed stalk at \(x\).

3.521. The finite visible cluster and its integer counts

For a local irreducible branch \(\Lambda\) of a visible \(C_S\) through \(p\), consider

\[ H_\Lambda(z,\xi)=\xi-dh_z:\Lambda\longrightarrow\mathbf C^m, \qquad m=\dim_{\mathbf C}M . \tag{CIS.15} \]

CIS.1 makes its zero fibre isolated. A small compact cotangent cut makes this map proper over a small parameter ball. Its fibres are compact affine analytic sets, hence finite. The branch is pure of dimension \(m\); the finite image dimension theorem makes it dominate that ball. Remove the source singular, original-boundary, nongeneric-normal and rank-drop subsets. Their finite images are proper analytic subsets. Choose \(a\) arbitrarily small outside their finite union. Compactness excludes all other visible graph points: their covectors are \(dh_z+a\), so neither a distant base point nor an unbounded covector can escape the chosen traps.

The graph of \(d(h+\ell)\) now meets the actual visible conormals at finitely many smooth transverse points. Each is a Morse point on its original stratum with its allowed generic normal direction. The finite analytic and Thom-count proof IH10–IH14, IHA1–IHA3 applies separately to these isolated visible branches and gives

\[ n_S=\#\{\text{perturbed points on }S\} \in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},\qquad p\in C_S\Longrightarrow n_S>0 . \tag{CIS.16} \]

The original complex fundamental cycle and its Thom evaluation are retained throughout the compact perturbation; every transverse complex sign is \(+1\). No raw quotient-length formula for a singular conormal is required. The calculation does not apply an isolated-fibre theorem to an invisible conormal whose original zero fibre may be positive dimensional.

At a retained point \(z\) on a stratum \(S_z\), the real height \(\operatorname{Re}(h+\ell)\) has tangential index \(\dim_{\mathbf C}S_z\). The original normal/tangential comparison and its orientation data give

\[ Q_z(P)\simeq N_{S_z}(P)[-\dim_{\mathbf C}S_z] =\mu_{S_z}(P). \tag{CIS.17} \]

The paths and orientation lines belong to that actual comparison. The dimension calculation needs its isomorphism class, not a global trivialization of a normal local system.

3.522. Zero invisible jumps and the finite restriction filtration

Use the proper real height \(\operatorname{Re}(h+\ell)\) on the same \(X\). Its actual microsupport graph in the band is the finite set just constructed. An original invisible stratum can still have nonisolated critical loci. At every such point outside that finite graph intersection, the actual supported test is zero by the definition of microsupport. MO31 consequently identifies the actual between-level restrictions there.

List the distinct exceptional real heights in the band and choose regular cuts between them. Equal real critical values are grouped together. Write

\[ D_0\subset D_1\subset\cdots\subset D_N,\qquad F_r=\operatorname{Fib}\bigl(R\Gamma(D_N;P) \longrightarrow R\Gamma(D_{N-r};P)\bigr). \tag{CIS.18} \]

The first and last section complexes are identified with the perturbed lower and upper band endpoints by the actual regular restrictions. Proper support localization at an exceptional height gives the direct sum of its point tests: the supported sheaf on that compact level fibre has zero stalks everywhere else. Thus the fibre-of-composite triangles give

\[ \begin{gathered} F_0=0,\quad F_N\simeq M_h(P)_x,\\ F_{r-1}\longrightarrow F_r \longrightarrow\!\!\bigoplus_{z\ {\rm at\ level}\ N-r+1}\!\!Q_z(P) \xrightarrow{+1}. \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.19} \]

The endpoint comparison is CIS.14 followed by CIS.11. The normal-degree proof PD1–PD6 puts every quotient in degree zero. The long exact sequences are therefore

\[ \begin{gathered} F_r\in D^{[0,0]}(K),\\ 0\longrightarrow H^0F_{r-1}\longrightarrow H^0F_r \longrightarrow\!\!\bigoplus_{z\ {\rm at\ level}\ N-r+1}\!\! \mu_{S_z}(P)\longrightarrow0 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.20} \]

Taking integer dimensions and using CIS.16 proves CIS.4. By the visible-conormal formula NG19, \(p\in\Sigma_P\) lies in at least one visible \(C_S\), so one summand is strictly positive. If the graph intersection is empty, ICR.4 gives zero. The zero-dimensional case is the direct point calculation. This proves CIS.1–CIS.4 over every field, without an index trace or reduction of an integer modulo the characteristic.

There is also a bounded-complex version. Let \(F\) be bounded finite-rank complex constructible with the same graph isolation. The identity PD7 gives \(\operatorname{SS}({}^pH^jF)\subset\operatorname{SS}(F)\). The single supported functor \(T_h(F)=(R\Gamma_{\{\operatorname{Re}h\geq0\}}F)_x\) sends all these perverse cohomology objects to degree zero by the theorem. Applying it to the finite perverse truncation triangles gives actual ordinary truncation triangles, hence

\[ \begin{gathered} H^jT_h(F)\simeq T_h({}^pH^jF),\\ p\in\operatorname{SS}(F)\Longrightarrow T_h(F)\ne0 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.21} \]

The implication uses PD7 to choose one perverse cohomology with a visible conormal through \(p\). No splitting of \(F\) into its perverse cohomology was assumed.

3.523. Full unbounded regular cycles detect a finite characteristic witness

Let \(U\) be smooth affine over \(\mathbf C\), \(E\in\mathscr R_\infty(U)\), \(h\in\mathcal O(U)\), \(h(x)=0\), and assume componentwise characteristic isolation CIC.1. Put \(B=\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E\). Equations ICR.5–ICR.6 already supply the actual comparison and maps

\[ \begin{gathered} \theta_B:i^!B\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*B,\\ i_*V\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{r}i_*V,\qquad V=i^!B,\quad ru=1 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.22} \]

Suppose some finite \(A_0\subset H^{m_0}E\) has \(p\in\operatorname{Char}(A_0)^{\mathrm{an}}\). Its perverse Riemann–Hilbert image has precisely that microsupport by AIC.8. The bounded result above makes its cycle coefficient \(V_{A_0}\) nonzero under the characteristic isolation alone. The exact regular cycle preserves the inclusion in the heart. Left exactness of \(H^0i^!\) and the actual finite-amplitude comparison give

\[ 0\ne V_{A_0}\hookrightarrow H^0i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}H^{m_0}E =H^{m_0}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E . \tag{CIS.23} \]

Thus CIS.22 is a nonzero retract with both infinite cohomological tails allowed. No common holonomic cone, common neighbourhood, transverse Hessian, smooth characteristic germ or isolated-critical condition on invisible strata is needed. Regular ind-membership and the componentwise characteristic isolation are still hypotheses.

For any specified exact functor \(T\), the same actual maps satisfy

\[ T(r)T(u)=1_{T(i_*V)}. \tag{CIS.24} \]

Nonvanishing after applying \(T\) requires \(T(i_*V)\ne0\). Sections 3.527–3.533 prove the actual proper-cycle comparison and nonzero point-image retract for the coefficient \(V\) and proper maps of complex smooth separated finite-type schemes on the full regular Ind category. The regular cycle functors and comparisons over a generic geometric field, the applicable stack presentations, global nilpotent regularity and the full supported-generation statements retain their separate requirements.

3.524. An invisible critical line that persists under perturbation

Exercise 3.GP. On \(M=\mathbf C^3\), use the two Whitney strata \(S\) and \(M\setminus S\), where

\[ \begin{gathered} S=\{(it,t,0):t\in\mathbf C\},\qquad P=K_M[3],\\ h=u^2+v^2+w^2,\quad h_\lambda=h-\lambda w . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.25} \]

Compute the actual characteristic test and the declared stratified critical locus. Show that for \(\lambda\ne0\) the invisible critical line persists, although the visible perturbation has only one point. Compute the original normalized cycle.

Solution 3.GP. The actual microsupport of \(P\) is the zero section. The original graph meets it only at the origin. The full perturbed differential gives

\[ \begin{gathered} dh_\lambda=(2u,2v,2w-\lambda),\\ z_\lambda=(0,0,\lambda/2),\qquad h_\lambda(z_\lambda)=-\lambda^2/4 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.26} \]

The Hessian is \(2I_3\), and \(z_\lambda\notin S\). The line \(S\) is invisible because the coefficient extends as a constant sheaf across it; its normal linear submersion has identical central and nearby coefficient, so its normal object is zero. Nevertheless

\[ h|_S=h_\lambda|_S=0,\qquad (\Phi_{h_\lambda}P)_z=0\quad(z\in S,\ \lambda\ne0). \tag{CIS.27} \]

For the second assertion \(dh_\lambda\ne0\) on \(S\), since its \(w\)-component is \(-\lambda\). A holomorphic submersion with constant coefficient has the invertible central-to-nearby unit in local product coordinates. Thus every point of \(S\) is a critical point of the declared restricted function, while none contributes an actual test.

The finite visible cluster has one point in the open stratum and one real tangential index \(3\). Its coefficient \(K[3]\) becomes \(K\) in degree zero. CIS.19 therefore gives

\[ (\Phi_hK_M[3])_0\simeq K,\qquad F_0=0,\quad F_1\simeq K \quad\text{in degree zero}. \tag{CIS.28} \]

This agrees with ICR.29 for three squares, but retains the specified two-stratum partition throughout. The lower band cohomology has not been declared zero; \(F_0\) is the zero relative fibre.

The numerical perturbation in Figure 3.65 has explicit admissible bands. Take \(C=\{|z|\leq1\}\), \(\epsilon=1/64\), \(\eta=1/16\), \(I=(-1,2)\), and \(h_s=h-sw/8\). Write \(c=s/8\) and \(V=\operatorname{Im}h\), so \(|c|<1/4\). On a moving height face one has \(|h|\leq21/64\). On the radial sphere, a relation \(d\rho=A\,d\operatorname{Re}h_s+B\,dV\) would have \(\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\leq8/7\): the norm of the right side is at least \((2-|c|)\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\), while \(|d\rho|=2\). Pair its complex-covector identity with \(z\). The resulting inequality is \(2\leq(8/7)(2\cdot21/64+1/4)=29/28\), a contradiction. A dependence of the two value rows forces the complex coordinates \(u=v=0\) and \(w=c/[2(1+iB)]\) for a real \(B\); then \(|V|<1/64\), so it misses the side faces \(|V|=1/16\). The only interior real-height critical point is \(z=(0,0,c/2)\), with value \(-c^2/4>-1/64\). Thus neither moving endpoint is critical, and every required face exclusion holds on the open interval \(I\). This verifies the chosen finite perturbation and its actual endpoint square.

Figure 3.65. For \(\lambda=1/8\), the left panel is the real coordinate section \((u,v,w)=(ib,b,c)\), \(b,c\in\mathbf R\). The horizontal line is the section of the invisible complex line; the marked point is the full ambient critical point \((0,0,1/16)\). Critical points of a restricted drawing plane are not being identified with ambient critical points. The middle panel is the actual cotangent section \(u=v=0\), \(w\in\mathbf R\), \(\xi_u=\xi_v=0\), \(\xi_w\in\mathbf R\): the zero section meets \(\xi_w=2w-1/8\) at \(w=1/16\). The lower panel gives the compact-pair continuation and the single relative jump. Proofs: CIS.12–CIS.20 and CIS.25–CIS.28.

3.525. Two conormal branches at a zero covector

Exercise 3.GQ. In \(U=\mathbf A^2_{u,v}\), let \(j_u\) and \(j_v\) be the closed inclusions of its two coordinate axes. For \(r,s\geq1\), take

\[ \begin{gathered} A=(j_u)_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}^{\oplus r} \oplus(j_v)_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}^{\oplus s}, \\ h=u^a+v^b,\quad a,b\geq2 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.29} \]

Compute the normalized cycle at the singular meeting point of its characteristic components, and the point coefficient for \(\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A[2n]\).

Solution 3.GQ. In cotangent coordinates \((\alpha,\beta)\), the characteristic set is the union \(\{v=0,\alpha=0\}\cup\{u=0,\beta=0\}\). The graph of \(dh\) meets it only at \(p=(0,0;0,0)\). On the two smooth conormal branches the local gradient quotients are respectively \(\mathbf C\{u\}/(u^{a-1})\) and \(\mathbf C\{v\}/(v^{b-1})\). Thus

\[ n_u=a-1,\quad n_v=b-1,\qquad \dim V_A=r(a-1)+s(b-1). \tag{CIS.30} \]

The point stratum is invisible: a generic linear test restricts to submersions on both axes, and its two normal objects are zero. Closed-transfer support sections reduce the two actual tests to \(u^a\) and \(v^b\). The covered-fibre diagonal calculation ICR.18 identifies, with its cyclic monodromies,

\[ \begin{aligned} V_A={}& \bigl(\mathbf C^r\otimes(\mathbf C^a/\mathbf C_{\rm diag})\bigr)\\ &\oplus \bigl(\mathbf C^s\otimes(\mathbf C^b/\mathbf C_{\rm diag})\bigr) \quad\text{in degree zero}. \end{aligned} \tag{CIS.31} \]

The ambient characteristic germ is singular at \(p\). Each local branch count has nevertheless been taken separately, with positive sign, and the invisible point contributes nothing. Every finite cohomology piece of \(E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A[2n]\) has the same isolated characteristic bound. Continuity of the actual regular cycles and both point adjoints gives

\[ \begin{gathered} i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E\simeq \bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}V_A[2n],\\ \dim H^{2m}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=r(a-1)+s(b-1),\\ H^{2m+1}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.32} \]

The maps are those of CIS.22; the calculation retains both infinite tails.

3.526. A degenerate visible point beside a nonisolated invisible locus

Exercise 3.GR. Keep the line \(S\) from CIS.25 and \(P=K_{\mathbf C^3}[3]\), but let \(a\geq3\) and

\[ h=u^2+v^2+w^a,\qquad h_\lambda=h-\lambda w,\quad \lambda\ne0 . \tag{CIS.33} \]

Compute the complete visible cluster, its normalized cycle rank, and the full even-shift point coefficient over \(\mathbf C\).

Solution 3.GR. The actual microsupport is again the zero section and its original graph intersection is just the origin, with degenerate Hessian. Let \(w_j\) range over all roots of \(a w^{a-1}=\lambda\). There are \(a-1\) distinct nonzero roots. The full critical equations, values and Hessians are

\[ \begin{gathered} z_j=(0,0,w_j),\qquad h_\lambda(z_j)=-\frac{a-1}{a}\lambda w_j,\\ \operatorname{Hess}_{z_j}h_\lambda =\operatorname{diag}(2,2,a(a-1)w_j^{a-2}) . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.34} \]

All points lie outside \(S\), all are Morse, and all converge to zero as \(\lambda\to0\). Their values are distinct. On \(S\) the perturbed function is still identically zero, while its ambient \(w\)-derivative is \(-\lambda\); hence the entire invisible critical line has zero actual tests, as in CIS.27.

The original zero-section intersection ideal is \((2u,2v,aw^{a-1})\), with quotient basis \(1,w,\ldots,w^{a-2}\). The visible cluster has \(a-1\) degree-zero quotients \(K\). The actual compact-band filtration gives

\[ V_h=(\Phi_hK_{\mathbf C^3}[3])_0\in D^{[0,0]}(K), \qquad \dim_KV_h=a-1 . \tag{CIS.35} \]

Equal real critical heights, if any, are grouped as finite direct sums; no choice of real ordering changes the integer dimension. A chosen global basis or trivial monodromy is not inferred from this filtration.

Over \(\mathbf C\), let \(E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^3}[2n]\). Each cohomology is regular with zero characteristic section, so componentwise isolation holds. The actual continuous ind-cycle and CIS.22 yield

\[ \begin{gathered} i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E\simeq \bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}V_h[2n],\\ \dim H^{2m}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=a-1,\qquad H^{2m+1}i^!\Phi_h^{\mathrm{reg}}E=0 . \end{gathered} \tag{CIS.36} \]

This nonzero retract uses actual characteristic isolation while the declared invisible critical locus remains positive dimensional. Its coefficient agrees with ICR.29 for exponents \(2,2,a\), without changing the original strata or substituting a single perturbed stalk for the original test.

3.527. Ambient regular cycles and proper algebraic maps

Let \(f:X\to Y\) be a proper morphism of smooth separated finite-type complex varieties. Work componentwise if their dimensions differ. Let \(g:Y\to\mathbf A^1\) be regular, put \(h=gf\), and write \(i_X:X_0=h^{-1}(0)\hookrightarrow X\) and \(i_Y:Y_0=g^{-1}(0)\hookrightarrow Y\). The zero fibres may be singular. Put \[ \mathscr R_0(X)=D^b_{\mathrm{rh}}(\mathcal D_X),\qquad \mathscr R_\infty(X)=\operatorname{Ind}\mathscr R_0(X),\qquad j_X:\mathscr R_\infty(X)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{qc}}(\mathcal D_X). \tag{PIC.1} \] Here the bounded category has its full derived mapping complexes, and \(j_X\) extends the actual inclusion. The same notation applies to \(Y\). Denote the normalized cycle followed by closed extension into its smooth ambient variety by \(C_h^X\). On bounded inputs its specified comparison is \[ \rho_{h,A}:\operatorname{DR}_X C_{h,0}^X A \xrightarrow{\sim}i_{X,*}\Phi_h\operatorname{DR}_X A, \qquad C_h^X=\operatorname{Ind}(C_{h,0}^X). \tag{PIC.2} \] This is the construction IAC.26, using bounded regular Riemann–Hilbert and closed support. It assigns no smooth differential-operator sheaf to a singular zero fibre. The bounded algebraic cycle theorem, its exact normalization and the closed-support comparisons were proved in §3.297 and its linked programme lessons.

The proper bounded direct image preserves \(\mathscr R_0\) by the algebraic four-map theorem, Theorem 5.17. Thus the following exact functor exists: \[ f_+^{\mathrm{reg}}=\operatorname{Ind}(f_{+,0}): \mathscr R_\infty(X)\longrightarrow\mathscr R_\infty(Y). \tag{PIC.3} \] We identify it with the actual ambient pushforward and construct its cycle comparison. Regular ind-membership remains an input. Neither an arbitrary geometric ground field nor a general algebraic stack is included in the statement.

3.528. A finite model for actual unbounded direct image

Use right modules temporarily. The forward transfer and its chain-rule action are \[ T_f=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal D_Y,\qquad f_+^r M=Rf_{\mathrm{sh},*} (M\otimes_{\mathcal D_X}^{L}T_f). \tag{PIC.4} \] PBW makes \(T_f\) locally free over \(\mathcal O_X\). The absolute transfer Spencer proof, Lemma 3.3, resolves it by \[ S_f^{-r}=\mathcal D_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X} \bigwedge^rT_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}T_f, \qquad 0\le r\le d_X. \tag{PIC.5} \] Its differential has the ordered operator-action, coefficient-action and bracket terms. Its square is zero by the representation and Jacobi identities; the symbol complex is the polynomial Koszul resolution. These prove its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Each term is left \(\mathcal D_X\)-flat because its tensor functor is tensor over \(\mathcal O_X\) with an \(\mathcal O_X\)-flat module. The differential and augmentation retain the right \(f^{-1}\mathcal D_Y\)-action. Consequently this bounded flat complex computes the transfer tensor of every unbounded \(M\). No bounded resolution of \(M\) is required.

Fix an affine open \(V\subset Y\). Cover \(f^{-1}V\) by \(c+1\) affine opens \(U_0,\ldots,U_c\). Separatedness makes their intersections affine. For a representative complex of quasicoherent right modules the actual local model is \[ \operatorname{Tot}\left[ \bigoplus_{i_0<\cdots<i_q} \Gamma\!\left(U_{i_0\cdots i_q}, M^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal D_X}S_f^{-r}\right) \right]_{0\le q\le c,\;0\le r\le d_X}. \tag{PIC.6} \] The total degree is the coefficient degree plus \(q-r\), with the Koszul signs. Each coefficient term is quasicoherent over \(\mathcal O_X\); the Spencer differential need not be \(\mathcal O_X\)-linear. It commutes with restriction and with the target right action, which is what the displayed complex needs.

Here is why this computes derived pushforward for both infinite tails. The augmented ordered Čech resolution is exact on stalks, by the contracting simplex of cover members containing that stalk. Its nonaugmented terms are direct images from affine intersections. Their sections are acyclic for a quasicoherent coefficient, by the earlier affine cohomology proof. This resolution has length \(c\). Dimension shifting along it gives cohomological dimension at most \(c\) on these coefficients. Resolving the coefficients for sheaf direct image and comparing the two augmented double complexes therefore gives the Čech comparison. Both auxiliary directions have bounded length. In every fixed total degree a finite band of coefficient degrees occurs; truncating beyond that band gives the bounded comparison, and enlarging the band does not change it. This proves the comparison for the unbounded complex, without a product totalization or an interchange of two infinite limits.

The model sends an acyclic coefficient complex to an acyclic complex: tensor in (PIC.5), affine sections and finite sums are exact, and the two finite filtrations detect acyclicity. It is thus independent of the representative. Refinement of the affine cover preserves its augmentation, so these local models glue to (PIC.4). On a fixed \(V\) they also prove \[ f_+^r(D^{[a,b]})\subset D^{[a-d_X,b+c]},\qquad f_+^r\!\left(\bigoplus_\alpha M_\alpha\right) \simeq\bigoplus_\alpha f_+^rM_\alpha. \tag{PIC.7} \] The sum identity follows term by term: flat tensor and affine quasicoherent sections commute with direct sums. Exactness and preservation of sums give preservation of all colimits in the stable derived categories. Side change by \(\omega_X\) and \(\omega_Y^{-1}\) is exact and continuous, so the same continuity holds for the actual left-module \(f_+\). Properness was not used in this continuity argument; it is used for the bounded regular target and for cycle comparison.

3.529. The scheme embedding and its comparison map

The affine perfectness proof IAC.1–IAC.5 extends to a finite separated scheme cover as follows. A bounded coherent operator complex restricts to a finite projective operator complex on every affine intersection. For a bounded regular \(A\), the mapping complex on \(X\) is the finite ordered Čech totalization of the local derived mapping complexes \[ R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_X}(A,M) \simeq \operatorname{Tot}_{q=0}^{c} \bigoplus_{i_0<\cdots<i_q} R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D(U_{i_0\cdots i_q})} (A|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_q}},M|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_q}}). \tag{PIC.8} \] To verify descent here, resolve the source locally by its finite projective complexes and resolve the target for sheaf Hom. The finite ordered cover resolves the resulting sheaf Hom complex; its affine pieces are computed by those projectives. The comparisons are the restriction maps of derived Hom and hence agree on refinements. The same finite-band argument as in (PIC.6) handles an unbounded target. Finitely many intersections give a finite maximum source resolution length. Each local mapping functor commutes with filtered colimits, and those colimits commute with the finite totalization. Hence \(A\) is compact in the actual ambient category.

For filtered presentations the ambient mapping complexes are therefore \[ R\operatorname{Hom}\left(j_X\operatorname*{colim}_i A_i, j_X\operatorname*{colim}_k B_k\right) \simeq \lim_i\operatorname*{colim}_k R\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_k). \tag{PIC.9} \] This is the defining Ind mapping formula, so \(j_X\) is fully faithful. This proof uses a finite affine scheme cover. It supplies no compactness assertion for bounded objects on \(B\mathbb G_m\) or an arbitrary stack.

The two continuous functors out of \(\mathscr R_\infty(X)\) that restrict to \(f_{+,0}\) now have their specified comparison \[ \gamma_f:j_Y f_+^{\mathrm{reg}} \xrightarrow{\sim}f_+j_X. \tag{PIC.10} \] For \(E=\operatorname*{colim}_i A_i\), it is the colimit of the identical bounded comparisons \(j_Yf_{+,0}A_i=f_+A_i\). This proves invertibility. Naturality and independence of the presentation follow from the Ind universal property on exact functors and their mapping spaces. Thus (PIC.10) compares the actual module functor, including its action and higher maps.

3.530. The actual bounded proper comparison on coefficients

For bounded constructible complex coefficients, Proper pushforwards of nearby and vanishing cycles, equations (2)–(10), proves the normalized comparison. Its mechanism is useful here. For an ambient covering coefficient \(B\) one has \[ Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(f^{-1}B,F) \simeq R\mathcal Hom(B,Rf_*F). \tag{PIC.11} \] Indeed testing against \(E\), inverse/direct adjunction followed by tensor–Hom adjunction gives the same Hom from \(f^{-1}(E\otimes^L B)\) to \(F\) on both sides. Yoneda gives (PIC.11), naturally in both variables and under restriction.

If \(F\) is carried by a closed set proper over the target, the same is true after this internal Hom: its restriction off that carrier has zero second argument. Thus forgetting proper support is an isomorphism before and after zero-fibre restriction. Proper-support base change, followed by that support-forgetting map, is the actual ordinary comparison \[ i_Y^{-1}Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(f^{-1}B,F) \xrightarrow{\sim} Rf_{0,*}i_X^{-1}R\mathcal Hom(f^{-1}B,F). \tag{PIC.12} \] The support-forgetting square commutes because both arrows restrict the same properly supported section. Applying the covering coefficient, its cone coefficient and the constant coefficients gives nearby cycles, normalized vanishing cycles and the two restriction terms. The earlier covering cohomological bound puts these particular Hom objects in the bounded category even though the covering coefficient has infinite rank.

After closed extension into the ambient varieties, the resulting map is \[ b_{f,g,F}: i_{Y,*}\Phi_g Rf_*F \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*i_{X,*}\Phi_hF. \tag{PIC.13} \] The identity \(i_Yf_0=fi_X\) supplies the target's type. Neither zero fibre must be smooth. Naturality in every covering-coefficient map proves the comparison commutes with the central restriction map, canonical map, variation and deck monodromy. In the nearby and vanishing terms this includes \[ \mathrm{var}\,\mathrm{can}=1-M_\psi,\qquad \mathrm{can}\,\mathrm{var}=1-M_\Phi. \tag{PIC.14} \] Both normalized triangles use the same source shift; no dimension shift is added by (PIC.13). The sheaf proper comparison is also stated in Massey, Notes on Perverse Sheaves and Vanishing Cycles, §3. The coefficient and support argument above identifies the maps used here.

3.531. A specified bounded D-module transformation

The earlier proper de Rham theorem, Theorem 3.3, supplies \[ \kappa_{f,A}:\operatorname{DR}_Y f_{+,0}A \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\operatorname{DR}_X A. \tag{PIC.15} \] Its proof applies to every bounded coherent operator complex. Proper-support comparison on all quasicoherent Spencer coefficients retains the horizontal operator action. The closed graph normal Koszul complex cancels its normal determinant and normal degree; horizontal and vertical Spencer totalization has shift \(d_X+d_Y\). These are the actual coefficient and density maps of that proof.

For \(A\in\mathscr R_0(X)\), all the terms in the following composite are defined and all arrows are equivalences: \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{DR}_Y C_{g,0}^Y f_{+,0}A &\xrightarrow{\rho_g} i_{Y,*}\Phi_g\operatorname{DR}_Y f_{+,0}A\\ &\xrightarrow{\Phi_g\kappa_{f,A}} i_{Y,*}\Phi_g Rf_*\operatorname{DR}_X A\\ &\xrightarrow{b_{f,g,\operatorname{DR}A}} Rf_*i_{X,*}\Phi_h\operatorname{DR}_X A\\ &\xrightarrow{Rf_*\rho_{h,A}^{-1}} Rf_*\operatorname{DR}_X C_{h,0}^X A\\ &\xrightarrow{\kappa_{f,C_{h,0}^XA}^{-1}} \operatorname{DR}_Y f_{+,0}C_{h,0}^X A . \end{aligned} \tag{PIC.16} \] In the second arrow the closed extension \(i_{Y,*}\) is understood. Full faithfulness of bounded regular Riemann–Hilbert lifts this specified natural composite to \[ \beta_{f,g,0}:C_{g,0}^Y f_{+,0} \xrightarrow{\sim}f_{+,0}C_{h,0}^X. \tag{PIC.17} \] Full faithfulness here is on mapping complexes. Equivalently, conjugation by the bounded equivalence identifies the two functor categories and their natural-transformation spaces. Thus the lift retains naturality and its higher coherences.

The nearby analogue uses the same five arrows. The ordinary and exceptional restriction analogues use the constant coefficient arrows in (PIC.12). Their diagrams with (PIC.17) commute: (PIC.13) is natural in these coefficient arrows; \(\rho\) transports these very arrows by definition; and \(\kappa\) is natural in its input. Consequently the actual unit, canonical, variation and monodromy squares, and both identities (PIC.14), hold on the D-module side.

For composable proper maps \(X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow kZ\), these comparisons satisfy \[ \beta_{kf,g,0} =(k_+\beta_{f,gk,0})\circ(\beta_{k,g,0}f_+), \tag{PIC.18} \] where the standard direct-image associators are included. Here is a map-level check. The sheaf coefficient adjunction for \(kf\) is the composite of the two adjunctions: both send a test morphism to its same tensor–Hom adjoint. The proper-support base-change squares compose by restriction of the same sections. For \(\kappa\), resolve successive transfers and totalize their Spencer complexes in the order \(X,Y,Z\). Both parenthesizations send an elementary ordered wedge to the same total wedge, with the same permutation sign; the intermediate density and its inverse contract. The comparison from algebraic to analytic coefficient germs and proper direct image commutes with these augmentations. Hence the two maps from the common resolved complex agree. The normal graph contractions retain their ordered evaluation, so there is no freely chosen scalar at a closed point. These checks prove composition compatibility of \(\kappa\), and hence (PIC.18) after (PIC.16). A third map uses the same associative tensor totalization, giving the higher composition coherence.

3.532. Ind extension and actual point images

An exact natural equivalence between functors on small stable categories extends to a continuous equivalence on their Ind categories: on every filtered presentation it is the colimit of its bounded equivalences. The universal property gives its naturality, composition and all specified commutative diagrams. Applying this to (PIC.17) yields \[ \beta_{f,g}:C_g^Y f_+^{\mathrm{reg}} \xrightarrow{\sim}f_+^{\mathrm{reg}}C_h^X \quad\text{on all }\mathscr R_\infty(X). \tag{PIC.19} \] There is no cohomological bound on the input. The nearby, restriction and coefficient maps extend at the same time, so (PIC.14) and (PIC.18) continue to hold. By (PIC.10), the direct images in this equation are actual ambient D-module direct images. The cycle functors have the regular Ind meaning (PIC.2); no assertion about cycles of all unbounded classical sheaves is required.

Let \(x\in X(\mathbf C)\), \(y=f(x)\), and let \(a_x,a_y\) denote the point inclusions. Transfer composition gives the bounded comparison, and then its continuous extension, \[ f_+^{\mathrm{reg}}(a_{x,+}V)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{y,+}V, \qquad V\in D(\mathbf C). \tag{PIC.20} \] For the bounded comparison one can use forward transfers on right modules: the chain-rule tensor identifies the two transfers with \(T_{a_y}\); the coefficient is carried by one point, so sheaf pushforward is exact there. Side change cancels the intermediate density. This is the point case of the ordered transfer associativity used in (PIC.18). Finite point complexes generate \(D(\mathbf C)\) by filtered colimits, and all three functors are continuous, proving (PIC.20) for every \(V\).

The point functor is fully faithful on this entire category. The affine Koszul calculation gives \[ a_y^!a_{y,+}V\simeq V,\qquad V\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ a_{y,+}V\ne0. \tag{PIC.21} \] It extends from finite complexes by its continuous finite-amplitude right adjoint, as in IAC.16–IAC.18. A neighbourhood of \(y\) suffices for this calculation, and closed extension makes it global. In particular no fibre-length multiplier occurs in (PIC.20), even for a ramified finite map.

If \(u:a_{x,+}V\to B\) and \(r:B\to a_{x,+}V\) satisfy \(ru=1\), the actual maps \[ a_{y,+}V\xrightarrow{\,f_+u\,}f_+B \xrightarrow{\,f_+r\,}a_{y,+}V \quad\text{have composite }1. \tag{PIC.22} \] The point-composition comparisons in (PIC.20) are included in these arrows. Thus the point image of a nonzero coefficient survives proper direct image.

3.533. Nonzero characteristic-isolated cycles after proper image

Suppose \(E\in\mathscr R_\infty(X)\) and \(C_h^XE\) has the point retract \[ a_{x,+}V\xrightarrow{u}C_h^XE \xrightarrow{r}a_{x,+}V,\qquad ru=1,\qquad V\ne0. \tag{PIC.23} \] A sufficient case is the affine characteristic-isolation theorem CIS.22–CIS.23: for every finite coherent submodule of every \(H^mE\), the graph of \(dh\) meets its actual characteristic set only at \((x,dh_x)\) on its own neighbourhood, and one such submodule contains that covector in its actual characteristic set. Zero covectors, singular conormal branches, degenerate tests, different neighbourhoods and both infinite tails are allowed. On a general \(X\), (PIC.23) is the stated premise; a local test must provide its actual global retract before this conclusion is applied.

Combining (PIC.19), (PIC.20) and the given unit/counit retract gives the specified maps \[ \begin{aligned} U&=\beta_{f,g,E}^{-1}\,f_+u: a_{y,+}V\longrightarrow C_g^Y f_+E,\\ R&=f_+r\,\beta_{f,g,E}: C_g^Y f_+E\longrightarrow a_{y,+}V,\\ RU&=1 . \end{aligned} \tag{PIC.24} \] All functors and coefficients in this formula are the full unbounded ones. The identity follows by cancelling the actual inverse comparisons and then using \(ru=1\). Equation (PIC.21) proves \[ C_g^Y f_+E\ne0. \tag{PIC.25} \] The target point need not be the only target cycle component. The conclusion is its actual nonzero retract. This theorem proves the proper comparison and point-image step over \(\mathbf C\) for the stated scheme and regular Ind inputs. Sections 3.537–3.543 construct the product-section retract for universal quadratic parameters and prove original-complex proper detection with componentwise isolation of the selected compatible point. Regular cycle categories over other geometric fields, general relative sections, independent nilpotent regularity and the full supported-generation/projector-image equalities retain their additional requirements.

3.534. Exercise and solution: a ramified tower and both tails

Exercise 3.GS. For positive integers \(a,b\ge2\), take \(f_a(z)=z^a\), \(f_b(t)=t^b\), and coordinate \(s\) on the final affine line. Compute the normalized \(s\)-cycles of their composite pushforward on a rank-\(r\) trivial connection, including monodromy and an input unbounded in both directions.

Solution 3.GS. The composite is \(q(z)=z^{ab}\). The covered fibre has \(ab\) points. The central comparison is the diagonal, so the actual normalized cycle coefficient is \[ V_{ab,r}=\mathbf C^r\otimes \left(\mathbf C^{ab}/\mathbf C_{\mathrm{diag}}\right), \qquad \dim V_{ab,r}=r(ab-1). \tag{PIC.26} \] This is the actual diagonal calculation ICR.18, including the perverse input \(\mathbf C[1]\). One positive circuit of \(s\) cyclically permutes the \(ab\) roots; its quotient action is the cycle monodromy. Proper comparison and point composition give \[ C_s(f_b)_+(f_a)_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}^{\,r} \simeq a_{0,+}V_{ab,r}. \tag{PIC.27} \] Both stages are finite and proper. Equation (PIC.18) identifies this map with the comparison for \(q\), including the cyclic action. At the intermediate stage the relevant function is \(t^b\) on the actual module \((f_a)_+\mathcal O^r\); replacing that module by a constant connection would discard its ramification. Consequently the rank is not obtained by multiplying the two separate constant-input cycle ranks.

For the input with both tails, continuity gives \[ E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}^{\,r}[2n], \qquad C_s q_+E\simeq a_{0,+}\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}V_{ab,r}[2n]. \tag{PIC.28} \] Every even coefficient cohomology has dimension \(r(ab-1)\), and every odd one is zero. This is an actual coproduct in the regular Ind category. Point composition has coefficient one; the cycle rank \(ab-1\) arose from the covered-fibre diagonal.

Figure 3.66. The upper square is the actual comparison PIC.19, with the source point coefficient and its target image joined by PIC.20. Both vertical retract composites are identities, by PIC.24. The lower diagram specializes to \(z\mapsto z^2\mapsto z^6\): the six-root permutation representation modulo its diagonal has dimension five, whereas a single point image retains its coefficient with multiplicity one. The drawing represents maps of complexes and a finite covering fibre. It does not identify that fibre's length with a point-image coefficient. Proofs: PIC.16–PIC.28.

3.535. Exercise and solution: a proper map with two output degrees

Exercise 3.GT. Let \(\pi:\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^1_t\to\mathbf A^1_t\), \(g=t^a\), \(a\ge2\). Compute \(\pi_+\mathcal O\) and its normalized \(g\)-cycles. Explain why the comparison needs no t-exactness of \(\pi_+\).

Solution 3.GT. The algebraic de Rham cohomology of \(\mathbf P^1\) is computed by its two affine charts. Their function Čech quotient vanishes because every Laurent polynomial is a sum of a polynomial in \(z\) and a polynomial in \(z^{-1}\). Global one-forms vanish. In the one-form Čech quotient the allowed chart forms have exponents at least zero or at most minus two; exactly the class \(dz/z\) remains. Derivatives of Laurent polynomials have zero \(z^{-1}\) coefficient. Constants give the remaining degree-zero class. Hence \[ R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1,\Omega_{\mathbf P^1}^{\bullet}) \simeq \mathbf C\oplus\mathbf C[-2]. \tag{PIC.29} \] The actual maps are the constant section and the Čech cocycle \(dz/z\); they give the displayed equivalence by the computation just made. The relative de Rham direct image has the normalization shift \([1]\). Its target connection is constant because these representatives are independent of \(t\). Therefore \[ \pi_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^1} \simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}[1]\oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}[-1]. \tag{PIC.30} \] Put \(V_a=\mathbf C^a/\mathbf C_{\mathrm{diag}}\), with its cyclic monodromy. Exactness of normalized cycles on the bounded regular category and (PIC.30) give \[ C_{t^a}\pi_+\mathcal O \simeq a_{0,+}(V_a[1]\oplus V_a[-1]). \tag{PIC.31} \] One can also start upstairs. For the closed inclusion \(j:\mathbf P^1\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^1\), the product covering and its diagonal identify \[ C_{t^a}^{\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf A^1}\mathcal O \simeq j_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}\otimes V_a,\qquad \pi_+j_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1} \simeq a_{0,+}(\mathbf C[1]\oplus\mathbf C[-1]). \tag{PIC.32} \] Indeed the product coefficient is \(\mathbf C_{\mathbf P^1}[1]\) tensored with the same diagonal quotient; (PIC.29) computes its proper image. These maps are those of (PIC.16). The source cycle is supported on the entire curve, so a point-isolation premise has not been used. The two output degrees show directly why proper direct image was not assumed t-exact. Replacing the input by its coproduct of shifts \([4n]\), \(n\in\mathbf Z\), gives both infinite tails by (PIC.19) and continuity, with the same two shifted coefficient summands for each \(n\).

3.536. Exercise and solution: the necessary properness hypothesis

Exercise 3.GU. Let \(j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_t\), and use \(g=t\). Compare cycles before and after direct image of the trivial connection.

Solution 3.GU. The source function has empty zero fibre, so \[ C_{t|_{\mathbf G_m}}\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_m}=0,\qquad j_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_m} =\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}(*0). \tag{PIC.33} \] On the target take \(P=\operatorname{DR}(\mathcal O(*0))\). Its stalk is the meromorphic de Rham complex, shifted by \([1]\). The kernel of differentiation is the constants, and its cokernel is generated by \(dt/t\): termwise Laurent integration removes every other term and preserves convergence; only finitely many negative powers occur. On the punctured disc this complex is \(\mathbf C[1]\) by the local primitive. The central map sends the constant to the same constant on the covered fibre. Thus the actual central restriction and nearby map are \[ i_0^*P\simeq\mathbf C[1]\oplus\mathbf C,\qquad \psi_tP\simeq\mathbf C[1],\qquad i_0^*P\longrightarrow\psi_tP \text{ induces the identity in degree }-1. \tag{PIC.34} \] The other component maps to zero: there is no degree-zero cohomology in the target, and finite vector complexes have no higher extensions. The normalized vanishing cycle is the fibre of this central map. It is therefore \(\mathbf C\) in degree zero. By bounded regular Riemann–Hilbert, \[ C_t j_+\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_m}\simeq a_{0,+}\mathbf C\ne0, \qquad j_+C_{t|_{\mathbf G_m}}\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_m}=0. \tag{PIC.35} \] This does not contradict the continuity calculation PIC.4–PIC.7, which did not require properness. The map \(j\) is not proper on the source support. Its missing limit point is precisely where the nonzero target cycle occurs. The proper-support base-change step (PIC.12) is unavailable.

The distinction also persists for arbitrary coefficients built by coproducts: \[ E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_{\mathbf G_m}[2n], \qquad C_t j_+E\simeq a_{0,+}\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathbf C[2n], \qquad j_+C_{t|_{\mathbf G_m}}E=0. \tag{PIC.36} \] All functors here have their regular Ind meaning and the actual ambient direct images. The example separates continuity, which holds, from proper cycle comparison, whose geometric hypothesis fails.

3.537. A universal quadratic test over the original complex field

Dimension estimates are componentwise on the smooth schemes. For the section calculation use the pure-dimensional component containing the chosen source point; the finitely many other open-and-closed components are direct summands.

Let \(f:X\to Y\) be proper, with \(X\) smooth separated of finite type over \(\mathbf C\) and \(Y\) smooth affine. Fix \(y\in Y(\mathbf C)\) and \(0\ne\eta\in T_y^*Y\). Choose a closed embedding \(\iota:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^N\), put \(v_i(z)=\iota_i(z)-\iota_i(y)\), and choose constants \(\xi_i\) such that \(\sum_i\xi_i\,dv_i|_y=\eta\). Such constants exist because a closed immersion surjects on cotangent spaces. On \(Q=\mathbf A^N_q\) define \[ \begin{gathered} g(q,z)=\sum_{i=1}^N\xi_i v_i(z) +\frac12\sum_{i=1}^Nq_i v_i(z)^2,\\ h=g\circ f_Q,\qquad f_Q=\mathrm{id}_Q\times f. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.1} \] The parameter derivatives give \[ \partial_{q_i}g=\frac12v_i^2,\qquad \bigl(d_Qg=0\bigr)\Longleftrightarrow z=y,\qquad g(q,y)=0,\quad d_Yg|_{(q,y)}=\eta. \tag{UQD.2} \] These are identities and equivalences of complex point sets. The equations \(v_i^2=0\) can retain nilpotents as scheme equations; no reducedness or tangent-space assertion follows from the middle equivalence.

The full differential of \(g\) never vanishes. Away from \(y\), one \(v_i\) is nonzero because \(\iota\) is a closed embedding, so one parameter derivative is nonzero. At \(y\), its \(Y\)-component is \(\eta\ne0\). Thus \[ g:Q\times Y\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1 \quad\text{is a submersion}. \tag{UQD.3} \] The source function \(h\) may have a positive-dimensional critical locus and zero differential along it. All coordinates and parameters above remain over \(\mathbf C\).

3.538. The actual characteristic graph of the family

For a coherent regular holonomic module \(A\) on \(X\), set \(A_Q=\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes A\), with its trivial connection in the parameter directions. A product good filtration gives \[ \operatorname{Char}(A_Q) =0_{T^*Q}\times\operatorname{Char}(A). \tag{UQD.4} \] Indeed filter by \(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes F_kA\). Parameter derivatives preserve filtration degree, so their positive symbols kill the associated graded; the remaining associated graded is the flat product of \(\operatorname{gr}A\). Faithful flatness over the field preserves exactly its support. This proves the stated equality, including zero covectors.

Define the compatible point set \[ Z_A(y,\eta)= \{x\in f^{-1}(y):(x,df_x^t\eta)\in\operatorname{Char}(A)\}. \tag{UQD.5} \] It is closed: the cotangent pullback of the fixed covector is algebraic on \(f^{-1}(y)\), and the characteristic variety is closed. For the actual full differential on \(Q\times X\), (UQD.2) and (UQD.4) give \[ \{(q,x):((q,x),dh_{q,x})\in\operatorname{Char}(A_Q)\} =Q\times Z_A(y,\eta)\subset h^{-1}(0). \tag{UQD.6} \] To check both inclusions, the parameter component of a covector in (UQD.4) must be zero. The parameter derivatives of \(h\) force \(f(x)=y\). At those points the \(X\)-component is exactly \(df_x^t\eta\), independently of \(q\). Conversely each compatible covector satisfies all these equations. There is no requirement that \(df_x^t\eta\) be nonzero, that the compatible scheme be reduced, or that the vertical Hessian be invertible.

3.539. From characteristic membership to the closed cycle carrier

We use the bounded complex-field statement Holomorphic critical support and graph covectors, HC0–HC2. With normalized cycles, its conclusion on a fixed zero level is \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{Supp}(\Phi_u F) =\{z\in u^{-1}(0):(z,du_z)\in\Sigma_F\},\\ F\text{ bounded finite-rank complex-constructible}. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.7} \] Here \(\Sigma_F\) is complex microsupport, and support means the closure of the nonzero-stalk locus. It is not an assertion that every stalk on this closed set is nonzero.

The complete programme proof matters for this use. The half-plane comparison HP0–HP2 identifies the actual specialization unit by restricting one negative strip of the logarithmic cover. The reverse implication prepares every actual characteristic component by GS0–GS4: projective conormal compactification retains whole fibres, the normal slice retains visible original normal objects, and the sliced actual graph intersection is isolated. The relative-conormal radial bound and the compact-band maps RB/IV then give a nonzero pure perverse contribution. The actual normal-slice comparison HN9, proved by cofinal compact normal packets and their unit square, returns it to the ambient cycle. Closed support contains the dense nonzero locus on that characteristic component. This proves (UQD.7), including positive-dimensional components and zero differentials. Its geometric antecedent also appears in Massey, A Little Microlocal Morse Theory, Corollary 4.15.

Apply the bounded regular comparison AIC.8 and the specified ambient cycle comparison PIC.2. Restriction and faithful bounded regular Riemann–Hilbert show that a module and its de Rham complex vanish on exactly the same open subsets; their closed carriers agree. The coherent module \(C_h A_Q\) consequently has the exact closed carrier \[ \operatorname{Supp}(C_h A_Q) =Q\times Z_A(y,\eta). \tag{UQD.8} \] The normalizing shift changes no support. Fix \(x_0\in f^{-1}(y)\). Suppose \(x_0\) is absent from \(Z_A\) or is an isolated point of its reduced carrier. In the latter case \(\{x_0\}\) is open and closed in \(Z_A\): remove the finitely many irreducible components not containing \(x_0\); every component through an isolated point is that point. Thus \(Z_A\setminus\{x_0\}\) is closed in \(X\), even when it has positive dimension. For \(a:Q\times\{x_0\}\hookrightarrow Q\times X\), bounded disjoint closed support and Kashiwara's equivalence, Theorem 3.1 give \[ C_h A_Q\simeq a_+V_A\oplus B_A,\qquad \operatorname{Supp}(B_A)\cap a(Q)=\varnothing, \qquad V_A=a^!C_h A_Q. \tag{UQD.9} \] If \(x_0\notin Z_A\), put \(V_A=0\). If \(x_0\in Z_A\), (UQD.8) says that the section part has support all of \(Q\), and in particular \(V_A\ne0\). Normalized cycles and closed extension are t-exact on bounded regular modules, so \(V_A\) is a regular holonomic module on \(Q\), in degree zero.

The decomposition is natural even when two modules have different closed away carriers. Every derived map from a section part to an away part, or in the opposite direction, is zero by disjoint closed support. Thus all coefficient maps preserve the specified section part. In particular its natural comparison is \[ \theta_{C_h A_Q}:a^!C_h A_Q \xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_h A_Q. \tag{UQD.10} \] This identity uses the actual two closed adjunctions. It is the identity on \(a_+V_A\); both inverse functors vanish on \(B_A\).

3.540. Closed-section adjunctions with both infinite tails

Put \(D=\dim(Q\times X)\), \(e=\dim Q\), and \(c=\dim X=D-e\). On the actual regular Ind categories the closed section has continuous adjunctions \[ a^*\dashv a_+\dashv a^!,\qquad a^*a_+\simeq1,\quad a^!a_+\simeq1. \tag{UQD.11} \] On bounded regular inputs these are the full closed-support adjunctions of Riemann–Hilbert and the ordered transfer calculation. All functors take bounded regular objects to bounded regular objects. Ind extends their units, counits and triangle identities; hence (UQD.11) holds on full mapping complexes. PIC.8–PIC.10 identify their direct images with the actual ambient module direct images.

The comparison \(\theta_B\) means \(a^*\) of the right counit \(a_+a^!B\to B\), preceded by the inverse of \(a^*a_+\simeq1\). The Ind t-structure has filtered bounded truncations, and ordinary module truncations commute with these filtered colimits. Thus the actual scheme embedding is t-exact as well as fully faithful.

Their amplitudes are uniformly finite. The backward transfer in normal coordinates is the quotient by the \(c\) commuting normal functions, with the inverse normal density. Its left-free Koszul resolution has length \(c\): PBW reduces exactness to that regular sequence in the structure-sheaf polynomial algebra. Hom computes the actual \(a^!\) in degrees \(0,\ldots,c\), retaining the right tangential operator action. The normal density contracts in the ordered closed-adjunction map. The earlier coherent-duality bounds on the two varieties also give a safe ordinary-inverse bound: \[ a^!:D^{[p,q]}\longrightarrow D^{[p,q+c]},\qquad a^*:D^{[p,q]}\longrightarrow D^{[p-D-c-e,\;q+D+e]}. \tag{UQD.12} \] For the second bound apply \(\mathbb D_{Q}\,a^!\,\mathbb D_{Q\times X}\) on bounded inputs. The first dual has safe heart range \([-D,D]\), and the last dual on \(Q\) has range \([-e,e]\); reversing the intermediate range gives precisely the displayed safe interval. Filtered Ind truncations extend these fixed bounds to arbitrary inputs. No dual of an infinite complex is taken.

Let \(B\) be arbitrary unbounded such that every \(H^mB\) is a filtered union of bounded heart objects having (UQD.9). Continuity gives pure degree-zero, identical section inverse images on those heart objects and their unions. The finite-amplitude window argument then proves \[ H^m(a^!B)\simeq a^!H^mB,\quad H^m(a^*B)\simeq a^*H^mB,\qquad \theta_B:a^!B\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*B. \tag{UQD.13} \] Explicitly, choose the lower input cutoff below the desired output degree minus both upper amplitude bounds minus two, and the upper cutoff above that degree minus both lower bounds plus two. The omitted tails vanish in that output degree and its neighbours. The finite Postnikov filtration of the window has only the degree-zero heart row for each inverse functor. It identifies the cohomology of the actual comparison with (UQD.10). The actual ambient embedding PIC.9 is t-exact and fully faithful, so its conservative module cohomology detects that \(\theta_B\) is an equivalence.

Write \(\varepsilon\) for the right-adjunction counit and \(\upsilon\) for the left-adjunction unit. The actual maps \[ \begin{gathered} V=a^!B,\qquad u=\varepsilon_B:a_+V\to B,\\ r=a_+(\theta_B^{-1})\upsilon_B:B\to a_+V,\qquad ru=1. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.14} \] give the full unbounded section retract. Naturality of the left unit identifies \(\upsilon_B\varepsilon_B\) with \(a_+\theta_B\), since that unit is the identity on the fully faithful image of \(a_+\). This proves the identity of maps, not only a decomposition of cohomology.

3.541. Componentwise isolation of one compatible point

Take \(E\in\mathscr R_\infty(X)\) and fix \(x_0\in f^{-1}(y)\). Each \(H^mE\) is a filtered union of coherent regular holonomic heart subobjects: use filtered bounded presentations and their t-exact truncations, take images, and use the Noetherian Serre property of the regular heart. Suppose that, for every such finite subobject in every degree, \[ A\subset H^mE\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_0\notin Z_A(y,\eta)\ \text{or }x_0 \text{ is isolated in }Z_A(y,\eta). \tag{UQD.15} \] The closed sets and the isolating neighbourhoods may depend on \(A\) and \(m\). The same \(x_0\) is used throughout. Other components of \(Z_A\) may be positive dimensional. Suppose also that one finite \(A_0\subset H^{m_0}E\) satisfies \[ (x_0,df_{x_0}^t\eta)\in\operatorname{Char}(A_0). \tag{UQD.16} \] Use \(E_Q=\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes E\). This is the normalized smooth inverse image, with no shift on the operator-module heart. Flatness and continuity give \(H^mE_Q=\operatorname*{colim}_A A_Q\). Consequently the actual continuous, t-exact normalized cycle functor has \[ H^m C_h E_Q=\operatorname*{colim}_{A\subset H^mE} C_h A_Q. \tag{UQD.17} \] Every term has the natural section decomposition (UQD.9) at the fixed \(x_0\), although its away carrier can vary. Equations (UQD.13)–(UQD.14) therefore give a section retract of \(C_hE_Q\). It is nonzero. Indeed (UQD.16) and (UQD.8) give \(V_{A_0}\ne0\); t-exactness of cycles preserves the inclusion from \(A_{0,Q}\), and \(H^0a^!\) is left exact because it is the heart of the right adjoint to the t-exact \(a_+\). Thus \[ 0\ne V_{A_0}\hookrightarrow H^{m_0}a^!C_hE_Q, \qquad a^!C_hE_Q\ne0. \tag{UQD.18} \] This uses a bounded finite witness inside a genuinely unbounded object. Neither a common neighbourhood nor an exchange with an infinite product has entered the proof.

3.542. Proper image of the section and a target characteristic witness

Let \(b:Q\times\{y\}\hookrightarrow Q\times Y\). The restriction of \(f_Q\) to the selected section is the isomorphism \((q,x_0)\mapsto(q,y)\). Actual transfer composition, first on bounded regular inputs and then by Ind, gives \[ (f_Q)_+a_+V\simeq b_+V. \tag{UQD.19} \] This retains the coefficient, including all its parameter-direction operator action. The intermediate density cancels; there is no fibre-length multiplier. Since \(b_+\) is fully faithful, \(V\ne0\) implies \(b_+V\ne0\).

PIC.19 and the actual product comparison give \[ \begin{gathered} C_g(f_Q)_+E_Q\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_Q)_+C_hE_Q,\\ (f_Q)_+(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes E) \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+E. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.20} \] For the second map the bounded product proof is Adjunctions, base change and the projection formula, equation (2.4): graph transfer extends by the product, the relative Spencer differential acts in the original directions, and finite affine Čech totalizations commute with the exterior coefficient tensor and its signs. Both functors are continuous by PIC.4–PIC.10, so the specified comparison extends to all Ind inputs.

Apply these exact functors to \(u,r\) in (UQD.14), inserting the inverse first comparison in (UQD.20) and (UQD.19). The resulting maps satisfy \[ \begin{gathered} b_+V\longrightarrow C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+E) \longrightarrow b_+V,\\ \text{composite }1,\qquad C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+E)\ne0. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.21} \] They are the actual functor images and adjunction maps. The coefficient triangles and monodromy are retained by PIC.16–PIC.19.

Suppose instead that the single covector \((y,\eta)\) belongs to the characteristic variety of no finite coherent submodule of any cohomology module of \(f_+E\). Apply (UQD.4)–(UQD.8) to each such \(F\) on the target, using the identity map of \(Y\). The actual graph carrier for \(g\) is empty, so \(C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes F)=0\). These \(F\) form the filtered unions of the target cohomology modules. T-exactness, continuity and conservative cohomology imply \[ \begin{gathered} (y,\eta)\notin\operatorname{Char}(F) \text{ for every finite }F\subset H^n(f_+E),\ n\in\mathbf Z\\ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+E)=0. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.22} \] This contradicts (UQD.21). Thus some finite \(F_0\subset H^{n_0}(f_+E)\) has \((y,\eta)\in\operatorname{Char}(F_0)\). This is an actual finite target witness, rather than membership only in the closure of a union. No common cotangent neighbourhood for all target submodules was used.

In particular \(f_+E\) cannot be cohomologically lisse, meaning that all its finite cohomology submodules have characteristic support in the zero section: \(\eta\ne0\) excludes the witness from that section. The finite zero-section criterion of §3.446 identifies those finite zero-support modules with flat connections.

3.543. The contrapositive and its geometric hypotheses

The result can be applied one covector at a time: \[ \begin{gathered} E\in\mathscr R_\infty(X),\quad \eta\ne0,\quad f(x_0)=y,\\ x_0\text{ absent or isolated in every }Z_A(y,\eta),\\ (y,\eta)\notin\operatorname{Char}(F) \text{ for every finite }F\subset H^n(f_+E),\ n\in\mathbf Z\\ \Longrightarrow\quad (x_0,df_{x_0}^t\eta)\notin\operatorname{Char}(A) \text{ for all }A\subset H^mE,\ m\in\mathbf Z. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.23} \] A sufficient way to obtain the isolation hypothesis is a closed conic bound \(\Lambda\) with \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{Char}(A)\subset\Lambda\text{ for all finite }A,\\ x_0\text{ absent or isolated in } \{x\in f^{-1}(y):(x,df_x^t\eta)\in\Lambda\}. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.24} \] Each \(Z_A\) is a closed subset of that compatible set, so it either avoids \(x_0\) or retains its isolated point. Componentwise finite compatible fibres imply this hypothesis at every selected point, but the theorem needs only the one isolated point. More generally the target may have its finite characteristic sets in a cone \(\Gamma\) avoiding \((y,\eta)\). For a product target \(Y=B\times C\), the relative lissity bound \(\Gamma=T^*B\times0_{T^*C}\) avoids every covector with nonzero \(C\)-component. The proof requires no zero-covector condition on its \(B\)-component.

In a Hecke application these are the actual compatible cotangent fibres, with the correspondence's signs and chart maps; the finite compatible-Higgs calculations in §§3.26–3.32 address that geometric input. The theorem above supplies the complex scheme proper-image detection step for regular Ind inputs, including a target characteristic bound only in the moving curve directions. It does not infer regular ind-membership from the independent nilpotent support condition, supply a smooth presentation of every required stack correspondence, or prove equality of the nilpotent and spectral-projector images. Those remain separate assertions. No category of cycles over a new geometric field is used in this argument.

3.544. Exercise and solution: cubic and higher ramification in a family

Exercise 3.GV. Take \(f(z)=z^a\), \(a\ge2\), \(y=0\), \(\eta=dt\), and a rank-\(r\) trivial connection on the source line. Compute the universal family and its normalized cycles, including both infinite cohomological tails.

Solution 3.GV. Here \(Q=\mathbf A^1_q\), and \[ \begin{gathered} g(q,t)=t+\frac q2t^2,\qquad h(q,z)=z^a+\frac q2z^{2a},\\ d_Qh=\frac12z^{2a},\quad d_zh=az^{a-1}(1+qz^a). \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.25} \] The full source critical set is \(Q\times\{0\}\), and \(dh=0\) all along it. The target function is a submersion: \(d_qg=t^2/2\), and at \(t=0\), \(d_tg=1\). Near any point of the source section choose the unique analytic root with value one and put \[ u=z(1+qz^a/2)^{1/a},\qquad h=u^a,\qquad V_{a,r}=\mathbf C^r\otimes (\mathbf C^a/\mathbf C_{\mathrm{diag}}). \tag{UQD.26} \] The derivative \(du/dz\) at the section is one, so the inverse-function proof gives genuine local coordinates preserving \(q\). These root germs agree on overlaps by their fixed value at the section. The actual covered-fibre diagonal therefore identifies the section coefficient with the constant regular connection \(\mathcal O_Q\otimes V_{a,r}\). Its value monodromy is the cyclic permutation of the \(a\) roots on the diagonal quotient. Parameter transport is trivial by those matching germs. Full bounded regular Riemann–Hilbert identifies this algebraic parameter connection with the trivial one.

Proper comparison and the section's isomorphic image give \[ C_g\!\left(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+\mathcal O^r\right) \simeq b_+(\mathcal O_Q\otimes V_{a,r}),\qquad \operatorname{rank}V_{a,r}=r(a-1). \tag{UQD.27} \] The target module \(f_+\mathcal O^r\) is consequently not cohomologically lisse, although \(g\) itself is a submersion. For both tails, exact continuity gives \[ \begin{gathered} E=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal O^r[2n],\\ C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+E) \simeq b_+\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z} (\mathcal O_Q\otimes V_{a,r})[2n]. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.28} \] Every even coefficient cohomology has rank \(r(a-1)\); every odd one is zero. The positive-dimensional source section, rather than an isolated point in the total space, is essential to the actual maps.

Figure 3.67. The upper panels are real coordinate sections of the complex \((q,z)\) and \((q,t)\) spaces. For \(f(z)=z^3\), the entire complex section \(z=0\) has \(dh=0\), while \(dg|_{t=0}=dt\ne0\). The map of sections preserves \(q\). The lower normal fibre uses \(q=0\) and \(h=1/64\), whose three roots are \(\zeta^j/4\), \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}\). Its central diagonal has a two-dimensional quotient, transported as a connection along the complex parameter line. The actual target module is \(f_+\mathcal O\); its nonzero family cycles show its failure of lissity. Proofs: UQD.1–UQD.6 and UQD.25–UQD.28.

3.545. Exercise and solution: two sections and unequal cycle ranks

Exercise 3.GW. Use \(f(z)=z^2(z-1)^3\), \(y=0\), \(\eta=dt\), and the trivial connection. Compute the two section coefficients in the universal family and explain the role of compatible-fibre multiplicities.

Solution 3.GW. The derivative and the universal family are \[ f'(z)=z(z-1)^2(5z-2),\qquad h(q,z)=f(z)+\frac q2f(z)^2,\qquad Z_{\mathcal O}(0,dt)=\{0,1\}. \tag{UQD.29} \] At zero, \(f=z^2u_0\) with \(u_0(0)=-1\). At one, \(f=(z-1)^3u_1\) with \(u_1(1)=1\). On the two disjoint normal neighbourhoods the chosen analytic roots give coordinates of orders two and three. Incorporating the additional unit \(1+qf/2\) as in (UQD.26) preserves these orders. Consequently the actual two section coefficients are \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal O_Q\otimes V_2,\qquad \mathcal O_Q\otimes V_3,\\ V_k=\mathbf C^k/\mathbf C_{\mathrm{diag}},\qquad \dim V_2=1,\quad\dim V_3=2. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.30} \] Monodromy is the two-cycle quotient on the first and the three-cycle quotient on the second. Proper direct image is their direct sum: \[ C_g(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes f_+\mathcal O) \simeq b_+\bigl(\mathcal O_Q\otimes(V_2\oplus V_3)\bigr), \qquad \operatorname{rank}=3. \tag{UQD.31} \] The compatible equation \(f'=0\) on the chosen fibre has lengths one and two at these points. Their reduced carrier has two points. Neither count changes the coefficient-one section-image comparison; the cycle ranks come from the two actual diagonal quotients. The third critical point \(z=2/5\) is excluded by the full parameter derivative: \[ f(2/5)=-\frac{108}{3125}\ne0,\qquad \partial_qh(q,2/5)=\frac12f(2/5)^2\ne0. \tag{UQD.32} \] Thus a vertical critical point of \(f\) outside the selected target fibre contributes no full-family critical graph point, for any \(q\).

3.546. Exercise and solution: isolation and other positive-dimensional components

Exercise 3.GX. Produce a nonzero regular holonomic module on a proper curve whose direct image to a point is zero, and compare its compatible fibre for a constant map to the affine line.

Solution 3.GX. On \(\mathbf G_m\) take the rank-one connection with horizontal monodromy \(-1\), represented by the equation \[ (z\partial_z+\tfrac12)e=0,\qquad j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1,\qquad M=j_+\mathcal E. \tag{UQD.33} \] It has regular logarithmic singularities at zero and infinity and is nonzero. Locally its meromorphic de Rham operator is \(z\partial_z-\tfrac12\); on a Laurent series it multiplies the \(z^n\) coefficient by \(n-\tfrac12\). All these scalars are invertible, and division preserves convergence. At infinity the residue changes sign and remains nonintegral. Hence its de Rham stalks at both missing endpoints are zero; on \(\mathbf G_m\) its de Rham complex is the monodromy-\(-1\) local system \(L[1]\). This is also \(Rj_*L[1]\), since the punctured-disc cellular differential is \(-2\), an isomorphism.

The deformation retraction of \(\mathbf C^*\) to the circle and its one-vertex, one-edge local-system complex give \[ R\Gamma(\mathbf G_m,L)\simeq [\,\mathbf C\xrightarrow{-2}\mathbf C\,]=0, \qquad R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1,\operatorname{DR}M)=0. \tag{UQD.34} \] Let \(f:\mathbf P^1\to\mathbf A^1_t\) be constant at zero. The proper de Rham comparison and full faithfulness imply \[ M\ne0,\qquad f_+M=0. \tag{UQD.35} \] For \(\eta=dt\ne0\), every pulled covector is zero. The zero covector belongs to the characteristic variety over every point of the support, which is the whole proper curve. Thus \[ \begin{gathered} Z_M(0,dt)=\mathbf P^1,\qquad h=g\circ f_Q=0,\\ C_h(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes M) =\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes M,\\ (f_Q)_+C_h(\mathcal O_Q\boxtimes M)=0. \end{gathered} \tag{UQD.36} \] The source cycle is carried by an entire proper curve over each parameter. Its nonzero cohomology coefficient can disappear under proper integration; there is no isolated product-section retract of the kind proved above.

The theorem nevertheless allows positive-dimensional components elsewhere. Take the disjoint union of the power map in Exercise 3.GV and this constant curve map, with input \(\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}\oplus M\). At the selected covector its compatible carrier is \(\{0\}\sqcup\mathbf P^1\); the source point on the affine-line component is isolated. The proper image is \(f_{a,+}\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1}\oplus0\), and the nonzero section coefficient \(V_a\) survives. Cancellation on the other component cannot remove its actual retract. Thus isolation of the selected point is essential, whereas finiteness of the entire compatible fibre is unnecessary.

3.547. Continuous operations on regular Ind objects

Work over \(\mathbf C\). For a smooth separated finite-type scheme \(M\), put \[ \mathscr R_0(M)=D^b_{\mathrm{rh}}(\mathcal D_M), \qquad \mathscr R_\infty(M)=\operatorname{Ind}\mathscr R_0(M) \subset D_{\mathrm{qc}}(\mathcal D_M). \tag{HRI.1} \] The embedding is the actual full embedding of §§3.527–3.529. Its proof uses finite operator resolutions and a finite affine Čech complex, so its mapping-complex comparison includes both unbounded tails. The image is stable and closed under colimits. Throughout this section, regular Ind membership means membership in this image; regularity of individual cohomology modules alone is not substituted for it.

If \(f:M\to N\) is a map of such smooth schemes, the actual inverse transfer gives \[ f^!K =\mathcal D_{M\to N} \otimes^L_{f^{-1}\mathcal D_N}f^{-1}K [\dim M-\dim N], \qquad f^!(\operatorname{colim}_iK_i) \simeq\operatorname{colim}_i f^!K_i . \tag{HRI.2} \] The transfer, chain-rule action and composition maps are proved in Inverse images, §§1–2. Derived tensor and sheaf inverse image preserve colimits; the actual quasicoherent comparison is checked on the finite affine covers. The bounded four-map theorem Regular singularities, Theorem 5.17 makes \(f^!\) preserve \(\mathscr R_0\). Thus HRI.2 preserves \(\mathscr R_\infty\). The actual direct image is continuous by PIC.4–PIC.10 and preserves bounded regular objects by the same theorem, so it too preserves regular Ind objects, without a properness hypothesis.

External products and the extraordinary tensor are separately continuous, and \[ \begin{aligned} (\operatorname{colim}_i A_i)\boxtimes (\operatorname{colim}_j B_j) &\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i,j}(A_i\boxtimes B_j),\\ A\otimes^! B&=\Delta_M^!(A\boxtimes B). \end{aligned} \tag{HRI.3} \] The coefficient external tensor is over the field; its operator actions are the two commuting actions. Diagonal inverse transfer gives the second formula, including its dimension shift. Regular singularities, Theorem 5.18 proves bounded regularity of these operations. Applying HRI.2 and the first formula to bounded presentations proves regular Ind preservation. No assertion is made that tensoring an arbitrary irregular input with a regular kernel makes it regular.

3.548. Closed base support and finite Zariski locality
