It is the RSC normalization by density side change and \([-1]\). The strong \(!\)-tensor embedding of HLA is \(i_!(E)=i_X(E)[1]\); in particular \(i_!(\mathbf1)=\omega_X\). We will retain this difference when returning to the actual Hecke coefficient and contraction maps. Its bounded-below image consists exactly of operator objects whose cohomology modules are ind-connections: \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{im}(i_X)\cap D_X^{\ge-a}\\ =\{K\in D_X^{\ge-a}: H^mK\in\operatorname{Ind}\operatorname{Conn}_{\mathrm f}(X) \text{ for every }m\}. \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.7} \] To see the reverse containment, each displayed heart object is a filtered union of finite connections and belongs to the image. Full faithfulness lifts every attaching map in a finite Postnikov tower. The direct colimit of the intelligent upper truncations then recovers any bounded-below \(K\): cohomology in each degree is eventually constant, filtered colimits are exact, and cohomology detects zero. Continuity of \(i_X\) supplies that colimit. This argument also proves actual regular Ind membership for such a \(K\); it does not assume it. The forward containment is RSC.1–RSC.3.

Apply PAC.6 to a compatible tower from \(\mathscr Q_X\). It supplies an actual operator realization \[ j_X:\mathscr Q_X=\lim_n\mathscr I_X^{\ge-n} \longrightarrow D_X,\qquad j_X(\{E_n\})=\lim_n i_X(E_n). \tag{PAC.8} \] Its image is exactly \[ \operatorname{im}j_X= \{K\in D_X: H^mK\in\operatorname{Ind}\operatorname{Conn}_{\mathrm f}(X) \text{ for every }m\}. \tag{PAC.9} \] Every object on the right has its actual lower truncations in PAC.7's image, and PAC.6 recovers it with those comparison maps.

3.580. Full maps, continuity and dualizable coefficients

For two effective towers with limits \(A,B\), mapping into the target limit and using the truncation adjunction gives \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Map}_{D_X}(A,B) &\simeq\lim_n\operatorname{Map}_{D_X} (\tau^{\ge-n}A,\tau^{\ge-n}B)\\ &\simeq\lim_n\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr I_X}(A_n,B_n). \end{aligned} \tag{PAC.10} \] Here a target in \(D_X^{\ge-n}\) receives maps uniquely through the source truncation \(\tau^{\ge-n}A\). These are mapping spaces; repeat the statement after every target shift to retain the entire stable mapping complex. The last limit is exactly the compatible mapping space in the category defining \(\mathscr Q_X\). Thus \(j_X\) is full. It is t-exact by PAC.6.

The ind-connection heart is Serre: for finite pieces the induced good filtration makes subquotients zero-characteristic connections, as in §3.1, and finite generators enclose the kernel and quotient pieces in finite connections. Its filtered unions are exact. The condition in PAC.9 therefore survives triangles, arbitrary sums and their stable colimit constructions, by the argument of NU.2–NU.4. Consequently the realization is continuous: \[ j_X(\operatorname{colim}_\alpha E_\alpha) \simeq\operatorname{colim}_\alpha j_X(E_\alpha). \tag{PAC.11} \] This assertion concerns colimits; PAC.4's qualification about arbitrary products remains necessary.

The category \(\mathscr Q_X\) is dualizable as a linear presentable category. RSC.11–RSC.14 proves it equals the compactly generated \(\mathscr I_X\) when \(g(X)>0\). RSC.19–RSC.26 gives the full module category \(\operatorname{Mod}_B\) in genus zero, with its free compact generator. The compact-module duality of SUL.22 applies in both cases: \[ \mathscr Q_X\text{ is dualizable},\qquad \mathscr Q_X=\mathscr I_X\ (g(X)>0),\qquad \mathscr Q_{\mathbf P^1}\simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{T_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C[1])}. \tag{PAC.12} \] The last algebra is associative, with one degree-minus-one generator; its square is not declared zero.

3.581. The exact affine coefficient functor

Let \(B_0\) be a smooth affine scheme, put \(R=D(B_0)\), and reserve \(B\) for the loop algebra in PAC.12 only when needed. The rectangular operator identity and descent of EFC.14 give \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Dmod}(B_0\times X) &\simeq R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}(D_X),\\ \operatorname{Dmod}(B_0)\otimes\mathscr Q_X &\simeq R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr Q_X). \end{aligned} \tag{PAC.13} \] The second equality is the free associative action bar: a left \(R\)-action, its associative relations and higher homotopies are exactly an internal module. Its augmented free resolution contracts by the unit insertion. The same bar gives the tensor-category universal property, exactly as in RSC.27. No commutativity of \(R\) or symmetric tensor over \(R\) is required.

The forgetful functor on the first module category has the concrete description \[ \mathsf U_{B_0}K= (\operatorname{pr}_X)_* \operatorname{oblv}_{B_0\text{-}\mathcal D}(K). \tag{PAC.14} \] Only the \(B_0\)-direction differential action is forgotten. Ordinary affine pushforward of the underlying quasi-coherent module is exact, continuous and conservative, and retains the commuting \(D_X\)-action. The recovered \(R\)-action includes both functions and derivatives in the \(B_0\)-direction. On an exterior product this is \[ \mathsf U_{B_0}(M\boxtimes E) =\Gamma(B_0,\operatorname{oblv}_{\mathcal D}M) \otimes_{\mathbf C}E. \tag{PAC.15} \] The sections are underlying affine sections. De Rham integration would instead use its relative Spencer differential and its shift. Thus the actual functor just defined satisfies \[ H^m(\mathsf U_{B_0}K)=\mathsf U_{B_0}(H^mK),\qquad \mathsf U_{B_0}\operatorname{colim}K_\alpha \simeq\operatorname{colim}\mathsf U_{B_0}K_\alpha . \tag{PAC.16} \] These identities hold on arbitrary unbounded objects.

3.582. Finite pieces determine the completed coefficient

Assume \(K\in\mathscr R_\infty(B_0\times X)\) and \[ \operatorname{SS}_\infty(K)\subset T^*B_0\times0_X . \tag{PAC.17} \] No cohomological bound is imposed. For each coherent regular \(N\subset H^mK\), EFC.16 supplies an actual external-category preimage. The continuous bilinear functor \((M,E)\mapsto\Gamma(B_0,\operatorname{oblv}M)\otimes E\) from \(\mathscr R_{B_0}\times\mathscr I_X\) to \(\mathscr I_X\) has, after \(i_X\), precisely PAC.15's comparison to \(\mathsf U_{B_0}J_{B_0}\). It agrees on exterior generators and extends through their full free bar with the original maps. It follows that \(\mathsf U_{B_0}N\in\operatorname{im}i_X\). Exactness of \(\mathsf U_{B_0}\) puts it in degree zero, so it is an ind-connection.

Now use the actual global coherent unions of HRI.6: \[ \begin{aligned} H^m(\mathsf U_{B_0}K) &=\operatorname*{colim}_{N\subset H^mK\ \mathrm{coherent}} \mathsf U_{B_0}N\\ &\in\operatorname{Ind}\operatorname{Conn}_{\mathrm f}(X). \end{aligned} \tag{PAC.18} \] This is a statement about each degree separately and allows both infinite tails. PAC.9 consequently gives a completed coefficient with an actual comparison \[ j_X(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf U_{B_0}K, \qquad Q\in\mathscr Q_X . \tag{PAC.19} \] No common finite piece or common conormal cone was chosen for the different degrees.

3.583. Retaining the original noncommutative action

Keep the original \(R\)-action on \(\mathsf U_{B_0}K\). All its free action-bar terms lift through \(j_X\), since \[ j_X(R^{\otimes n}\otimes Q) \simeq R^{\otimes n}\otimes j_X(Q). \tag{PAC.20} \] Here \(R\) is an ordinary complex vector space. Its tensor operation is a colimit of finite sums of copies, and PAC.11 gives the stated comparison. Multiplication, unit and action faces of the bar have their original maps after \(j_X\). Full faithfulness lifts every one of these maps and their relations, with contractible spaces of lifts. The unit insertion contracts the augmented free resolution after the conservative \(j_X\), hence before it as well. We obtain the actual module lift \[ \widetilde K\in R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr Q_X), \qquad R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}(j_X)(\widetilde K)\xrightarrow{\sim}K . \tag{PAC.21} \] The comparison preserves the original \(R\)-action, not merely its underlying curve object. Using PAC.13 proves \[ \begin{gathered} K\in\operatorname{im}J^{\mathscr Q}_{B_0},\\ J^{\mathscr Q}_{B_0}: \operatorname{Dmod}(B_0)\otimes\mathscr Q_X \longrightarrow\operatorname{Dmod}(B_0\times X). \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.22} \] This functor is full because \(R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}(j_X)\) is full: its underlying mapping complexes and the equalities of action maps are computed in the full \(j_X\). The assertion does not require that the first tensor factor be \(\mathscr R_{B_0}\).

3.584. Descent of the completed coefficients

Let \(Y=\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)\) and \(\mathcal M=\operatorname{Dmod}(Y)\). On its full smooth affine chart diagram, PAC.12 gives \[ \mathcal M\otimes\mathscr Q_X \simeq \lim_{A\to Y}\bigl(\operatorname{Dmod}(A)\otimes\mathscr Q_X\bigr). \tag{PAC.23} \] Tensor with a dualizable category has both adjoints given by tensor with its dual, so preserves this limit. Inverse transfer on the \(A\)-factor commutes with the curve exterior factor: on affine rectangles the two operator directions commute, and the graph and relative Spencer maps act in their original directions. Their full derived bars retain this comparison for arbitrary curve complexes, together with its composition and unit paths. The extraordinary chart shifts remain the same.

Suppose \(K\) on \(Y\times X\) is chartwise regular Ind and every finite witness has zero curve covector. PAC.22 gives factors on all affine bundle charts. Their full functors uniquely lift the actual transition maps and all higher descent paths. PAC.23 therefore supplies the actual global factor: \[ \begin{gathered} K\in\operatorname{im}J_Y^{\mathscr Q},\\ J_Y^{\mathscr Q}:\mathcal M\otimes\mathscr Q_X \longrightarrow\operatorname{Dmod}(Y\times X). \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.24} \] No bound on either cohomological tail is needed. For positive genus, PAC.12 identifies precisely the original coefficient category, so \[ K\in\mathcal M\otimes\mathscr I_X \qquad(g(X)>0). \tag{PAC.25} \] The ind-connection comparisons in positive genus will also retain the existing multi-coordinate Hecke maps. More explicitly, if \(K=J_Y^{0}(Z_0)\) uses the t-exact curve embedding above, the same object has the actual \(i_!\)-coefficient lift \(Z_0[-1]\), since \(J_Y^{!}(Z_0[-1])=K\). For the RA.2 family \(K[1]\), its \(i_!\)-lift is \(Z_0\) itself. These equalities use the given shift comparisons and retain the original open coefficients and units.

3.585. The unbounded regular-input criterion in positive genus

Assume now \(g(X)>0\), and let \(F\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\) be arbitrary. Independent nilpotent support is still the union of actual finite characteristic witnesses, without closure. HRI.16–HRI.19 puts every actual Hecke output in the regular Ind category on every target chart. RHC.28 gives \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{SS}_\infty(F)\subset\mathcal N \quad\Longrightarrow\\ \operatorname{SS}_\infty \bigl((\mathrm H_{V_\nu}F)|_{B_0\times X}\bigr) \subset\mathcal N_{B_0}\times0_X . \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.26} \] PAC.25 therefore gives the full HLA.13 condition. Conversely that condition implies the cohomological curve bound by RHC.36 and hence nilpotent support by RHC.34. Thus \[ \begin{gathered} F\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}},\quad g(X)>0:\\ F\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(F)\subset\mathcal N . \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.27} \] Both infinite cohomological tails are included. No assertion that every cohomologically nilpotent object is regular has been made. For the specified half root, SH.19 gives the actual transport \[ \mathrm H^L_{V_\nu} =\mathcal T_{Y\times X}^{-1}\mathrm H_{V_\nu}\mathcal T_Y . \tag{PAC.28} \] Its intermediate line evaluations are RH.17, and the line is pulled from the bundle factor. Principal symbols and the curve direction are unchanged. RA.2's fixed curve shift also leaves the full coefficient image unchanged. These specified comparisons transport PAC.26–PAC.27 to those conventions.

3.586. Regular nilpotent coefficients and the full Ran parameters

Write \(\mathcal C\) for the full chartwise regular Ind subcategory with nilpotent cohomological support. Under the positive-genus hypothesis, PAC.27 identifies it with \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}}\). It is presentable by the full-kernel construction of §3.208, applied inside the presentable \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\) of EFC.26. Restrict HLA.13's small family of continuous obstruction functors to that category. Choose an uncountable regular \(\kappa\) for its small generator presentation, all target presentations and the cell bounds of the images of those generators. Then the functors preserve \(\kappa\)-compact objects. The proof of HLA.11–HLA.12 uses those objects and works at this cardinal: a \(\kappa\)-compact approximation mapping to a kernel object can be enlarged along a countable chain until all its obstruction transitions are null. The chain colimit is still \(\kappa\)-compact and is in the kernel. Amalgamating fewer than \(\kappa\) such approximations and repeating that construction supplies the coherent cones, so the factorization category is \(\kappa\)-filtered. The full small-relations bar identifies the kernel with the corresponding Ind-completion. It is therefore presentable, with its full inclusion preserving ambient colimits; compact generation at the original cardinal is not assumed. Its cohomological support condition is also stable under triangles and colimits directly by NU.2–NU.4.

Let \(Z\) be the actual \(i_!\)-coefficient lift for the chosen Hecke-family convention, as specified after PAC.25, and put \(N=J_Y^{!}(Z)\). For \(F\in\mathcal C\) and compact \(E\in\mathscr I_X\), the HLA.17 contraction and its operator normalization are \[ \begin{aligned} C_E(Z)&=(\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal M}\otimes\Gamma_{\mathscr I}) (E^\vee\otimes Z),\\ \mathcal P_E(N)&=p_{Y,+} \bigl(\operatorname{pr}_X^!i_!(E^\vee)\otimes^!N\bigr),\\ C_E(Z)&\simeq\mathcal P_E(N)[-2]. \end{aligned} \tag{PAC.29} \] Here \(p_Y:Y\times X\to Y\) is the actual proper curve projection on the output object \(N\). NTR.1–NTR.6 proves the displayed comparison with its Spencer evaluation map and the shift \([-2]\). Its unit test is \(p_{X,+}\omega_X=\Gamma_{\mathscr I}(\mathbf1)[2]\). Thus the t-exact curve embedding and the strong \(!\)-tensor embedding have not been substituted for one another. For finite connections, the tensor is flat in the curve direction and has zero curve symbol. Its source is regular Ind, and proper integration preserves this property by HRI and PIC. If a target covector lies outside \(\mathcal N_{B_0}\), its pullback under the projection is \((\eta,0_X)\). PAC.26 makes the compatible set of every finite source piece empty. The general proper upper argument RHC.23–RHC.26, with its fixed output window, therefore gives \[ C_E(Z)\in\mathcal C . \tag{PAC.30} \] Finite cones, shifts and retracts prove this for all compact \(E\). To extend the conclusion, write \(P=E^\vee\). Duality permutes the compact objects. The functor \(P\mapsto(\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal M}\otimes\Gamma_{\mathscr I})(P\otimes Z)\) is continuous in \(P\). Expressing any \(P\in\mathscr I_X\) as a colimit of compact objects and using the colimit closure of \(\mathcal C\) puts every value of this functor in \(\mathcal C\).

The self-duality HLA.17–HLA.18 identifies \(\mathcal M\otimes\mathscr I_X\) with continuous functors \(\mathscr I_X\to\mathcal M\). All values in PAC.30 and the full inclusion of \(\mathcal C\) give precisely a continuous functor with values in \(\mathcal C\). Consequently \[ \begin{gathered} \mathrm H_{V_\nu}(\mathcal C)\subset\mathcal C\otimes\mathscr I_X,\\ \Phi_\psi(\vec V,N;F)\in\mathcal C \quad(F\in\mathcal C,\ N\in\operatorname{Dmod}(X^J)). \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.31} \] For several coordinates, HLA.14–HLA.16 retains the actual exchange, collision and unit maps; compact coefficient contractions can be performed successively. An arbitrary full parameter \(N\) contracts the independent curve factors to a complex of vector spaces. It need not be regular: this operation leaves the first \(\mathcal C\)-factor unchanged and uses its colimit closure. Every comparison map and higher relation uniquely lifts through the full inclusion. Thus the existing full unital Ran action restricts to \(\mathcal C\), with its actual parameter functors.

3.587. The projective line and the precise remaining scope

The completed coefficient conclusion PAC.24 holds in genus zero, but it gives \(\mathscr Q_X\). For \(X=\mathbf P^1\), RSC.19–RSC.26 gives the exact distinction \[ \begin{gathered} B=T_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C[1]),\quad |u|=-1,\quad v=u^2,\\ \mathscr Q_X=\operatorname{Mod}_B,\\ \mathscr I_X=\{M:B[v^{-1}]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}M=0\}. \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.32} \] The degree-minus-one generator is associative, with \(u^2\ne0\). In particular \[ L=B[v^{-1}]\ne0,\qquad \operatorname{RHom}_B(\mathbf C,L)=0,\qquad L\notin\mathscr I_X . \tag{PAC.33} \] The actual operator realization supplied by PAC.8 does not remove this distinction. A genus-zero Hecke-specific torsion argument is required for the unrestricted ind-connection image; the local lower-bounded result EFC.30 continues to apply in every genus.

The independent regularity and generation statement \[ \{F:\operatorname{SS}_\infty(F)\subset\mathcal N\} \ \subset\ \mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}} \tag{PAC.34} \] is separate even in positive genus. It is not inferred from PAC.27, whose regular-input hypothesis is explicit. AIC.17's full supported factorization, equality with all independently nilpotent-supported objects and derived tempered Satake retain their requirements. GFP.55–GFP.56 give original-field enhanced generation and regular nilpotent landing on arbitrary inputs. Free further reading for completions and curve coefficients is Arinkin–Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Raskin–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky, Appendices E.1–E.2 and E.9. The actual operator effectivity, affine action lift and comparison arguments used here are proved above.

Figure 3.71. The tower and flat restriction comparisons are PAC.1–PAC.6. The affine coefficient retains both \(z\) and \(\partial_z\), as in PAC.13–PAC.22 and Exercise 3.HI. The positive-genus conclusion is PAC.25–PAC.31; the projective-line localized coefficient is PAC.32–PAC.33 and Exercise 3.HJ. The drawn tower is the exact finite-prefix example of Exercise 3.HH, not an assumption that arbitrary products commute with localization.

3.588. Three calculations with towers and coefficient actions

Exercise 3.HH. On \(\mathbf A^1_z\), let \(\delta=D/Dz\), and compare a Postnikov tower of its shifts with the ordinary product of copies of \(\delta\). Does localization at \(z\ne0\) preserve that product?

Solution 3.HH. The tower with its projection transitions is \[ \begin{gathered} K_n=\bigoplus_{j=0}^n\delta[j],\qquad \tau^{\ge-n}K_{n+1}=K_n,\\ \lim_nK_n=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\delta[j]. \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.35} \] Its differential is zero and there is one copy in each degree \(0,-1,-2,\ldots\). The degreewise product computing its limit has exactly that one copy in each degree, which proves the last equality. All terms and its limit restrict to zero on \(z\ne0\).

By contrast, in \(P=\prod_{j\ge0}\delta\), in degree zero, take \(a=(\partial_z^j\delta)_{j\ge0}\). The Weyl relation gives \[ z^r\partial_z^j\delta= \begin{cases} (-1)^r\,\dfrac{j!}{(j-r)!}\,\partial_z^{j-r}\delta,&j\ge r,\\ 0,&j<r. \end{cases} \tag{PAC.36} \] For every \(r\), its \(j=r\) component is nonzero, so no power of \(z\) kills \(a\). Localization of the underlying coefficient module therefore leaves \(a/1\ne0\), while every individual \(\delta\) localizes to zero: \[ P[z^{-1}]\ne0,\qquad \prod_{j\ge0}(\delta[z^{-1}])=0 . \tag{PAC.37} \] This is an actual affine operator-module example. It explains why PAC.4 proves the tower comparison from stable cohomology.

Exercise 3.HI. For \(B_0=\mathbf A^1_z\) and a finite connection \(E\) on \(X\), compute both the coefficient functor and de Rham integration on \(K=\mathcal O_{B_0}\boxtimes E\).

Solution 3.HI. The exact coefficient functor is \[ \begin{gathered} \mathsf U_{B_0}K=\mathbf C[z]\otimes E,\\ z(z^n)=z^{n+1},\quad \partial_z(z^n)=n z^{n-1},\quad [\partial_z,z]=1 . \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.38} \] The commutator follows by subtracting \(n z^n\) from \((n+1)z^n\). De Rham integration uses instead the actual relative Spencer complex: \[ (\operatorname{pr}_X)_+K =\bigl[\mathbf C[z]\xrightarrow{\partial_z} \mathbf C[z]\,dz\bigr][1]\otimes E \simeq E[1]. \tag{PAC.39} \] Here the bracket before shifting has degrees zero and one. Its kernel is the constants; it is surjective since \(z^n dz\) has the primitive \(z^{n+1}/(n+1)\). The full coefficient action in PAC.38, with its infinite basis, is what is lifted by PAC.21.

Exercise 3.HJ. In the projective-line coefficient algebra of PAC.32, verify that \(L=B[v^{-1}]\) is nonzero but invisible to Hom from the unit. Give an actual contracting homotopy.

Solution 3.HJ. The word basis and inverse are \[ L=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}\mathbf C u^j,\qquad |u^j|=-j,\qquad d=0,\qquad u^{-1}=u v^{-1}. \tag{PAC.40} \] The constant word is nonzero. The actual finite semifree unit resolution RSC.20 is \[ \begin{gathered} Q=B\oplus B\tau,\qquad |\tau|=-2,\qquad d\tau=u,\\ d(b\tau)=(-1)^{|b|}bu,\qquad Q\longrightarrow\mathbf C . \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.41} \] Its second summand maps injectively onto the positive-word ideal, so its only cohomology is the constant word. A homogeneous \(B\)-linear Hom cochain of degree \(k\) is determined by \(a=f(1)\in L^k\) and \(b=f(\tau)\in L^{k-2}\), using \(f(cm)=(-1)^{k|c|}cf(m)\). The Hom differential \(df=-(-1)^kf\,d_Q\) consequently gives \[ \begin{gathered} d(a,b)=(0,-u a),\qquad h(a,b)=(-u^{-1}b,0),\\ dh+hd=\mathrm{id}. \end{gathered} \tag{PAC.42} \] Indeed \(dh(a,b)=(0,b)\) and \(hd(a,b)=(a,0)\). This is a contraction in every degree, with the original resolution signs. Thus the derived Hom is zero while \(L\ne0\). The word localization is nonzero on \(L\), so it is outside the ind-connection subcategory in PAC.32. No regular Ind assertion about an arbitrary completed coefficient is needed for this distinction.

3.589. The restricted spectral action on regular nilpotent objects

Work over \(\mathbf C\), assume \(g(X)>0\), and retain every connected reductive group and bundle component. Put \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal M=\operatorname{Dmod}(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)),\qquad \mathcal N=\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}},\\ \mathcal C=\{F\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}: \operatorname{SS}_\infty(F)\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_G\}. \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.1} \] All categories and mapping complexes are full and unbounded. PAC.27 identifies \(\mathcal C=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap\mathcal N\). PAC.31 proves that this presentable full subcategory is closed under the actual full Ran action. Its inclusion preserves colimits.

Write \(\mathcal A=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X))\), and use the actual functors of UID.2–UID.6: \[ \mathsf D:\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal R,\qquad L\mathsf D\xrightarrow{\theta}\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal A},\qquad r\otimes\mathsf D(a)\simeq\mathsf D(L(r)\otimes a). \tag{ERP.2} \] These are continuous functors with the specified module comparisons. In particular every \(a\), including a noncompact one, has the given Ran lift. The spectral action \(\Psi\) of RSE.36 and NTR.14–NTR.15 satisfies, with its actual natural maps, \[ \Psi(a,c)\simeq \Psi(L\mathsf D(a),c)\simeq \Phi(\mathsf D(a),c)\in\mathcal C . \tag{ERP.3} \] The last membership is PAC.31. Thus the action takes its values in the full subcategory \(\mathcal C\). Full faithfulness lifts the multiplication, unit and every higher relation from \(\mathcal N\). Continuity follows because its colimits are ambient colimits. We obtain \[ \Psi_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal C\longrightarrow\mathcal C, \qquad j:\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathcal N \text{ is a continuous unital }\mathcal A\text{-module functor}. \tag{ERP.4} \] The unit here is the existing action unit. This argument does not declare \(\mathsf D\) strong unital monoidal: \(\mathsf D(\mathbf1)=p\) has the nonunital structure of UID.7–UID.11.

3.590. Full enhanced stages with regular nilpotent underlying objects

Let \(K_E\) and \(\mathcal T_E=\operatorname{QCoh}(Z_E)\) be the actual finite equivariant Koszul stages of ESG.18–ESG.24. Distinguish the algebra \(K_E\in\mathcal A\) from the enhanced induction functor \(P_E\). The full module bar gives \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal C_E&=\mathcal C\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T_E \simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{K_E}(\mathcal C),\\ \mathcal N_E&=\mathcal N\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T_E \simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{K_E}(\mathcal N). \end{aligned} \tag{ERP.5} \] To see the comparison and its exact image, start with an actual \(K_E\)-module in \(\mathcal N\) whose underlying object is in \(\mathcal C\). All its free action terms \(K_E^{\otimes n}\star c\) belong to \(\mathcal C\) by ERP.4. Full faithfulness lifts the action, multiplication and unit faces, and all their coherent paths. The augmented free resolution has its original unit insertion as contracting extra degeneracy. Its realization in \(\mathcal C\) therefore maps to the original module with its original action. The same full mapping-space comparison lifts module maps. Consequently \[ \mathcal C_E\hookrightarrow\mathcal N_E\text{ is full},\qquad F\in\mathcal C_E \Longleftrightarrow J_E^{\mathcal N}F\in\mathcal C . \tag{ERP.6} \] These are object and mapping statements; cohomological membership alone does not replace the action lift.

Tensor the actual \(\mathcal A\)-linear adjunctions ESG.22–ESG.24 by \(\mathcal C\). Their units, counits and triangles descend in the same relative bar. Thus \[ \operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal C}\otimes f_E^* \dashv J_E^{\mathcal C} \dashv\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal C}\otimes f_E^!, \qquad J_E^{\mathcal C}=\text{the actual module forgetful functor}. \tag{ERP.7} \] The rightmost functor is continuous: ESG.23 expresses it by finite perfect dual tensor, with its determinant factor and shifts retained. The forgetful functor is continuous and conservative. The adjunction therefore proves \[ J_E^{\mathcal C}(\mathcal C_E^c)\subset\mathcal C^c . \tag{ERP.8} \] Indeed mapping from such an image is mapping from its compact source into the continuous right adjoint. The same assertion for \(\mathcal N_E\to\mathcal N\) is ESG.25.

3.591. Actual regular point objects in the enhanced stages

For a complex bundle point \(y\), retain SPT.21–SPT.24's intrinsic object, point normalization and fibre line: \[ \delta_y^!\in\mathcal M^c\cap\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}},\qquad \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal M}(\delta_y^!,m)\simeq y^!m . \tag{ERP.9} \] This is the adjunction on the full target, including unbounded objects and stabilizer directions. For every \(m\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\), ESG.33 makes \(T_E m=J_EP_E m\) regular. Its specified factorization through \(\mathcal N\), and the necessary RHC.34–RHC.36 criterion, give \[ T_E(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}})\subset\mathcal C . \tag{ERP.10} \] No regularity of an arbitrary nilpotent object was used.

Under ESG.13 and ESG.26 the enhanced \(P_E m\) has underlying object \(T_E m\). ERP.6 therefore supplies its unique full lift to \(\mathcal C_E\). For the point object write it as \[ Q_{E,y}\in\mathcal C_E,\qquad Q_{E,y}\mapsto P_E\delta_y^!\in\mathcal N_E,\qquad jJ_E^{\mathcal C}Q_{E,y}=J_E^{\mathcal N}P_E\delta_y^!. \tag{ERP.11} \] The last equality is in \(\mathcal N\); its inclusion in \(\mathcal M\) is exactly \(T_E\delta_y^!\). The action maps are the given module maps, rather than a new module structure on the same cohomology.

The point object is compact in the full enhanced stage, by ESG.29 and continuity of \(J_E\). The inclusion in ERP.6 is full and preserves colimits, so it remains compact in the smaller stage: \[ Q_{E,y}\in\mathcal C_E^c,\qquad P_E\delta_y^!\in\mathcal N_E^c . \tag{ERP.12} \] Here compactness is tested by the whole mapping complex.

3.592. Point generators of the regular nilpotent category

Choose the chart-point detectors NC.4–NC.7 on each bounded open of the cofinal exhaustion, and let \(\{y_i\}\) be their composite bundle points. Smooth inverse-image composition identifies each chart test with \(y_i^!\), up to its stated relative shift and an invertible fibre line. These factors preserve vanishing. Thus \[ c\in\mathcal C,\qquad y_i^!c=0\text{ for every }i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c=0 . \tag{ERP.13} \] The proof of NC.7 applies to arbitrary cohomological degrees: its normal Koszul complex has finitely many columns, and on the chosen stratum all cohomology modules and their relevant quotients are flat connections. No point-conservativity assertion on the full \(\mathcal N\) is being made.

For \(F\in\mathcal C_E\), the full inclusion and enhanced adjunction give \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal C_E}(Q_{E,y_i},F) \simeq y_i^!\bigl(\iota jJ_E^{\mathcal C}F\bigr), \qquad \iota:\mathcal N\hookrightarrow\mathcal M . \tag{ERP.14} \] If these complexes vanish, ERP.13 makes the underlying object zero. Conservativity of the actual module forgetful functor makes \(F=0\). Together with ERP.12 this proves \[ \mathcal C_E=\operatorname{Loc}\{Q_{E,y_i}:i\}. \tag{ERP.15} \] For completeness, a set of compact objects with this zero test generates by its full small-DG-module bar. The bar evaluation has cone right-orthogonal to every object in the set; its compact Hom tests are enriched Yoneda contractions. The zero test kills that cone. This proves generation of objects and full mapping complexes.

The actual stage pushforwards jointly generate every unital \(\mathcal A\)-module, by ESG.27–ESG.28: express the supported spectral unit by its compact generator bars, then act on the module. Apply this to \(\mathcal C\), using ERP.15 and continuity. We obtain \[ \begin{gathered} G_{E,i}=J_E^{\mathcal C}Q_{E,y_i}\in\mathcal C^c,\\ \mathcal C=\operatorname{Loc}\{G_{E,i}:E,i\}. \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.16} \] Their compactness is ERP.8. The same objects are compact in \(\mathcal N\), since their enhanced lifts are compact there and ESG.25 preserves compact objects.

3.593. The continuous spectral-linear right adjoint

Every compact object of \(\mathcal C\) is a retract of a finite cell object on the generators ERP.16. Indeed the full free bar and its finite-dimensional coefficient subcomplexes give a filtered system of finite cell approximations. A compact identity factors through one approximation. Finite sums, cones and retracts of their images are compact in \(\mathcal N\). Hence \[ j(\mathcal C^c)\subset\mathcal N^c . \tag{ERP.17} \] Choose a small full DG model of \(\mathcal C^c\). Define \[ r(n)=\int^{c\in\mathcal C^c} c\otimes_{\mathbf C}\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal N}(jc,n). \tag{ERP.18} \] This is the entire enriched coend with its composition and identity faces. For a compact test \(d\), moving its Hom through that bar and contracting the representable gives \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal C}(d,rn) =\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal N}(jd,n)\). Both sides carry source colimits to limits, so the comparison extends to every source in \(\mathcal C\). Its evaluation is the counit. Yoneda gives the unit and its triangles. Thus \[ j\dashv r,\qquad rj\simeq\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal C}, \qquad r\text{ is continuous}. \tag{ERP.19} \] Continuity follows directly in ERP.18 from ERP.17. This is an adjunction for the full regular nilpotent inclusion into \(\mathcal N\); it is not an adjunction inferred for \(\Pi\).

The right adjoint is also \(\mathcal A\)-linear. For a dualizable coefficient \(a\), its adjunction mate is an equivalence, since for every \(c\) the two Hom tests are \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal C}(c,r(a\star n)) &\simeq\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal N}(j(a^\vee\star c),n)\\ &\simeq\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal C}(c,a\star r(n)). \end{aligned} \tag{ERP.20} \] SDU.1–SDU.3 proves that the compact generators of \(\mathcal A\) are dualizable even though its unit need not be compact. All coefficients are colimits of those generators. Continuity of both sides extends the mate to all \(a\). Its unit, associativity and higher comparisons are the same adjunction mates of the \(\mathcal A\)-linear inclusion. Their diagrams commute before taking mates and therefore afterwards, with their triangle maps. This proves full module linearity.

3.594. Full coefficient extension and the remaining geometric test

Let \(\mathcal T\) be any presentable \(\mathcal A\)-module category. Tensor the entire continuous \(\mathcal A\)-linear adjunction ERP.19 over \(\mathcal A\) by \(\mathcal T\). Its units, counits and triangle maps descend through the balanced bar. The unit remains an equivalence, so \[ j_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal C\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T \hookrightarrow\mathcal N\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T, \quad j_{\mathcal T}\dashv r_{\mathcal T},\quad r_{\mathcal T}j_{\mathcal T}\simeq\operatorname{Id}. \tag{ERP.21} \] In particular the inclusion is full, and its right adjoint is continuous. Its actual orthogonal localization is \[ \begin{gathered} \ell_{\mathcal T}F =\operatorname{Cofib}(j_{\mathcal T}r_{\mathcal T}F\longrightarrow F),\\ \operatorname{im}\ell_{\mathcal T} =(\operatorname{im}j_{\mathcal T})^\perp,\qquad \ker\ell_{\mathcal T}=\operatorname{im}j_{\mathcal T}. \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.22} \] Applying \(r_{\mathcal T}\) to the triangle gives zero on its last term by the adjunction triangle. Equivalently all maps from the full image to that term vanish. For an orthogonal target, mapping the triangle into it identifies maps from \(\ell_{\mathcal T}F\) with maps from \(F\). This proves the localization adjunction, its unit and its image and kernel statements.

These comparisons persist under abstract scalar extension. If \(K/\mathbf C\) is any field and \(\mathcal V_K=\mathcal V\otimes_{\mathbf C}\operatorname{Vect}_K\), then \[ \begin{gathered} (\mathcal C\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T)_K \simeq\mathcal C_K\otimes_{\mathcal A_K}\mathcal T_K,\\ (j_{\mathcal T},r_{\mathcal T},\ell_{\mathcal T})_K =(j_{\mathcal T_K},r_{\mathcal T_K},\ell_{\mathcal T_K}). \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.23} \] Associative scalar tensor and the full balanced bar prove the first comparison: its terms, faces and realizations are the same after extension. Tensoring the actual triangle proves the second. In particular a right-orthogonal object remains right-orthogonal to the extended image. This does not identify \(\mathcal C_K\) with every regular nilpotent object on the geometrically extended curve.

Here is a precise sufficient geometric assertion for equality with the full Hecke-lisse category. For every original stage \(E\) and field extension \(K/\mathbf C\), require actual geometric realizations of the extended enhanced category and its point adjunction, compatible with \(P_E,J_E\) and operator scalar extension. Require, for every \(K\)-rational bundle point \(y\), \[ P_{E,K}\delta_y^! \in\operatorname{im}(\mathcal C_E)_K . \tag{ERP.24} \] This is a condition on all the new geometric points, not merely base changes of the original detectors.

Under these additional hypotheses take \(F\in\mathcal N_E\) right-orthogonal to \(\mathcal C_E\). ERP.23 and the point adjunction make every \(y^!J_{E,K}F_K\) vanish. A nonzero underlying object has a nonzero smooth affine chart restriction. FE.1–FE.12 chooses a residue-field extension and a closed rational chart point with nonzero derived fibre. Composition of inverse images identifies this with the corresponding bundle-point test; the required geometric point adjunction retains its stabilizer and shift. This contradicts the vanishing. Thus \(J_EF=0\), and its conservativity gives \(F=0\). ERP.22 then gives equality of the stages. Their actual forgetful images generate \(\mathcal N\) by ESG.28, so the additional hypotheses imply \[ \mathcal C_E=\mathcal N_E\text{ for all }E \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal C=\mathcal N . \tag{ERP.25} \] The actual geometric point adjunction and operator comparisons are GFP.25–GFP.44; GFP.49–GFP.52 prove the membership in ERP.24. Equality with the independently defined category of all nilpotent cohomological support also retains its separate arbitrary-input and supported-generation requirements. The genus-zero torsion problem of PAC.32–PAC.34 is unchanged. The field-extension strategy is discussed in Arinkin–Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Raskin–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky, §20.9; the adjunction, generator, linearity and coefficient-extension arguments used above are proved here.

Figure 3.72. The action comparison is ERP.2–ERP.4. Full module lifts and compact point generators are ERP.5–ERP.17. The adjunction and full coefficient extension are ERP.18–ERP.23. The dashed arrow is the proved change of field in Exercise 3.HL. The brown final statement gives the geometric membership ERP.24 and its proof GFP.49–GFP.52; abstract scalar extension alone does not supply it.

3.595. Exercise and solution: a nonformal thickened stage

Exercise 3.HK. Let \(R=\mathbf C[t]\), let \(\mathcal C\subset D(R)\) be the full category with \(t\)-power-torsion cohomology, and put \(A_2=R/(t^2)\), \(k=R/(t)\). Compute the continuous right adjoint of the inclusion. Compute \(A_2\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k\) as an actual \(A_2\)-module complex, and decide whether it is the direct sum of its cohomology modules.

Solution 3.HK. Flat localization and its fibre give \[ r_R(F)=\operatorname{Fib}(F\longrightarrow F[t^{-1}]),\qquad r_R(R)=(R[t^{-1}]/R)[-1]. \tag{ERP.26} \] The localization of the fibre is zero. If a complex \(c\) has torsion cohomology, then its localization is zero. Conversely flat localization tests this condition on all cohomology modules. Restriction of scalars identifies maps into a localized module with maps from the localized source. Thus maps from \(c\) into \(F[t^{-1}]\) vanish in every degree, and its fibre represents exactly maps from \(c\) into \(F\). This proves the adjunction. The formula is continuous, since localization and finite stable limits preserve colimits.

The fractions \(t^{-n}R/R\) are \(R/(t^n)\), with transition multiplication by \(t\). Therefore \[ R[t^{-1}]/R=\operatorname*{colim}_{n\ge1}R/(t^n),\qquad \mathcal C=\operatorname{Loc}\{k\}. \tag{ERP.27} \] Each quotient has a finite filtration by \(k\). Tensor the fibre formula for \(R\) with an arbitrary free-module bar for \(F\). It identifies \(r_R(F)=r_R(R)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F\), so its image lies in \(\operatorname{Loc}\{k\}\). On a torsion complex it is the identity, proving the equality. The two-term free resolution of \(k\) proves its compactness in \(D(R)\), hence in \(\mathcal C\).

Every \(A_2\)-module is already supported at \(t=0\), so the full action-bar comparison identifies \(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_2}(\mathcal C)=D(A_2)\). The same resolution gives the actual enhanced object \[ A_2\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k=[A_2\xrightarrow{\,t\,}A_2], \quad\text{degrees }-1,0,\qquad H^{-1}=k,\quad H^0=k . \tag{ERP.28} \] Its differential is nonzero. This finite free \(A_2\)-complex is compact. It is not isomorphic in \(D(A_2)\) to \(k[1]\oplus k\). Indeed the free resolution \[ \cdots\xrightarrow{t}A_2\xrightarrow{t}A_2 \xrightarrow{t}A_2\longrightarrow k,\qquad \operatorname{Ext}_{A_2}^n(k,k)=k\quad(n\ge0) \tag{ERP.29} \] is exact before its augmentation because \(\ker(t:A_2\to A_2)=tA_2=\operatorname{im}t\). Applying Hom into \(k\) gives zero differentials and the displayed Ext groups. A compact \(A_2\)-module is a retract of a finite free cell complex, by the same finite-bar argument as ERP.17. Its Hom into degree-zero \(k\) is bounded, so \(k\) is not compact. If ERP.28 split as the indicated cohomology sum, its retract \(k\) would be compact, a contradiction. Retaining the enhanced module and its actual differential is essential.

3.596. Exercise and solution: two normal directions and a new field point

Exercise 3.HL. On \(\mathbf A^2_{x,y}\), put \[ \begin{gathered} V=\mathbf C^2,\quad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z}(\mathbf C(x)[y]\otimes V)[2m],\\ \partial_x f=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x},\qquad \partial_y f=\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+yJf . \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.30} \] Verify the operator relations. Compare all original closed-point tests with the test at \((u,0)\) after \(K=\mathbf C(u)\), where \(u\) is transcendental and the operators kill \(K\).

Solution 3.HL. The extra matrix term commutes with multiplication by \(y\), so the two coordinate Weyl commutators are identities. The cross commutators vanish: \(J\) is constant and \(yJ\) is independent of \(x\). These actions therefore define a left operator module on every summand.

For \((a,b)\in\mathbf C^2\), the point Hom is the cochain Koszul complex on \(x-a,y-b\). Multiplication by \(x-a\) is invertible. With \(e_x,e_y\) the cochain basis its actual contraction is \[ d=(x-a)e_x\wedge+(y-b)e_y\wedge,\qquad h=(x-a)^{-1}\iota_{e_x},\qquad dh+hd=1 . \tag{ERP.31} \] The identity follows from \(e_x\wedge\iota_{e_x}+\iota_{e_x}e_x\wedge=1\) and anticommutation with \(e_y\wedge\). All original closed-point tests thus vanish.

Write \(S=\mathbf C[x]\setminus\{0\}\). After field extension the coefficient ring is \(S^{-1}K[x,y]\). Evaluation at \(x=u,y=0\) survives localization since every \(s(u)\) is nonzero. The sequence \(x-u,y\) is regular: its first term is nonzero in this domain, and its quotient is \(K[y]\), where the second term is injective. The finite cochain Koszul complex consequently gives \[ \begin{gathered} \Delta_{(u,0)} =D_{\mathbf A^2_K}/\bigl(D_{\mathbf A^2_K}(x-u)+D_{\mathbf A^2_K}y\bigr),\\ \operatorname{RHom}(\Delta_{(u,0)},M_K) \simeq\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z}K^2[\,2m-2\,]\ne0 . \end{gathered} \tag{ERP.32} \] The ordered coordinates \(x-u,y\) fix the normal determinant factor. The point resolution has only three cochain degrees, \(0,1,2\), so it commutes with this direct sum on both infinite tails. Its differential uses the two coordinate multiplications, not the connection coefficient \(yJ\). There is one copy of \(K^2\) in every even cohomological degree and none in odd degrees. This exact example explains why ERP.24 requires the new geometric points as well as the original ones.

3.597. The regular Hecke-lisse intersection in every genus

Let \(X/\mathbf C\) be a smooth projective connected curve, and let \(G\) be connected reductive. Every genus and bundle component is allowed. Use the full unbounded categories \[ \mathcal M=\operatorname{Dmod}(\operatorname{Bun}_G(X)),\qquad \mathcal N=\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}},\qquad \mathcal D=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap\mathcal N . \tag{GFP.1} \] The inclusion of \(\mathcal D\) preserves colimits. It is presentable: restrict HLA.13's small continuous obstruction family to the presentable \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Choose an uncountable regular cardinal for its generator presentation, all target presentations and the cell bounds of the images. These obstruction functors preserve compactness at that cardinal. The countable null-transition construction in §3.586 then gives a generating filtered system of kernel objects and its full small-relations bar. This proves presentability of this intersection without a support converse.

For \(d\in\mathcal D\), every Hecke output is regular Ind by HRI.16–HRI.19 and CDK.23. Since \(d\) is already Hecke-lisse, its actual curve coefficient is an object \(Z\in\mathcal M\otimes\mathscr I_X\). For compact \(E\in\mathscr I_X\), the actual coefficient test is \[ \begin{aligned} C_E(Z)&=(\operatorname{Id}\otimes\Gamma_{\mathscr I})(E^\vee\otimes Z),\\ C_E(Z)&\simeq p_{Y,+}\bigl(\operatorname{pr}_X^!i_!(E^\vee)\otimes^!J_Y^!(Z)\bigr)[-2], \qquad Y=\operatorname{Bun}_G(X). \end{aligned} \tag{GFP.2} \] These are PAC.29's actual maps and NTR.1–NTR.6's Spencer normalization. The chosen Hecke convention retains the coefficient shift after PAC.25; its unit test is \(p_{X,+}\omega_X=\Gamma_{\mathscr I}(\mathbf1)[2]\). Finite connection tensor and proper curve integration make this test regular Ind. It belongs to \(\mathcal N\) by HLA.16, since the same proper integral is a full Ran parameter action, up to the displayed fixed shift. Thus every compact test lies in \(\mathcal D\). Reindex by \(P=E^\vee\); duality permutes the compact objects. The continuous pairing in \(P\), colimit closure and HLA.17–HLA.18 give \[ Z\in\mathcal D\otimes\mathscr I_X,\qquad \Phi_\psi(\vec V,N;d)\in\mathcal D \quad(N\in\operatorname{Dmod}(X^J)). \tag{GFP.3} \] For several coordinates use the actual HLA.14–HLA.16 exchange, collision and unit maps and successive compact tests. An arbitrary full operator parameter contracts only the independent connection factors; it leaves \(\mathcal D\) as the first factor. Fullness lifts all comparison maps. This proves the full unital Ran action on \(\mathcal D\).

The continuous Ran section of UID.2–UID.6 and the normalized RSE.36/NTR.14 comparison give \[ \Psi(a,d)\simeq\Phi(\mathsf D(a),d),\quad L\mathsf D(a)\simeq a, \qquad \mathcal D\text{ is a unital }\mathcal A\text{-module}, \quad \mathcal A=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z_H^{\mathrm{restr}}(X)). \tag{GFP.4} \] Its unit and higher maps are inherited from \(\mathcal N\). No equality of \(\mathscr Q_X\) and \(\mathscr I_X\) is used.

3.598. Enhanced generators and the actual orthogonal triangle

Use the original finite equivariant Koszul stages \(K_E\) and \(\mathcal T_E\) of ESG.18–ESG.24. The full action-bar argument ERP.5–ERP.8, applied to GFP.4, gives \[ \mathcal D_E=\operatorname{Mod}_{K_E}(\mathcal D) \simeq\mathcal D\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T_E \hookrightarrow \mathcal N_E=\mathcal N\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal T_E . \tag{GFP.5} \] This inclusion is full and preserves colimits. Its image consists exactly of modules whose actual underlying object is in \(\mathcal D\). The two finite-stage adjunctions retain the actual perfect dual, determinant factor and shifts. The module forgetful functor is conservative and has a continuous right adjoint.

ESG.33 makes \(T_E m=J_EP_E m\) regular for every regular input; ESG.17 puts it in \(\mathcal N\). Hence the intrinsic SPT compact points have actual enhanced lifts in \(\mathcal D_E\). RHC.34–RHC.36 gives independent nilpotent support for every object of \(\mathcal D\). The fixed NC.4–NC.7 point family therefore detects it. The enhanced adjunction identifies all Hom tests from the lifted points with those point fibres. Conservativity of the forgetful functor proves \[ \begin{gathered} Q_{E,i}=P_E\delta_{y_i}^!\in\mathcal D_E^c\cap\mathcal N_E^c,\\ \mathcal D_E=\operatorname{Loc}\{Q_{E,i}\},\qquad \mathcal D=\operatorname{Loc}\{J_E^{\mathcal D}Q_{E,i}:E,i\}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.6} \] The first compactness follows from the full enhanced adjunction and continuity of \(J_E\); restriction through the full continuous inclusion preserves it. The last generators are compact both in \(\mathcal D\) and in \(\mathcal N\), by the finite-stage continuous right adjoints. These are exactly the ERP.12–ERP.17 arguments; here the independent support implication is needed only on \(\mathcal D\), where regularity is part of its definition.

The full compact coend and its actual evaluation give \[ j:\mathcal D\hookrightarrow\mathcal N,\quad j\dashv r,\qquad r(n)=\int^{d\in\mathcal D^c} d\otimes\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal N}(jd,n), \quad rj\simeq\operatorname{Id}. \tag{GFP.7} \] Compactness of the images in \(\mathcal N\) makes \(r\) continuous. For a dualizable coefficient, its adjunction mate is the dual evaluation comparison of ERP.20. SDU.1–SDU.3's dualizable compact generators and continuity extend that mate to every coefficient, with its full module coherences. Thus \(r\) is \(\mathcal A\)-linear. Tensoring the entire adjunction with a coefficient module and a field extension retains the unit, counit and triangles. In particular \[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal D_{E,K}\hookrightarrow\mathcal N_{E,K} \text{ is full},\\ j_{E,K}r_{E,K}F\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\ell_{E,K}F,\qquad \operatorname{im}\ell_{E,K}=(\operatorname{im}j_{E,K})^\perp , \quad K/\mathbf C . \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.8} \] All three functors are continuous, and the last object is the actual cofiber of the counit. This uses ERP.21–ERP.23's balanced bar proof, not an adjunction assigned to the nonunital idempotent.

3.599. Characteristic support under arbitrary field extension

Let \(U/k\) be smooth affine of finite type in characteristic zero, and let \(K/k\) be any field extension. KF.8 is the actual identity \[ D(U_K)=D(U)\otimes_kK,\qquad H^m(M\otimes_kK)=H^m(M)\otimes_kK . \tag{GFP.9} \] A good filtration on a coherent module extends to a good filtration. Exact field tensor preserves its pieces, quotients and associated graded module. Thus its characteristic support is the extended closed support. Containment in an extended closed cone is reflected as well: localization of the symbol module at a complementary principal open commutes with field tensor, and a nonzero localization stays nonzero under faithful extension.

The coherent submodules of an extended cohomology module need not be free extensions of old submodules. The required statement is instead \[ \begin{gathered} A\subset H^m(M_K)\text{ coherent} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A\subset B\otimes_kK\subset H^m(M_K),\\ B\subset H^m(M)\text{ coherent over }D(U). \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.10} \] Choose finitely many generators of \(A\). Each is a finite \(K\)-linear combination of old cohomology vectors. Their finitely many old vectors generate a coherent \(D(U)\)-submodule \(B\), by operator Noetherianity. Its exact scalar extension contains the chosen generators and hence \(A\). The characteristic Serre submodule rule puts \(\operatorname{Ch}(A)\) inside \(\operatorname{Ch}(B)_K\). Conversely an old coherent submodule remains an actual submodule after faithful field tensor. Consequently, for every closed conical \(\Lambda\), \[ \operatorname{SS}_\infty(M)\subset\Lambda \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(M_K)\subset\Lambda_K . \tag{GFP.11} \] This proves both directions on arbitrary unbounded complexes.

There is also a statement for an arbitrary internal \(K\)-module whose underlying object is supported over \(k\). Its finite \(D(U_K)\)-submodule generators lie in a finite old submodule \(B\); the internal \(K\)-action gives the same quotient from \(B\otimes K\). Apply this on all bundle charts. The global nilpotent equations and their chart pullbacks extend by the same invariant-polynomial equations for the Higgs field, including its central part. Hence \[ c\in\mathcal D_K=\operatorname{Mod}_K(\mathcal D) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(c)\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G,K} \text{ on the actual }Y_K . \tag{GFP.12} \] Smooth transfer, its relative shifts and the half-line comparisons are the actual KF.8–KF.9 comparisons. No assertion that a new coherent submodule itself descends has entered the proof.

3.600. The original fixed detectors over the new field

The finite FD.2 stratification of each original nilpotent chart remains smooth with its closed filtration and conormal fibre bounds after \(K/\mathbf C\). Its connected strata stay connected. Here is a direct proof of this last assertion in the needed scope. For a finite affine cover, flat field tensor commutes with the kernel computing global sections, giving \[ \Gamma(S_K,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O)\otimes_{\mathbf C}K . \tag{GFP.13} \] Suppose a nontrivial idempotent existed on the right. Its finitely many coefficient functions, their products and the unit span a finite-dimensional complex vector space. The equation \(e^2=e\) is a finite polynomial system for its \(K\)-valued coefficients. Choose a nonzero coordinate of \(e\) and of \(e-1\) and adjoin their inverses. This finite-type complex algebra has a \(K\)-point, so is nonzero; the weak Nullstellensatz gives a complex point. That point supplies a nontrivial idempotent on \(S\), contradicting connectedness. Thus \[ S\text{ connected over }\mathbf C \quad\Longrightarrow\quad S_K\text{ connected}. \tag{GFP.14} \] The argument needs no finite generation of the entire section algebra.

FD.6–FD.12 is an algebraic characteristic-zero proof. On the selected stratum, every coherent zero-symbol submodule and the relevant quotients are finite flat connections. Their unions are flat. The normal point Koszul resolution has only finitely many columns, so its cohomology computation is valid in every degree. The same original point on the connected extended stratum detects it. The finite closed filtration and supported Kashiwara comparison therefore give \[ \operatorname{SS}_\infty(M)\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G,K},\qquad (y_i)_K^!M=0\ \forall i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad M=0 . \tag{GFP.15} \] Use NC.4–NC.7's finite chart family on each bounded open and then its cofinal exhaustion. Composition of inverse images retains the relative shift and invertible fibre line in every chart-point test. The cone of a supported morphism is supported, so the same proof gives \[ \begin{gathered} ((y_i)_K^!f\text{ are all equivalences}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f\text{ is an equivalence},\\ f\text{ a morphism in the nilpotent-supported category}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.16} \] These are tests on this fixed support, not tests on arbitrary operator objects.

3.601. The exact supported image in an extended enhanced stage

The original enhanced adjunction and the original point object extend with all their maps. Compactness of the point makes its Hom functor continuous, and its free internal field-module bar identifies this extension with the actual inverse-transfer point test. For every \(F\in\mathcal N_{E,K}\), \[ \operatorname{RHom}_{\mathcal N_{E,K}} ((P_E\delta_{y_i}^!)_K,F) \simeq (y_i)_K^!J_{E,K}F . \tag{GFP.17} \] Only extensions of the original points occur in this formula. New point adjunctions will be constructed below.

Suppose the actual \(J_{E,K}F\) has nilpotent cohomological support. In GFP.8 the first term has that support by GFP.12; the middle term has it by hypothesis. The support Serre rule and triangles give \[ \operatorname{SS}_\infty(J_{E,K}\ell_{E,K}F) \subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G,K}. \tag{GFP.18} \] Orthogonality of the last term makes all GFP.17 tests vanish. GFP.15 kills its underlying object. The actual \(K_E\)-module forgetful functor \(J_{E,K}^{\mathcal N}\) is conservative, so \[ \ell_{E,K}F=0,\qquad F\in\mathcal D_{E,K}. \tag{GFP.19} \] The converse is GFP.12. We have proved the full essential-image criterion \[ F\in\mathcal D_{E,K} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(J_{E,K}F)\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G,K}, \qquad F\in\mathcal N_{E,K}. \tag{GFP.20} \] This theorem has no regular-input assumption over \(K\). It concerns the scalar-extended original enhanced stage, and uses the actual counit triangle and all cohomological degrees.

3.602. Countable fields and perfect stabilizer cochains

Every countable characteristic-zero field embeds in \(\mathbf C\). To see this, choose a transcendence basis, which is at most countable. Recursively choose algebraically independent complex numbers: the algebraic closure of the field generated by the preceding countable set is countable, whereas \(\mathbf C\) is uncountable. Map the basis to these numbers. Enumerate the remaining algebraic generators and extend the embedding successively by roots in the algebraically closed complex field. Thus \[ k_0\text{ countable, }\operatorname{char}k_0=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf C . \tag{GFP.21} \] The chosen embedding need not agree with another realization of a common countable subfield.

Let \(A/k_0\) be smooth affine of finite type. Its actual de Rham form complex commutes with field extension, since affine sections, forms and their differential do. After a complex embedding SPT.7 makes its cohomology bounded finite dimensional. Exact faithful field tensor reflects that statement. Consequently \[ C_A=R\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Dmod}(A)}(\omega_A,\omega_A) \text{ is perfect over }k_0,\qquad B_A=C_A^\vee . \tag{GFP.22} \] The normalization is the same Spencer normalization as SPT.7. For any further field \(L/k_0\), a finite perfect representative gives \[ C_{A_L}=C_A\otimes_{k_0}L,\qquad B_{A_L}\simeq B_A\otimes_{k_0}L . \tag{GFP.23} \] This is derived perfect duality; it does not tensor a raw infinite linear dual of the form complex.

The finite Spencer Hom calculation, group multiplication, identity and inversion retain the complete Hopf maps. SPT.8–SPT.13's full action and groupoid mapping bars therefore apply over \(k_0\). Their extra-unit contraction gives the actual equivalence and free point \[ \operatorname{Dmod}(BA)=\operatorname{Mod}_{B_A},\quad q^!=\operatorname{oblv},\qquad q_!k_0=B_A,\quad q_!\dashv q^! . \tag{GFP.24} \] All limits in the mapping bar remain their full totalizations. The Hopf inversion identity supplies invertible groupoid transports. Both tensor duality and the contracted free-module bar commute with the field extensions in GFP.23.

3.603. Intrinsic point adjunctions over the countable model

Let the curve, group and a rational bundle point be defined over a countable characteristic-zero field \(k_0\). Use a bounded framed quotient \(U=[Z/H_0]\) containing the point, where \(H_0\) is a product of general linear groups. A frame exists over the field. The stabilizer \(A\) is smooth: SPT.1–SPT.3's formal-group proof uses only characteristic zero. Its smooth orbit is locally closed by the same orbit and Jacobian argument after an algebraic closure, followed by faithful descent. Thus \[ y:\operatorname{pt}\xrightarrow{q}BA \xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}Y \tag{GFP.25} \] has the actual locally closed residual-gerbe factorization. The group point object is GFP.24.

On a smooth target chart extend this coefficient by finite normal transfer and by coherent duality for the open part: \[ (j_0)_!F=\mathbb D_T(j_0)_*\mathbb D_{T_0}F . \tag{GFP.26} \] Here ordinary open direct image is its finite affine Čech localization complex. These models commute with field extension. After a complex embedding they are the SPT.17–SPT.24 bounded regular objects. Bounded coherence descends: cohomology commutes with faithful field tensor, and finitely many generators after extension are finite sums of old vectors. Those vectors generate before extension, since the quotient tensors to zero. Operator Noetherianity supplies coherence of the relations. Boundedness is reflected degree by degree.

The finite filtered resolution of Holonomic D-modules and duality, Lemma 3.0 uses the regular symbol ring and works in characteristic zero. It makes every bounded coherent coefficient locally a finite operator-projective complex. Coherent duals therefore commute with field extension. Biduality, the ordinary open adjunction and the finite normal adjunction give SPT.18–SPT.19 on coherent targets. The full compact generator bar extends the same maps to every unbounded target.

The canonical smooth-base-change mates are isomorphisms after the complex embedding, by the SPT comparison. Their cones vanish before extension by faithfulness. Their higher compositions are the same adjunction-mate identities. Strong operator descent therefore glues the point object and its full adjunction: \[ \delta_{y,k_0}^!=j_!i_!q_!k_0,\qquad \operatorname{RHom}_{Y}(\delta_{y,k_0}^!,M)\simeq y^!M \quad(M\text{ arbitrary}). \tag{GFP.27} \] This descent takes the limit of compatible mapping complexes; no individual infinite mapping product is tensored with a field. The represented inverse image is continuous on charts, so this point object is compact. The perfect group dual, finite normal transfer, finite open Čech model and coherent dual all extend. Thus, for every \(L/k_0\), \[ (\delta_{y,k_0}^!)_L\simeq\delta_{y_L,L}^!, \qquad \operatorname{RHom}(\delta_{y_L,L}^!,M_L)\simeq y_L^!M_L . \tag{GFP.28} \] Two models represent the same point functor and are identified, with all their maps, by enriched Yoneda. The same construction applies to the specified half twist with its actual fibre line.

3.604. Actual enhanced operator extension

For the finite quotient stage \(Z_E=[\operatorname{Spec}K_E/H]\), the affine Hopf nerve and its full module categories commute with categorical field extension. Apply KF.3 and KF.7 to their coordinate algebras and compatible maps. Hence \[ \operatorname{QCoh}(Z_E)\otimes\operatorname{Vect}_L \simeq\operatorname{QCoh}((Z_E)_L). \tag{GFP.29} \] The same PBW, transfer and strong smooth-descent argument is KF.8–KF.9 for \(\mathcal M\). The finite-set Ran diagram uses these actual operator transfers and the Hopf coefficient categories. Its colimit commutes with categorical scalar extension. KG.19–KG.23 is a characteristic-zero construction; its finite duality maps and regular algebra therefore extend with their adjunction maps.

The quotient stage unit is compact. To check this over a model field, its Hom is rational reductive invariants of the underlying module. Exactness descends from a complex embedding: a lift of an invariant vector uses finitely many vectors, whose coactions give a finite linear system over the original field; a complex solution gives a solution there by Gaussian elimination. The common countable model also retains the normalized rational Reynolds integral: its values on the countable Hopf basis are countably many coefficients. Its two invariance identities and normalization are coefficientwise identities over that field. Inserting it in the full rational cobar gives the actual GSL.5–GSL.6 contraction, including unbounded complexes. Invariants commute with direct sums, so this is the continuous full functor. Compactness and the internal field-module bar then identify \[ (\Gamma_{Z_E})_L =\Gamma_{(Z_E)_L},\qquad \Gamma_{Z_E}=\operatorname{RHom}(\mathbf1,-). \tag{GFP.30} \] On free scalar extensions this is compact Hom commuting with field tensor. The split free bar gives it on all objects.

Let \(f:\mathcal R\to\mathcal T_E\) be the actual coefficient functor. The enhanced algebra, free module functor and integration are \[ \begin{gathered} K_f=(\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal R}\otimes f)R_{\mathcal R},\qquad P_f=F_{K_f}(-\boxtimes\mathbf1),\\ J_f=(\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal M}\otimes\Gamma_{Z_E}) \operatorname{oblv}_{K_f}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.31} \] Full algebra-action bars and GFP.29–GFP.30 give their actual geometric extensions, including units, counits, action maps and every derived transformation. In particular the point adjunctions and operator composite are \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{RHom}(P_{f,L}\delta_y^!,F)\simeq y^!J_{f,L}F,\\ (J_fP_f)_L=J_{f,L}P_{f,L}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.32} \] For the original stage, ESG.13 and ESG.26 identify this with the scalar-extended \(\mathcal N_E\) and its conservative actual module forgetful functor. This statement does not identify every local system over \(L\) with a scalar extension of an old one.

3.605. Compact universal coefficients on the finite stage

For a finite representation \(V\), let \(\mathcal E_E(V)\) be the actual stage coefficient of BLI.16. The finite CW model of RBC.1–RBC.5 identifies it with a \(\mathcal T_E\)-valued local system. Its stalk at the chosen point is the tautological finite bundle \[ \mathcal E_E(V)|_x=K_E\otimes V\in\mathcal T_E^c . \tag{GFP.33} \] Compactness is ESG.18–ESG.24: its Hom is rational invariants of the finite-representation dual tensored with the underlying module. All stalks are equivalent compact objects.

A local system with compact stalks on a finite CW complex is compact in the full functor category. Attach its finitely many cells. Functors on a cell pushout form a pullback of functor categories; the mapping complex is the corresponding finite fibre of the mapping complexes on the old skeleton, the cell and its sphere. On a contractible cell it is Hom from a compact stalk. Induct on dimension for the attaching spheres and then on the number of cells. Finite fibres commute with colimits of complexes. Thus \[ \operatorname{Map}(\mathcal E_E(V),\operatorname{colim}F_\alpha) \simeq\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Map}(\mathcal E_E(V),F_\alpha) \quad\text{in }\operatorname{Fun}(K_{\mathrm{CW}},\mathcal T_E). \tag{GFP.34} \] The compactly generated \(\mathcal T_E\) is categorically dualizable. Tensor by it preserves the local-system category limit, and RBC.4's full continuous embedding remains full after this tensor. Consequently \(\mathcal E_E(V)\) is compact in \(\mathcal T_E\otimes\mathscr I_X\). The full finite-cell bar then gives \[ \mathcal E_E(V)\in \operatorname{Thick}\{t_a\boxtimes L_b: t_a\in\mathcal T_E^c,\ L_b\in\mathscr L_X\}. \tag{GFP.35} \] Only finitely many of these objects occur for a fixed \(V\). Here \(\mathscr L_X\) is the actual bounded finite-connection operator category, not a set of monodromy isomorphism classes.

Retain an actual finite-cell retract presentation \(\mathcal P_V\) and the entire equivalence to the coefficient. In full resolved DG models this includes closed maps and homotopies \[ u:\mathcal P_V\rightleftarrows\mathcal E_E(V):v,\qquad dh_0=vu-\operatorname{id},\qquad dh_1=uv-\operatorname{id}. \tag{GFP.36} \] For a split retract retain its idempotent and splitting maps as well. Its finite free bar is a countable model for the splitting. This keeps the coefficient and its specified maps, including the normalized finite-projective fibre.

3.606. A countable model retaining the entire coherent functor

Choose split forms of \(G\) and \(H\) over a characteristic-zero prime-field model and their given complex identifications. The compact representation category has a countable skeleton: finite graded sums of the highest-weight irreducibles. Its matrix Hom spaces have finite bases in each relevant degree. There are countably many labels, finite tuples and coherence cells. Choose GFP.35–GFP.36 for each representation in this skeleton. Then there is a countable subfield \[ \begin{gathered} k_0\subset\mathbf C,\quad \text{with models of }X,G,H,K_E,\mathcal E_E\\ \text{and every specified tensor and action comparison}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.37} \] Here is the full countability argument. Compact stage objects have finite perfect equivariant models over the finite-cell framed algebra, by SDU.1–SDU.3 and ESG.18–ESG.24. Each bounded finite connection has a finite affine cover with finite bundle and connection matrices. Affine coordinate and operator algebras have countable algebraic bases. Their free module resolutions, Čech models and rational group action bars have countably many cells. A chosen map or higher homotopy is a column-finite countable matrix on those models, or a sequence of these matrices in the countable bar directions. It uses at most countably many complex coefficients. Compositions are finite on each column or finite bar word.

Retain the maps, their inverses and all higher cells, at every finite arity. Each fixed column identity is a finite equation of the form \[ \sum_{\nu=1}^{r}\epsilon_\nu a_{\nu,1}\cdots a_{\nu,s_\nu}=0, \qquad \epsilon_\nu\in\{1,-1\}, \tag{GFP.38} \] with the actual graded signs; differential terms are included. Take the field generated by all coefficients of this countable collection of data. A field generated by countably many elements over \(\mathbf Q\) is countable. The equations hold there because its inclusion into \(\mathbf C\) is injective. Explicit inverse and homotopy witnesses retain equivalences, rather than only cohomological identifications.

This also covers finite-cell retracts and transformations: include their splitting maps, homotopies and all their coherent relations before taking the coefficient field. A finite perfect module or map descends by its finite projective matrices and their idempotent equations. The countable union here retains the whole infinite coherent diagram. The finite-object statement is also recorded in the Stacks Project, Lemma 0BC7.

For any embedding \(\sigma:k_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf C\), the connection models remain bounded finite connections on the conjugate projective curve. The finite external presentations and all their retained comparisons give the actual coherent functor \[ \mathcal E_\sigma: \operatorname{Rep}(H_\sigma) \longrightarrow\mathcal T_\sigma\otimes\mathscr I_{X_\sigma}. \tag{GFP.39} \] Its tensor, unit and higher maps are the specified extended maps. Their full inclusions are faithful on transformation complexes, so the maps lift uniquely with their relations. The remaining representation objects and maps are supplied by the continuous full representation bar. Arbitrary scalar matrices are obtained by scalar extension, not by independent choices of their images.

For the original embedding, these data recover \(\mathcal E_E\) with its full scalar action. The normalized coefficient evaluation and finite-set folds therefore give \[ f_0:\mathcal R_{X_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal T_0,\qquad (f_0)_{\mathbf C}=f_E,\qquad (f_0)_L \text{ is its actual extended coefficient functor}. \tag{GFP.40} \] The construction uses the proper diagonal pairing and NTR's transpose, including the empty-coordinate unit. At the level of full categories, the comparison is GFP.29–GFP.32 and the split field-module bar. No claim that tensoring an individual infinite product of vector spaces preserves that product is used.

3.607. The conjugate kernels are the actual IC kernels

The source action also has a common countable model. There are countably many dominant labels and finite fusion strings. The bundle charts can be chosen from the finite framed Quot atlases indexed by integer degree and section bounds in §1.15. There are countably many such bounds and bundle components. Choose a finite affine cover at each bound; their nerves and finite-labelled correspondences are a countable family. Further chart comparisons are the actual transfer base changes. For each finite IC coefficient retain its smooth ambient, constant open-stratum normalization and algebraic intermediate-extension construction. On an open ambient \(T_0\) containing its smooth support stratum, let \(v\) be the closed stratum inclusion and \(j_0:T_0\hookrightarrow T\). The operator middle extension is \[ \operatorname{IC}_Z= \operatorname{im}\bigl( H^0(j_0)_!v_+\mathcal O_U \longrightarrow H^0(j_0)_*v_+\mathcal O_U\bigr), \tag{GFP.41} \] with the given dimension and density convention. This formula is made in the supported smooth ambient.

The closed transfer and ordinary open Čech functor are defined over the coefficient field. Their bounded coherence descends from the original complex realization as in GFP.26. Coherent duality is computed locally by the finite operator resolutions, so it commutes with field extension. Flat extension is exact on cohomology modules and images. Thus \[ ((j_0)_!F)_L=(j_{0,L})_!(F_L),\qquad (\operatorname{im}\alpha)_L=\operatorname{im}(\alpha_L) \tag{GFP.42} \] for these actual coherent coefficients and their canonical maps. The comparison includes the adjunction units and counits.

After any complex embedding, GFP.41 is therefore the ordinary complex operator middle extension of the same normalized constant connection. The strict intermediate-extension characterization identifies it with the genuine IC object: \[ (\operatorname{IC}_Z)_\sigma =\operatorname{IC}_{Z_\sigma}. \tag{GFP.43} \] This can also be checked in the full coherent target category: the two middle extensions inject into the same ordinary direct image and are the image of the same extraordinary-to-ordinary map. Their restrictions are the fixed constant coefficient, and their kernels and cokernels have no boundary subquotients. No assumption that an arbitrary holonomic object is regular is used. This specific coefficient is the regular middle extension.

Include all finite kernel maps, inverse comparisons and higher fusion strings in the countable matrix collection of GFP.38. They remain coherent maps on the same actual geometric correspondences under every embedding. For the conjugate complex realization their unintegrated Hecke transforms have the normalized IC kernels GFP.43. Their source group labels and all integer shifts are unchanged. The half-root is its modeled line with the given square and fibre evaluations. The full regular algebra and action bars consequently give \[ \begin{gathered} (T_0)_L=J_{f_0,L}P_{f_0,L},\qquad (T_0)_{\mathbf C}=T_E,\\ (T_0)_\sigma \text{ acts through the genuine}\\ \text{conjugate IC Hecke transforms}. \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.44} \] This is a comparison of the constructed maps and coherent bars, not a choice of unrelated isomorphisms on their cohomology.

3.608. A compact-unit restricted coefficient operator

Let \(\mathcal T\) be a compactly generated complex symmetric monoidal coefficient category with compact unit and an actual continuous strong tensor coefficient functor \(\operatorname{Rep}(H)\to\mathcal T\otimes\mathscr I_X\). Use its normalized Ran coefficient functor \(f\). The full kernel presentation and its actual transition maps are \[ K_f=(\operatorname{Id}\otimes f)R_{\mathcal R} =\operatorname*{colim}_{\psi\in\Xi} (j_\psi\otimes\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal T})B_{\psi,f}. \tag{GFP.45} \] This is CDK.9–CDK.14 with the given coefficient functor. The representation kernel is the full finite-representation coend; the curve kernel is \(\Delta_*\omega\). The proper diagonal duality triangle recovers the coefficient itself, with NTR's actual curve-coordinate shifts.

Ordinary \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=\operatorname{RHom}(\mathbf1,-)\) is continuous here by compactness of the unit. It passes through the entire kernel colimit, including the action faces, and gives \[ \overline B_{\psi,f} \in\operatorname{Rep}(H)^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathscr I_X^{\otimes J}, \qquad J_fP_f(m)=\operatorname*{colim}_{\psi} \Phi_\psi(\overline B_{\psi,f};m). \tag{GFP.46} \] These are the actual coefficient contractions of CDK.12–CDK.16. Finite representation and bounded finite-connection generators preserve chartwise regular inputs by CDK.17–CDK.24. Their full generator bars and the outer colimit preserve that property. Hence \[ J_fP_f(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}) \subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}} . \tag{GFP.47} \] This proof needs neither an affine map to the restricted stack nor a particular Koszul presentation of \(\mathcal T\).

The full enhanced algebra-action comparison BLI.19–BLI.21 gives the unintegrated Hecke coefficient in \(\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal T\otimes\mathscr I_X\). Continuous \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\) retains that coefficient. Thus every regular input satisfies \[ J_fP_f(m)\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}},\qquad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(J_fP_f(m))\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_G \quad(m\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}). \tag{GFP.48} \] The last implication is the necessary RHC.34–RHC.36 criterion on the now regular output. This proves the statement in every genus and for every compact-unit coefficient category with the displayed restricted functor and actual IC action.

3.609. The new geometric point belongs to the extended original stage

Let \(K/\mathbf C\) be arbitrary and let \(y\in Y_K(K)\). The bundle point has finite algebraic torsor data on a finite cover of the projective curve. Adjoin its finitely many new coordinates and the required constants to the countable model of GFP.37. The resulting subfield of \(K\) is still countable: \[ k_0\subset k_1\subset K,\qquad y=y_0\otimes_{k_1}K,\qquad \sigma:k_1\hookrightarrow\mathbf C . \tag{GFP.49} \] GFP.21 supplies the last embedding. It need not fix the original complex realization of \(k_0\), and no embedding of all of \(K\) into \(\mathbf C\) is required.

Construct the point object over \(k_1\) by GFP.25–GFP.28 and the actual stage operator by GFP.31 and GFP.40–GFP.44. Under \(\sigma\), the input is a genuine regular compact complex bundle point. GFP.39 retains the whole restricted coefficient functor, and GFP.43 retains the genuine IC kernels. GFP.47–GFP.48 therefore give \[ T_\sigma\delta_{y_\sigma}^!\in\mathcal M_{\sigma,\mathrm{reg}}, \qquad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(T_\sigma\delta_{y_\sigma}^!) \subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G_\sigma}. \tag{GFP.50} \] No regularity-descent assertion over \(K\) is needed.

GFP.11 reflects this characteristic-support containment to the countable model and preserves it to \(K\). The actual point and operator comparisons identify the resulting object exactly: \[ (T_0\delta_{y_0}^!)_K =J_{E,K}P_{E,K}\delta_y^!,\qquad \operatorname{SS}_\infty(J_{E,K}P_{E,K}\delta_y^!) \subset\operatorname{Nilp}_{G,K}. \tag{GFP.51} \] This argument is degreewise valid on arbitrary cohomological tails: field tensor is exact, and every finite witness is handled by GFP.10–GFP.11.

Apply the exact supported-image criterion GFP.20 inside the original extended enhanced stage. It proves \[ P_{E,K}\delta_y^!\in\mathcal D_{E,K} \qquad\text{for every }K/\mathbf C,\ y\in Y_K(K). \tag{GFP.52} \] This is membership in the scalar extension of the original regular Hecke-lisse stage. It does not replace that category by an unproved category of all newly defined regular objects over \(K\).

3.610. The full original-complex Hecke-lisse image is regular

Take \(F\in\mathcal N_E\) right-orthogonal to \(\mathcal D_E\). The actual continuous right-adjoint triangle of GFP.8 gives \[ F_K\in(\mathcal D_{E,K})^\perp \qquad\text{for every }K/\mathbf C . \tag{GFP.53} \] For every new rational bundle point GFP.52 and the actual enhanced point adjunction yield \[ 0=\operatorname{RHom}(P_{E,K}\delta_y^!,F_K) \simeq y^!J_{E,K}F_K . \tag{GFP.54} \] If \(J_EF\ne0\), choose a nonzero smooth affine chart restriction. FE.1–FE.12 detects its underlying nonzero complex at a closed rational point after a residue-field extension. Composition of inverse images identifies this with the corresponding bundle point test in GFP.54, retaining its relative shift, fibre line and stabilizer. The contradiction gives \(J_EF=0\). Conservativity gives \(F=0\).

The orthogonal localization has zero image, so GFP.8 gives equality of the full stages. Their actual forgetful images jointly generate by ESG.28. Consequently, in every genus, \[ \mathcal D_E=\mathcal N_E\text{ for every }E, \qquad \mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}} =\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}} . \tag{GFP.55} \] This is an original-field theorem on all unbounded objects. The generators GFP.6 are compact generators of the full Hecke-lisse category.

RSE.37–RSE.38 and NTR.16 identify the actual restricted Beilinson functor's full image with that category. RHC's necessary support implication now applies to every image object. Thus \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{EssIm}\Pi_{\mathrm r}=\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Hl}} \subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}},\\ \operatorname{SS}_\infty(\Pi_{\mathrm r}m)\subset\operatorname{Nilp}_G \qquad(m\in\mathcal M). \end{gathered} \tag{GFP.56} \] The input has no regularity, holonomicity or cohomological bound. No unit, counit or adjunction for the nonunital Ran algebra is inferred from this image theorem.

Equality with the independently defined category of all nilpotent cohomological support remains a separate converse. GFP.56 alone does not prove regularity of every such object, the unrestricted genus-zero cohomological converse, or AIC.17's full supported factorization. The completed projective-line coefficient remains distinct from the ind-connection category. Derived tempered Satake retains its separate requirements. For the field-point strategy see Arinkin–Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Raskin–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky, §20.9. The operator, point, support, common-model and orthogonality arguments used here are given above.

Figure 3.73. The countable fields and their embeddings are GFP.21 and GFP.37–GFP.49. The auxiliary complex realization is used for GFP.50; faithful support reflection and extension give GFP.51–GFP.52. The actual orthogonal triangle and all-field point adjunction give GFP.53–GFP.56.
